```ts
  test("the numbers the API and the composer share", () => {
    expect(MEDIA_MAX_BYTES).toBe(20_971_520);
    expect(MEDIA_MAX_PER_POST).toBe(4);
    expect(ALT_MAX_LENGTH).toBe(1000);
    expect([...MEDIA_ACCEPTED_TYPES]).toEqual(["image/jpeg", "image/png", "image/webp", "image/avif", "image/gif"]);
  });

  test("error codes and failure reasons", () => {
    // 3d Task 7: upload_refused, a post that attaches an upload korbat did not accept.
    // 2d Task 3 (9.4): avatar_not_ready, an upload set as the avatar that is processing, failed or refused; not_an_avatar, a
    // post's image sent as the avatar.
    expect(MediaErrorCode.options).toEqual(["unsupported_media_type", "file_too_large", "too_many_pending_uploads", "uploads_unavailable", "media_unavailable", "upload_refused", "avatar_not_ready", "not_an_avatar"]);
    expect(MediaFailure.options).toEqual(["unsupported_format", "animated_not_supported", "image_too_large", "corrupt_image", "processing_failed"]);
  });

  test("image paths end in .webp, which is what a CDN caches by default", () => {
    expect(mediaPath(id(7), "small")).toBe(`/api/media/${id(7)}/small.webp`);
    expect(mediaPath(id(7), "large")).toBe(`/api/media/${id(7)}/large.webp`);
  });
});

describe("alt text", () => {
  test("normalization: NFC, every run of whitespace to one space, trimmed", () => {
    expect(normalizeAltText("  a  red\tbarn\r\n\r\nat dusk ")).toBe("a red barn at dusk");
    expect(normalizeAltText("e\u0301")).toBe("\u00e9");
  });

  test("a description is required", () => {
    expect(AltText.safeParse("").success).toBe(false);
    expect(AltText.safeParse(" \n\t ").success).toBe(false);
    expect(AltText.parse(" a cat ")).toBe("a cat");
  });

  test("length is counted in code points after normalization", () => {
    const astral = "\u{1F600}";
    expect(altLength(astral.repeat(3))).toBe(3);
    expect(AltText.safeParse(astral.repeat(ALT_MAX_LENGTH)).success).toBe(true);
    expect(AltText.safeParse(astral.repeat(ALT_MAX_LENGTH + 1)).success).toBe(false);
    expect(AltText.safeParse(`${"a".repeat(ALT_MAX_LENGTH)}   `).success).toBe(true);
  });

  test("control characters are refused, including ones JavaScript does not count as whitespace", () => {
    expect(AltText.safeParse("a\u0000b").success).toBe(false);
    expect(AltText.safeParse("a\u0085b").success).toBe(false);
    expect(AltText.safeParse("a\u001bb").success).toBe(false);
  });

  test("media ids are canonical: any spelling of a UUID becomes its lowercase form", () => {
    expect(MediaAttachment.parse({ id: id(10).toUpperCase().replace("0000000A", "0000000a"), alt: "x" }).id).toBe(id(10));
    expect(MediaAttachment.parse({ id: "3F2A9C1E-8B7D-4E6F-A5C4-0123456789AB", alt: "x" }).id).toBe("3f2a9c1e-8b7d-4e6f-a5c4-0123456789ab");
  });

  test("an attachment is an upload id and a description", () => {
    expect(MediaAttachment.parse({ id: id(1), alt: "  a   cat " })).toEqual({ id: id(1), alt: "a cat" });
    expect(MediaAttachment.safeParse({ id: "nope", alt: "a cat" }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(MediaAttachment.safeParse({ id: id(1) }).success).toBe(false);
  });
});

describe("upload and status responses", () => {
  test("an upload starts as processing", () => {
    expect(UploadResponse.parse({ id: id(1), status: "processing" })).toEqual({ id: id(1), status: "processing" });
    expect(UploadResponse.safeParse({ id: id(1), status: "ready" }).success).toBe(false);
  });

  test("each status carries exactly what it needs", () => {
    expect(MediaStatusResponse.safeParse({ id: id(1), status: "processing" }).success).toBe(true);
    expect(MediaStatusResponse.safeParse({ id: id(1), status: "ready", width: 2048, height: 1536, blurhash: "L2Eo_P_3jb_3" }).success).toBe(true);
    expect(MediaStatusResponse.safeParse({ id: id(1), status: "ready" }).success).toBe(false);
    // A sealed image is ready and shown to nobody: its status carries the size and no blurhash, which is made from the image.
    expect(MediaStatusResponse.safeParse({ id: id(1), status: "ready", width: 2048, height: 1536 }).success).toBe(true);
    expect(MediaStatusResponse.safeParse({ id: id(1), status: "ready", width: 2048, height: 1536, blurhash: "short" }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(MediaStatusResponse.safeParse({ id: id(1), status: "ready", width: 0, height: 1536, blurhash: "L2Eo_P_3jb_3" }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(MediaStatusResponse.safeParse({ id: id(1), status: "failed", error: "animated_not_supported" }).success).toBe(true);
    expect(MediaStatusResponse.safeParse({ id: id(1), status: "failed", error: "because" }).success).toBe(false);
  });
});

describe("images on posts", () => {
  const image = { id: id(9), width: 2048, height: 1536, blurhash: "L2Eo_P_3jb_3", alt: "a cat", small: mediaPath(id(9), "small"), large: mediaPath(id(9), "large") };
  const post = {
    id: id(2),
    author: { id: id(1), handle: "ada", displayName: "Ada", verified: false, avatar: null },
    body: "",
    createdAt: "2026-09-18T10:00:00.000Z",
    state: "visible",
    replyTo: null,
    counts: { likes: 0, reposts: 0, replies: 0, quotes: 0 },
    quoteOf: null,
    imported: null,
    mentions: [],
    countsHidden: false,
  };

  test("a media view has dimensions, a placeholder, a description and both paths", () => {
    expect(MediaView.parse(image)).toEqual(image);
    expect(MediaView.safeParse({ ...image, blurhash: "" }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(MediaView.safeParse({ ...image, large: undefined }).success).toBe(false);
  });

  test("every post view has a media list, and a post may consist of images only", () => {
    expect(PostView.parse({ ...post, media: [image] }).media).toEqual([image]);
    expect(PostView.parse({ ...post, body: "text", media: [] }).media).toEqual([]);
    expect(PostView.safeParse(post).success).toBe(false);
  });

  test("a quoted post carries its images too", () => {
    const quoted = { ...post, id: id(3), media: [image] };
    const parsed = PostView.parse({ ...post, body: "look", media: [], quoteOf: quoted });
    expect(parsed.quoteOf).toMatchObject({ media: [image] });
  });

  test("the author's own image that moderation withheld or removed carries that state, and no other", () => {
    expect(MediaView.parse({ ...image, moderation: "withheld" })).toEqual({ ...image, moderation: "withheld" });
    expect(MediaView.parse({ ...image, moderation: "removed" })).toEqual({ ...image, moderation: "removed" });
    // A sealed image is never a media view: nobody is given its size, its blurhash, its description or its paths.
    for (const state of ["sealed", "visible", "hidden"]) expect(MediaView.safeParse({ ...image, moderation: state }).success, state).toBe(false);
    expect("moderation" in MediaView.parse(image)).toBe(false);
  });

  test("a hidden image is its id and the mark, with `sealed` only as true, and carries nothing of the image", () => {
    expect(HiddenMedia.parse({ id: id(9), hidden: true })).toEqual({ id: id(9), hidden: true });
    expect(HiddenMedia.parse({ id: id(9), hidden: true, sealed: true })).toEqual({ id: id(9), hidden: true, sealed: true });
    expect(HiddenMedia.safeParse({ id: id(9) }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(HiddenMedia.safeParse({ id: id(9), hidden: false }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(HiddenMedia.safeParse({ id: id(9), hidden: true, sealed: false }).success).toBe(false);
    // No size, no blurhash, no description and no path: a placeholder that carries one is not one.
    for (const member of ["width", "height", "blurhash", "alt", "small", "large"] as const) {
      expect(HiddenMedia.safeParse({ id: id(9), hidden: true, [member]: image[member] }).success, member).toBe(false);
    }
    expect(Object.keys(HiddenMedia.shape).sort()).toEqual(["hidden", "id", "sealed"]);
  });

  test("a post's media list holds images and hidden images side by side, in their order, on the post and on a quoted post", () => {
    const hidden = { id: id(10), hidden: true as const };
    const sealed = { id: id(11), hidden: true as const, sealed: true as const };
    const own = { ...image, id: id(12), moderation: "removed" as const };
    const media = [image, hidden, own, sealed];
    const parsed = PostView.parse({ ...post, media, quoteOf: { ...post, id: id(3), media: [hidden, image] } });
    expect(parsed.media).toEqual(media);
    expect(parsed.quoteOf).toMatchObject({ media: [hidden, image] });
    expect(parsed.media.map(isHiddenMedia)).toEqual([false, true, false, true]);
    // Something that is neither is refused.
    expect(PostView.safeParse({ ...post, media: [{ id: id(10) }] }).success).toBe(false);
  });
});

describe("2d Task 3: avatars (design, sections 7.1, 7.2 and 9.3)", () => {
  test("the two kinds of upload and the three crop positions along the longer side", () => {
    expect([...MEDIA_KINDS]).toEqual(["post", "avatar"]);
    expect([...AVATAR_CROPS]).toEqual(["start", "centre", "end"]);
  });

  test("UploadQuery: without kind an upload is a post's image; kind=avatar takes exactly one crop, and a crop never goes without it", () => {
    expect(UploadQuery.parse({})).toEqual({ kind: "post" });
    expect(UploadQuery.parse({ kind: "post" })).toEqual({ kind: "post" });
    for (const crop of AVATAR_CROPS) expect(UploadQuery.parse({ kind: "avatar", crop })).toEqual({ kind: "avatar", crop });
    // A crop on a post's image, and an avatar without a crop, are both invalid_request: the picker always sends one.
    expect(UploadQuery.safeParse({ crop: "centre" }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(UploadQuery.safeParse({ kind: "post", crop: "start" }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(UploadQuery.safeParse({ kind: "avatar" }).success).toBe(false);
    // Only the three positions and the two kinds; a repeated parameter arrives as a list, which is refused too.
    for (const bad of [{ kind: "avatar", crop: "center" }, { kind: "avatar", crop: "middle" }, { kind: "banner" }, { kind: "AVATAR", crop: "centre" }, { kind: ["avatar", "avatar"], crop: "centre" }, { kind: "avatar", crop: ["start", "end"] }]) {
      expect(UploadQuery.safeParse(bad).success, JSON.stringify(bad)).toBe(false);
    }
    // Any other parameter is dropped, never refused, as before: the route read no query until now.
    expect(UploadQuery.parse({ kind: "avatar", crop: "end", t: "1" })).toEqual({ kind: "avatar", crop: "end" });
  });

  test("an avatar is its two paths, as mediaPath makes them, and nothing else", () => {
    const view = { small: mediaPath(id(9), "small"), large: mediaPath(id(9), "large") };
    expect(AvatarView.parse(view)).toEqual(view);
    expect(AvatarView.safeParse({ small: view.small }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(AvatarView.parse({ ...view, width: 400 })).toEqual(view);
  });
});
```

```ts
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";

  AltText,

  ViewerPostState,
  normalizePostBody,
  postLength,
  visibleLength,
} from "../src/index";

const id = (n: number) => `00000000-0000-4000-8000-${String(n).padStart(12, "0")}`;
// 2d Task 3: every author carries its avatar, null while it has none.
const author = { id: id(1), handle: "ada", displayName: "Ada", verified: false, avatar: null };
const counts = { likes: 0, reposts: 0, replies: 0, quotes: 0 };
const post = (n: number, extra: Record<string, unknown> = {}) => ({
  id: id(n),
  author,
  body: "hello",
  createdAt: "2026-09-17T10:00:00.000Z",
  state: "visible",
  replyTo: null,
  counts,
  media: [],
  quoteOf: null,
  imported: null,
  mentions: [],
  countsHidden: false,
  ...extra,
});

describe("post bodies", () => {
  test("normalization: NFC, CR LF to LF, at most two line breaks, trimmed", () => {
    expect(normalizePostBody("  e\u0301\r\nb\n\n\n\nc  ")).toBe("\u00e9\nb\n\nc");
    expect(PostBody.parse("\n a\r\n\r\nb \n")).toBe("a\n\nb");
  });
  test("tab and line feed are allowed, other control characters are not", () => {
    expect(PostBody.safeParse("a\tb\nc").success).toBe(true);
    expect(PostBody.safeParse(`a${String.fromCharCode(7)}b`).success).toBe(false);
    expect(PostBody.safeParse("a\u0085b").success).toBe(false);
  });
  test("length is counted in code points after normalization", () => {
    expect(postLength("\u{1F600}".repeat(3))).toBe(3);
    expect(PostBody.safeParse("\u{1F600}".repeat(1000)).success).toBe(true);
    expect(PostBody.safeParse("\u{1F600}".repeat(1001)).success).toBe(false);
    expect(PostBody.safeParse("   \n  ").success).toBe(false);
  });
  test("a post is a reply or a quote, never both", () => {
    expect(CreatePostRequest.safeParse({ body: "x", replyToId: id(2) }).success).toBe(true);
    expect(CreatePostRequest.safeParse({ body: "x", quoteOfId: id(2) }).success).toBe(true);
    expect(CreatePostRequest.safeParse({ body: "x", replyToId: id(2), quoteOfId: id(3) }).success).toBe(false);
  });
});

describe("invisible characters", () => {
  const rlo = String.fromCharCode(0x202e);
  const zwsp = String.fromCharCode(0x200b);
  const zwj = String.fromCharCode(0x200d);
  test("direction overrides and zero-width spaces are refused in bodies, alt text and display names", () => {
    expect(PostBody.safeParse(`a${rlo}b`).success).toBe(false);
    expect(PostBody.safeParse(`a${zwsp}b`).success).toBe(false);
    expect(AltText.safeParse(`cat${rlo}`).success).toBe(false);
    expect(DisplayName.safeParse(`Ada${zwsp}`).success).toBe(false);
  });
  test("joiners inside emoji stay allowed but do not count as text on their own", () => {
    const family = `${String.fromCodePoint(0x1f468)}${zwj}${String.fromCodePoint(0x1f469)}`;
    expect(PostBody.safeParse(family).success).toBe(true);
    expect(PostBody.safeParse(zwj).success).toBe(false);
    expect(CreatePostRequest.safeParse({ body: zwj, media: [] }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(visibleLength(`a${zwj}b`)).toBe(2);
  });
  test("post ids are lowercased", () => {
    expect(PostId.parse("3B241101-E2BB-4255-8CAF-4136C566A962")).toBe("3b241101-e2bb-4255-8caf-4136c566a962");
  });
  test("a reply may point at a parent whose author is hidden from the viewer", () => {
    expect(PostView.safeParse(post(1, { replyTo: { id: id(2), authorHandle: null } })).success).toBe(true);
    expect(PostView.safeParse(post(1, { replyTo: { id: id(2) } })).success).toBe(false);
  });
});

describe("handles", () => {
  test("handle params strip the @ and lowercase, and reject invalid handles", () => {
    expect(HandleParam.parse(" @Ada_Lovelace ")).toBe("ada_lovelace");

    expect(HandleParam.safeParse("has space").success).toBe(false);
  });
});

describe("post views", () => {
  test("a quote embeds one level and is otherwise a tombstone", () => {
    expect(PostView.safeParse(post(1, { quoteOf: post(2) })).success).toBe(true);
    expect(PostView.safeParse(post(1, { quoteOf: { id: id(2), deleted: true } })).success).toBe(true);
    expect(PostView.safeParse(post(1, { quoteOf: { id: id(2), unavailable: true } })).success).toBe(true);
    // The embedded post may not carry its own expanded quote, and a tombstone needs a reason.
    expect(PostView.safeParse(post(1, { quoteOf: post(2, { quoteOf: post(3) }) })).success).toBe(false);
    expect(PostView.safeParse(post(1, { quoteOf: { id: id(2) } })).success).toBe(false);
  });
  test("deleted is not a post state; deleted posts are tombstones", () => {
    expect(PostView.safeParse(post(1, { state: "deleted_by_author" })).success).toBe(false);
    expect(ThreadResponse.safeParse({ ancestors: [{ id: id(9), deleted: true }, post(2)], post: post(1), replies: { items: [], nextCursor: null } }).success).toBe(true);
  });

});

    expect(ProfileView.safeParse(view).success).toBe(false);
    // A post's author and a quoted post's author carry it too.
    expect(PostView.parse(post(2, { author: { ...author, avatar } })).author.avatar).toEqual(avatar);
  });

    expect(AvatarRequest.parse({ mediaId: id(9).toUpperCase() })).toEqual({ mediaId: id(9) });

    const avatar = { small: `/api/media/${id(9)}/small.webp`, large: `/api/media/${id(9)}/large.webp` };

    expect(AvatarResponse.parse({ avatar: null })).toEqual({ avatar: null });
    expect(AvatarResponse.safeParse({}).success).toBe(false);
  });

  test("the error codes are exactly the seven social ones, 3e's account_suspended last", () => {
    expect(SocialErrorCode.options).toEqual(["post_unavailable", "not_author", "blocked", "self_target", "account_too_new", "explore_refreshed", "account_suspended"]);
  });
});

describe("profile editing", () => {
  const rlo = String.fromCharCode(0x202e);
  const zwsp = String.fromCharCode(0x200b);
  const zwj = String.fromCharCode(0x200d);

  test("a bio is trimmed, may be empty, and has at most 160 code points", () => {
    expect(BIO_MAX_LENGTH).toBe(160);
    expect(Bio.parse("  Unpopular opinions, daily.  ")).toBe("Unpopular opinions, daily.");
    expect(Bio.parse("")).toBe("");
    expect(Bio.parse("   ")).toBe("");
    expect(Bio.safeParse("a".repeat(BIO_MAX_LENGTH)).success).toBe(true);
    expect(Bio.safeParse("a".repeat(BIO_MAX_LENGTH + 1)).success).toBe(false);
    const astral = String.fromCodePoint(0x1f600);
    expect(Bio.safeParse(astral.repeat(BIO_MAX_LENGTH)).success).toBe(true);
    expect(Bio.safeParse(astral.repeat(BIO_MAX_LENGTH + 1)).success).toBe(false);
  });

  test("a bio is one line of plain text: no control, direction or zero-width characters; emoji joiners stay", () => {
    expect(Bio.safeParse(`a${String.fromCharCode(7)}b`).success).toBe(false);
    expect(Bio.safeParse(`a${String.fromCharCode(10)}b`).success).toBe(false);
    expect(Bio.safeParse(`a${String.fromCharCode(9)}b`).success).toBe(false);
    expect(Bio.safeParse(`a${String.fromCharCode(0x85)}b`).success).toBe(false);
    // The Unicode line and paragraph separators are line breaks too, though not control characters.
    expect(Bio.safeParse(`a${String.fromCharCode(0x2028)}b`).success).toBe(false);
    expect(Bio.safeParse(`a${String.fromCharCode(0x2029)}b`).success).toBe(false);
    expect(Bio.safeParse(`a${rlo}b`).success).toBe(false);
    expect(Bio.safeParse(`a${zwsp}b`).success).toBe(false);
    expect(Bio.safeParse(`${String.fromCodePoint(0x1f468)}${zwj}${String.fromCodePoint(0x1f469)}`).success).toBe(true);
  });

  test("a profile edit changes the display name, the bio or both, never nothing", () => {
    expect(ProfileEditRequest.parse({ displayName: " Ada " })).toEqual({ displayName: "Ada" });
    expect(ProfileEditRequest.parse({ bio: "" })).toEqual({ bio: "" });
    expect(ProfileEditRequest.parse({ displayName: "Ada", bio: " hi " })).toEqual({ displayName: "Ada", bio: "hi" });
    expect(ProfileEditRequest.safeParse({}).success).toBe(false);
    expect(ProfileEditRequest.safeParse({ displayName: "" }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(ProfileEditRequest.safeParse({ displayName: "x".repeat(51) }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(ProfileEditRequest.safeParse({ bio: `a${rlo}b` }).success).toBe(false);
  });

  test("a handle change carries the handle as typed, lowercased; the flow decides whether it is valid", () => {
    expect(HandleChangeRequest.parse({ handle: " Ada_Lovelace " })).toEqual({ handle: "ada_lovelace" });
    expect(HandleChangeRequest.safeParse({}).success).toBe(false);
    expect(HandleChangeRequest.safeParse({ handle: "" }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(HandleChangeRequest.safeParse({ handle: "x".repeat(65) }).success).toBe(false);
  });
});

describe("posts with images", () => {
  const img = (n: number, alt = "an image") => ({ id: id(n), alt });

  test("a post needs text or an image; the body defaults to empty and media to none", () => {
    // 2d (decision 26): and hideCounts to off.
    expect(CreatePostRequest.parse({ body: "hello" })).toEqual({ body: "hello", media: [], hideCounts: false });
    expect(CreatePostRequest.parse({ media: [img(1)] })).toEqual({ body: "", media: [img(1)], hideCounts: false });
    expect(CreatePostRequest.parse({ body: "  ", media: [img(1)] }).body).toBe("");
    expect(CreatePostRequest.safeParse({}).success).toBe(false);
    expect(CreatePostRequest.safeParse({ body: "   ", media: [] }).success).toBe(false);
  });

  test("at most four images, each only once, each with a description", () => {
    expect(CreatePostRequest.safeParse({ body: "x", media: [img(1), img(2), img(3), img(4)] }).success).toBe(true);
    expect(CreatePostRequest.safeParse({ body: "x", media: [img(1), img(2), img(3), img(4), img(5)] }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(CreatePostRequest.safeParse({ body: "x", media: [img(1), img(1)] }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(CreatePostRequest.safeParse({ body: "x", media: [img(1, "  ")] }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(CreatePostRequest.safeParse({ body: "x", media: [{ id: id(1) }] }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(CreatePostRequest.parse({ body: "x", media: [img(1, "  a   cat ")] }).media[0]!.alt).toBe("a cat");
  });

  test("the text rules still hold for a post with images, and replies and quotes may carry images", () => {
    expect(CreatePostRequest.safeParse({ body: "a".repeat(1001), media: [img(1)] }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(CreatePostRequest.safeParse({ body: "a\u0000b", media: [img(1)] }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(CreatePostRequest.safeParse({ replyToId: id(7), media: [img(1)] }).success).toBe(true);
    expect(CreatePostRequest.safeParse({ quoteOfId: id(7), media: [img(1)] }).success).toBe(true);
    expect(CreatePostRequest.safeParse({ replyToId: id(7), quoteOfId: id(8), media: [img(1)] }).success).toBe(false);
  });
});
```

```ts
describe("the retirement of a handle (3e design, sections 10.1, 10.2, 10.3 and W.1)", () => {

describe("announced measures, replies and termination (3e design, sections 10.1 to 10.3, Task 4)", () => {
  const T = "2026-10-12T10:00:00.000Z";
  const ID = "3f1c2b1e-8d4a-4c1e-9b2a-6f0e5d4c3b2a";

    expect(QueuePage.safeParse({ cases: [], nextCursor: null }).success).toBe(false);
    const standing = {
      state: "held",
      earliestStart: T,
      startsAt: null,
```

```ts
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";
import { actionKind } from "../src/schema/moderation";

/**
 * The rule for the new values of action_kind (3e design, section 6, "The rule for the new enum values"; invariant 1).
 * drizzle's migrator runs every pending migration in one transaction, and a value that ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE added
 * cannot be used as an enum literal before that transaction commits (SQLSTATE 55P04) in anything that is parsed when it
 * is created or run: a view, an SQL-language function, a check, a default, an index predicate, a plain statement. Only a
 * PL/pgSQL body is parsed when it is first called, which no migration statement does. So in 3e's migrations a new value
 * appears as a literal only inside a PL/pgSQL function's body, and everywhere else a kind is compared as text
 * (`kind::text = 'strike'`). This test reads 3e's migration files and refuses any other use.
 *
 * The SQL is read statement by statement, its comments dropped, and every run of white space made one space, so the
 * patterns below need no escapes.
 */

const MIGRATIONS = path.resolve(import.meta.dirname, "../migrations");

/** 3c's twelve kinds come first in the enum; 3e's ten follow them, and 3f's two follow those (read below). */
const OLD_KINDS = 12;
const KINDS_3E = 10;
const NEW_KINDS: readonly string[] = actionKind.enumValues.slice(OLD_KINDS, OLD_KINDS + KINDS_3E);

/** 3e's first migration: 3c ended at 0019_redaction_scope, so 3e's migrations are 0020 and after. */
const FIRST_3E_MIGRATION = 20;

const NEWLINE = String.fromCharCode(10);
const BREAKPOINT = "--> statement-breakpoint";

/** The journal's entries of 3e's migrations, oldest first. */
function migrationsOf3e(): { idx: number; tag: string }[] {
  const journal = JSON.parse(readFileSync(path.join(MIGRATIONS, "meta", "_journal.json"), "utf8")) as { entries: { idx: number; tag: string }[] };
  return journal.entries.filter((entry) => entry.idx >= FIRST_3E_MIGRATION);
}

/** A statement with its line comments dropped: a comment may name a kind in any words it likes. */
function withoutComments(statement: string): string {
  return statement
    .split(NEWLINE)
    .map((line) => {
      const at = line.indexOf("--");
      return at < 0 ? line : line.slice(0, at);
    })
    .join(NEWLINE);
}

/** Every run of white space (a code point up to the space) as one space, trimmed. */
function flat(text: string): string {
  return [...text]
    .map((char) => (char.charCodeAt(0) <= 32 ? " " : char))
    .join("")
    .split(" ")
    .filter((word) => word !== "")
    .join(" ");
}

/**
 * A statement with the body of a PL/pgSQL function blanked, so that only what is parsed at once is left: a statement that
 * creates a function in LANGUAGE plpgsql keeps its signature and loses what lies between its outer dollar quotes. A DO
 * block keeps its body: it runs inside the migration, and its literals are parsed then.
 */
function withoutPlpgsqlBody(statement: string): string {
  const upper = statement.toUpperCase();
  const creates = upper.startsWith("CREATE FUNCTION") || upper.startsWith("CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION");
  if (!creates || !upper.includes("LANGUAGE PLPGSQL")) return statement;
  const open = statement.indexOf("$$");
  const close = statement.lastIndexOf("$$");
  if (open < 0 || close <= open) return statement;
  return `${statement.slice(0, open + 2)} ${statement.slice(close)}`;
}

/**
 * The places where a literal is compared as text: `::text` followed by `=`, `<>`, `IN (` or `= ANY (ARRAY[` and then a
 * list of quoted words. A new kind's literal there is a text, and parses whatever the enum holds.
 */
const TEXT_COMPARISON = /::text ?(?:=|<>|!=|in ?[(]|= ?any ?[(] ?array ?[[]) ?'[a-z_]+'(?: ?, ?'[a-z_]+')*/gi;

/** The statement that adds a value names it, as a label and not as a literal of the enum. */
const ADDED_VALUE = /alter type [^ ]+ add value '[a-z_]+'/gi;

/** Every use of a new kind's literal in the SQL that is outside a PL/pgSQL body and not compared as text, each with its context. */
function enumLiteralViolations(sqlText: string, kinds: readonly string[] = NEW_KINDS): string[] {
  const violations: string[] = [];
  const literal = new RegExp(`'(${kinds.join("|")})'`, "g");
  for (const statement of sqlText.split(BREAKPOINT)) {
    const scanned = withoutPlpgsqlBody(flat(withoutComments(statement)));
    const allowed: [number, number][] = [];
    for (const pattern of [TEXT_COMPARISON, ADDED_VALUE]) {
      for (const match of scanned.matchAll(pattern)) allowed.push([match.index, match.index + match[0].length]);
    }
    for (const match of scanned.matchAll(literal)) {
      const at = match.index;
      const castToText = /^ ?::text(?![a-z_])/i.test(scanned.slice(at + match[0].length));
      if (castToText || allowed.some(([from, to]) => at >= from && at < to)) continue;
      violations.push(scanned.slice(Math.max(0, at - 60), at + match[0].length + 20));
    }
  }
  return violations;
}

describe("the enum-literal rule of 3e's migrations", () => {
  test("action_kind's new values are the ten of 3e, after 3c's twelve", () => {
    expect(NEW_KINDS).toEqual(["strike", "suspend", "terminate", "retire_handle", "warn_reporting", "restrict_reporting", "overrule", "lift_suspension", "unretire_handle", "lift_reporting"]);
  });

  test("3e's migrations are there: the schema (0020) and standing_ledger (0021) at least", () => {
    const tags = migrationsOf3e().map((entry) => entry.tag);
    expect(tags.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(2);
    expect(tags[1]).toBe("0021_standing_ledger");
  });

  test("no file of 3e names a new kind as a literal outside a PL/pgSQL body", () => {
    for (const entry of migrationsOf3e()) {
      const text = readFileSync(path.join(MIGRATIONS, `${entry.tag}.sql`), "utf8");
      expect(enumLiteralViolations(text), entry.tag).toEqual([]);
    }
  });

  test("the files of 3e do name the new kinds, inside PL/pgSQL bodies, so the test reads what it should", () => {
    const ledger = readFileSync(path.join(MIGRATIONS, `${migrationsOf3e()[1]!.tag}.sql`), "utf8");
    // The same file read without blanking the bodies would hold many: the bodies are where the kinds are used.
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(ledger.split("LANGUAGE plpgsql").join("LANGUAGE sql")).length).toBeGreaterThan(20);
  });

  test("a deliberate violation of each kind is caught, and the allowed forms are not", () => {
    // Caught: a view, an SQL function, a check and an index predicate that name a new kind as the enum, and a cast.
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT 1 FROM decision_actions a WHERE a.kind = 'strike';`)).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`CREATE FUNCTION f() RETURNS boolean LANGUAGE sql AS $$ SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM decision_actions a WHERE a.kind IN ('suspend', 'terminate')) $$;`)).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`ALTER TABLE decision_actions ADD CONSTRAINT c CHECK (kind <> 'overrule');`)).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`CREATE INDEX i ON decision_actions (created_at) WHERE kind = 'strike';`)).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`SELECT 'lift_reporting'::public.action_kind;`)).toHaveLength(1);
    // A DO block runs inside the migration: its body is no exemption.
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`DO $$ BEGIN PERFORM 1 FROM decision_actions a WHERE a.kind = 'strike'; END $$;`)).toHaveLength(1);
    // Two statements: the second's violation is found although the first is a PL/pgSQL function.
    const two = `CREATE FUNCTION f() RETURNS void LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN PERFORM 1; END $$;${BREAKPOINT}${NEWLINE}CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT 1 FROM decision_actions a WHERE a.kind = 'suspend';`;
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(two)).toHaveLength(1);
    // Allowed: a comparison as text, a cast to text, any literal inside a PL/pgSQL body, an old kind, a comment, and the
    // statement that adds the value.
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT 1 FROM decision_actions a WHERE a.kind::text = 'strike' AND a.kind::text IN ('suspend', 'terminate');`)).toEqual([]);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT 'strike'::text AS k;`)).toEqual([]);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`CREATE FUNCTION f() RETURNS void LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN PERFORM 1 FROM decision_actions a WHERE a.kind = 'strike'; END $$;`)).toEqual([]);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT 1 FROM decision_actions a WHERE a.kind = 'remove';`)).toEqual([]);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`-- a.kind = 'strike' in a comment${NEWLINE}SELECT 1;`)).toEqual([]);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`ALTER TYPE "public"."action_kind" ADD VALUE 'strike';`)).toEqual([]);
  });
});

/**
 * 3f (design, section 6, "The rule for the new enum values"; invariant 1): the migration orders adds eight values to seven
 * enums: action_kind's disable_by_order and reinstate_by_order, `order` to decision_kind, decision_source and intake_kind,
 * `authority` to intake_channel and `disabled` to moderation_level and post_state. drizzle runs 3f's migrations in one

const VALUES_3F: readonly string[] = ["disable_by_order", "reinstate_by_order", "order", "authority", "disabled"];

/** The journal's entries from the migration that adds 3f's values, oldest first. */
function migrationsFromOrders(): { idx: number; tag: string }[] {

  test("3d review: 0041_review is read under the stricter form: neither label as a literal, in its bodies either; kinds are compared as text", () => {

    expect(flat(withoutComments(text))).toContain("i.kind::text = 'automated'");

  });
});

/**
 * 3b (design, sections 6 and 6.7; Task 2): import from other platforms adds two enums of its own and no value to any enum
 * that exists, so the rule above has nothing new to hold in its migrations; the 3e, 3f and 3d describes above read them
 * all the same, from their first files on. This case holds that: from 0043_imports on, no file adds a value with ALTER
 * TYPE, and import_source and import_status are created whole, each in one CREATE TYPE with every value of the design.
 */
describe("3b's migrations: two enums created whole, no value added to an existing one", () => {
  test("from 0043_imports on, no ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE, and import_source and import_status are created with their values", () => {
    const journal = JSON.parse(readFileSync(path.join(MIGRATIONS, "meta", "_journal.json"), "utf8")) as { entries: { idx: number; tag: string }[] };
    const first = journal.entries.find((entry) => entry.tag === "0043_imports");
    expect(first?.idx).toBe(43);
    // 2d Task 1: 3b's six files, 0043_imports to 0048_import_staff_end. 2d's migrations create enums of their own and add
    // values to action_kind, each read by a describe of its own below.
    const last = journal.entries.find((entry) => entry.tag === "0048_import_staff_end");
    expect(last?.idx).toBe(48);
    const files = journal.entries.filter((entry) => entry.idx >= first!.idx && entry.idx <= last!.idx);
    expect(files.slice(0, 3).map((entry) => entry.tag)).toEqual(["0043_imports", "0044_imported_posts", "0045_import_readers"]);
    const created: Record<string, string[]> = {};
    for (const entry of files) {
      const text = flat(withoutComments(readFileSync(path.join(MIGRATIONS, `${entry.tag}.sql`), "utf8")));
      expect(text, entry.tag).not.toMatch(/ALTER TYPE [^ ]+ ADD VALUE/i);
      for (const match of text.matchAll(/CREATE TYPE "public"."([a-z_]+)" AS ENUM ?[(]([^)]*)[)]/g)) {
        created[match[1]!] = [...match[2]!.matchAll(/'([a-z_]+)'/g)].map((value) => value[1]!);
      }
    }
    expect(created).toEqual({
      import_source: ["x", "mastodon", "bluesky"],
      import_status: ["uploading", "scanning", "ready", "preparing", "publishing", "done", "stopped", "undoing", "undone", "failed", "cancelled", "expired"],
    });
  });
});

/**
 * 2d (design, sections 6 and 6.8; Task 1): the migrations activity and post_options create two enums of their own and add
 * no value to any enum that exists, so 3e's rule has nothing new to hold in them; the 3e, 3f and 3d describes above read
 * them all the same, from their first files on. This case reads those two files alone, by tag: 2d's later migrations
 * create media_kind (Task 3) and add values to action_kind (Task 4's avatar_kinds), each under a describe of its own.
 */
/**
 * 2d Task 3 (design, sections 6.4 and 6.8): the migration avatars creates media_kind whole, in one CREATE TYPE with both of
 * the contracts' MEDIA_KINDS, and adds no value to an enum that exists; its hand-written functions compare the kind, the
 * status and the moderation state as text, as 2d compares every enum.
 */
describe("2d's migration avatars: media_kind created whole, no value added to an existing one", () => {
  test("0051_avatars adds no value with ALTER TYPE, creates media_kind with post and avatar, and compares enums as text in its bodies", () => {
    const journal = JSON.parse(readFileSync(path.join(MIGRATIONS, "meta", "_journal.json"), "utf8")) as { entries: { idx: number; tag: string }[] };
    const entry = journal.entries.find((candidate) => candidate.tag === "0051_avatars");
    expect(entry?.idx).toBe(51);
    const raw = readFileSync(path.join(MIGRATIONS, "0051_avatars.sql"), "utf8");
    const text = flat(withoutComments(raw));
    expect(text).not.toMatch(/ALTER TYPE [^ ]+ ADD VALUE/i);
    const created: Record<string, string[]> = {};
    for (const match of text.matchAll(/CREATE TYPE "public"."([a-z_]+)" AS ENUM ?[(]([^)]*)[)]/g)) {
      created[match[1]!] = [...match[2]!.matchAll(/'([a-z_]+)'/g)].map((value) => value[1]!);
    }
    expect(created).toEqual({ media_kind: ["post", "avatar"] });
    for (const literal of ["kind::text <> 'avatar'", "status::text <> 'ready'", "moderation_state::text <> 'visible'"]) expect(text, literal).toContain(literal);

  });
});

describe("2d's migrations activity and post_options: two enums created whole, no value added to an existing one", () => {
  test("0049_activity and 0050_post_options add no value with ALTER TYPE, and create activity_kind and activity_reach with their values", () => {

      }
```

```ts
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";

const byName = new Map(tables.map((t) => [getTableConfig(t).name, getTableConfig(t)]));

  test("auth tables live in the auth schema", () => {
    for (const name of ["users", "devices", "sessions", "email_codes", "passkeys", "auth_events"]) {

  });
});

describe("row level security", () => {
  test("every table has RLS enabled and at least one policy", () => {
    expect(tables.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    for (const t of tables) {
      const cfg = getTableConfig(t);
      expect(cfg.enableRLS, cfg.name).toBe(true);
      expect(cfg.policies.length, cfg.name).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    }
  });
});

  });
});

    expect(purges.indexes.map((i) => [i.config.name, i.config.columns.map((c) => (c as { name: string }).name)]).sort()).toEqual([
      ["edge_purges_due_idx", ["next_at"]],
      ["edge_purges_media_idx", ["media_id", "id"]],
    ]);
    expect(purges.enableRLS).toBe(true);
    expect(purges.policies.map((p) => [p.name, p.for, p.to])).toEqual([["edge_purges_api_all", "all", apiRole]]);
  });
  test("3d's release (section 6.2): the leave, the release with its notice's state, its mark keyed on the post, and the day's notice; the API's role is granted nothing on the leave", () => {
    const leaves = byName.get("release_leaves")!;
    expect(leaves.columns.map((c) => c.name).sort()).toEqual(
      ["id", "notification_id", "leave_from", "reference", "received_on", "untold", "untold_until", "recorded_at", "recorded_by", "withdrawn_at", "withdrawn_by"].sort(),
    );
    expect(leaves.checks.map((c) => c.name).sort()).toEqual(["release_leaves_from", "release_leaves_reference", "release_leaves_texts", "release_leaves_untold", "release_leaves_withdrawn"]);
    expect(leaves.foreignKeys).toEqual([]);
    expect(leaves.policies.map((p) => [p.name, p.for, p.to])).toEqual([["release_leaves_api_none", "select", apiRole]]);
    const releases = byName.get("releases")!;
    expect(releases.columns.map((c) => c.name).sort()).toEqual(
      [
        "id",
        "seal_action_id",
        "upload_refusal_id",
        "post_ids",
        "basis",
        "leave_id",
        "their_reference",
        "released_by",
        "released_at",
        "replay_of",
        "backups_clear_at",
        "author_notice",
        "author_notice_at",
        "imported_at",
      ].sort(),
    );
    expect(releases.checks.map((c) => c.name).sort()).toEqual(["releases_basis", "releases_leave", "releases_notice", "releases_reference", "releases_replay"]);
    // The admin who released is a profile; no foreign key names a seal, a leave or a refusal: a replay may come first.
    expect(releases.foreignKeys.map((fk) => fk.reference().foreignTable[Symbol.for("drizzle:Name") as never])).toEqual(["profiles"]);
    const marks = byName.get("release_posts")!;
    expect(marks.primaryKeys.length + marks.columns.filter((c) => c.primary).length).toBe(1);
    expect(marks.columns.find((c) => c.primary)?.name).toBe("post_id");
    expect(marks.foreignKeys.map((fk) => fk.reference().foreignTable[Symbol.for("drizzle:Name") as never])).toEqual(["releases"]);
    const notices = byName.get("release_notices")!;
    expect(notices.columns.find((c) => c.primary)?.name).toBe("subject_id");
    for (const table of [leaves, releases, marks, notices]) expect(table.enableRLS, table.name).toBe(true);
  });
  test("3d's quarantine_files: a file's row keyed by its image and its name, with its three ends and no right for the API (section 6.1)", () => {
    const files = byName.get("quarantine_files")!;
    expect(files.schema ?? "public").toBe("public");
    expect(files.columns.map((c) => c.name).sort()).toEqual(
      ["media_id", "file", "post_id", "size", "sha256", "moved_at", "returned_at", "destroyed_at", "release_id", "lost_at", "lost_told", "imported_at", "unknown"].sort(),
    );
    expect(files.primaryKeys.map((k) => [k.getName(), k.columns.map((c) => c.name)])).toEqual([["quarantine_files_pkey", ["media_id", "file"]]]);
    expect(files.checks.map((c) => c.name).sort()).toEqual(["quarantine_files_digest", "quarantine_files_ends", "quarantine_files_file", "quarantine_files_release", "quarantine_files_told"]);
    // Task 2: a destroyed file names the release it was destroyed for.
    expect(files.foreignKeys.map((fk) => fk.reference().foreignTable[Symbol.for("drizzle:Name") as never])).toEqual(["releases"]);
    expect(files.indexes.map((i) => i.config.name).sort()).toEqual(["quarantine_files_post_idx", "quarantine_files_untold_idx"]);
    expect(files.enableRLS).toBe(true);
    expect(files.policies.map((p) => [p.name, p.for, p.to])).toEqual([["quarantine_files_api_none", "select", apiRole]]);
  });
  test("3f's recovery tables: a gap's class and disposition, its closing and the copy marks (section 6.6)", () => {
    const gaps = byName.get("restore_gaps")!;
    expect(gaps.schema ?? "public").toBe("public");
    expect(gaps.columns.map((c) => c.name).sort()).toEqual(
      ["id", "import_id", "place", "hash", "action", "target_type", "target_id", "metadata", "acted_at", "imported_at", "class", "closed_at", "closed_by", "disposition"].sort(),
    );
    expect(gaps.checks.map((c) => c.name).sort()).toEqual(["restore_gaps_class", "restore_gaps_closed", "restore_gaps_disposition", "restore_gaps_hash", "restore_gaps_place"]);
    expect(gaps.uniqueConstraints.map((u) => u.name)).toEqual(["restore_gaps_place_key"]);
    expect(gaps.indexes.map((i) => i.config.name)).toEqual(["restore_gaps_open_idx"]);
    expect(gaps.enableRLS).toBe(true);
    const marks = byName.get("copy_marks")!;
    expect(marks.columns.map((c) => c.name).sort()).toEqual(["at", "id", "place", "staff_id"]);
    expect(marks.checks.map((c) => c.name)).toEqual(["copy_marks_place"]);
    expect(marks.enableRLS).toBe(true);
  });
  test("the tables 3c retired are gone, with their enums and the reputation column", () => {
    for (const name of ["reports", "strikes", "transparency_log"]) expect(byName.has(name), name).toBe(false);
    for (const name of ["targetType", "reportStatus", "caseAction", "appealStatus", "reports", "strikes", "transparencyLog"]) {
      expect(Object.keys(schema), name).not.toContain(name);
    }
    expect(byName.get("profiles")!.columns.map((c) => c.name)).not.toContain("reputation");
  });
  test("audit_log policies allow only insert and select", () => {
    const kinds = byName.get("audit_log")!.policies.map((p) => p.for).sort();
    expect(kinds).toEqual(["insert", "select"]);
  });
});

    expect(cfg.columns.find((c) => c.name === "changed_at")?.notNull).toBe(true);
    expect(cfg.columns.find((c) => c.name === "changed_at")?.hasDefault).toBe(true);

    expect(fk).toEqual([{ table: "profiles", columns: ["id"], onDelete: "cascade" }]);

  test("one phone per account: a unique index on phone_hash that leaves out the accounts without one", () => {

    expect(idx?.config.unique).toBe(true);

    expect(idx?.config.where).toBeDefined();

    const values = schema.authEventType.enumValues;
    expect(values.slice(values.indexOf("not_me"), values.indexOf("account_deleted") + 1)).toEqual([
      "not_me",
      "profile_updated",
      "handle_changed",
      "email_changed",
      "badge_verified",
      "badge_removed",
      "export_created",
      "account_deleted",
```
