```ts
  carriesR1Marker,
  VARIANTS,
  isMediaId,
  parseFormats,
  resultFileId,
  storeLayout,
  uploadsLayout,
} from "../src/index";

const ID = "3f2a9c1e-8b7d-4e6f-a5c4-0123456789ab";

describe("limits", () => {
  test("pixel caps follow what decoding costs: AVIF has its own", () => {
    expect(PIXEL_CAP).toEqual({ jpeg: 50_000_000, png: 50_000_000, webp: 50_000_000, gif: 50_000_000, avif: 16_000_000 });
    expect(MAX_SIDE).toBe(16_383);
    expect(VARIANTS).toEqual({ large: { edge: 2048, quality: 82 }, small: { edge: 1024, quality: 80 } });
    // 2d Task 3 (design, sections 7.1 and 7.4): an avatar's two squares, under the same two names.
    expect(AVATAR_VARIANTS).toEqual({ large: { edge: 400, quality: 82 }, small: { edge: 128, quality: 80 } });
    expect(MAX_ATTEMPTS).toBe(3);
    expect(HEARTBEAT_STALE_MS).toBeGreaterThan(HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS * 3);
  });

  test("MEDIA_FORMATS: unset means all, a subset keeps the canonical order", () => {
    expect(parseFormats(undefined)).toEqual([...MEDIA_FORMATS]);
    expect(parseFormats("webp, JPEG")).toEqual(["jpeg", "webp"]);
    expect(parseFormats("jpeg,png,webp,gif")).toEqual(["jpeg", "png", "webp", "gif"]);
    expect(parseFormats("png,png")).toEqual(["png"]);
  });

  test("MEDIA_FORMATS: a typo or an empty entry stops the process instead of silently changing what is accepted", () => {
    expect(() => parseFormats("jpeg,tiff")).toThrow(/unknown formats: tiff/);
    expect(() => parseFormats("")).toThrow(/at least one format/);
    expect(() => parseFormats("jpeg,,png")).toThrow(/no empty entries/);
  });
});

describe("layout", () => {
  test("only lowercase UUIDs are media ids", () => {
    expect(isMediaId(ID)).toBe(true);
    for (const bad of ["", ID.toUpperCase(), `${ID}.json`, `../${ID}`, `${ID}/..`, "..", "heartbeat", `${ID} `, ID.replace("-", "_")]) expect(isMediaId(bad)).toBe(false);
  });

  test("the uploads volume", () => {
    const up = uploadsLayout(path.join("x", "uploads"));
    expect(up.part(ID)).toBe(path.join("x", "uploads", "tmp", `${ID}.part`));
    expect(up.upload(ID)).toBe(path.join("x", "uploads", "incoming", ID));
    expect(up.deletion(ID)).toBe(path.join("x", "uploads", "delete", ID));
    expect([up.tmp, up.incoming, up.deletions]).toEqual(["tmp", "incoming", "delete"].map((name) => path.join("x", "uploads", name)));
    // A deletion that is owed is no request: its marker lies beside the requests, in a directory the worker never reads.
    expect(up.owed).toBe(path.join("x", "uploads", "delete-owed"));
    expect(up.owedDeletion(ID)).toBe(path.join("x", "uploads", "delete-owed", ID));
    // 2d Task 3 (design, section 7.2): an avatar's job file lies beside its upload, under a name that is no media id, so the
    // worker's scan of incoming/ never takes it for an upload of its own.
    expect(up.avatarJob(ID)).toBe(path.join("x", "uploads", "incoming", `${ID}.avatar`));
    expect(isMediaId(path.basename(up.avatarJob(ID)))).toBe(false);
  });

  test("the store volume shards image folders by the id's first two characters", () => {
    const store = storeLayout(path.join("x", "store"));
    expect(store.shard(ID)).toBe(path.join("x", "store", "files", "3f"));
    expect(store.imageDir(ID)).toBe(path.join("x", "store", "files", "3f", ID));
    expect(store.image(ID, "large")).toBe(path.join("x", "store", "files", "3f", ID, "large.webp"));
    expect(store.image(ID, "small")).toBe(path.join("x", "store", "files", "3f", ID, "small.webp"));
    expect(store.result(ID)).toBe(path.join("x", "store", "results", `${ID}.json`));
    expect(store.attempt(ID)).toBe(path.join("x", "store", "attempts", ID));
    expect(store.heartbeat).toBe(path.join("x", "store", "heartbeat"));
  });

  test("nothing but a media id can become part of a path", () => {
    const up = uploadsLayout("u");
    const store = storeLayout("s");
    for (const bad of ["../../etc/passwd", "..", "", ID.toUpperCase(), `${ID}/x`]) {
      for (const make of [up.part, up.upload, up.deletion, up.owedDeletion, up.avatarJob, store.shard, store.imageDir, store.result, store.attempt]) expect(() => make(bad)).toThrow("not a media id");
      expect(() => store.image(bad, "large")).toThrow("not a media id");
    }
  });

  test("result file names map back to ids", () => {
    expect(resultFileId(`${ID}.json`)).toBe(ID);
    for (const bad of [ID, `${ID}.json.tmp`, "x.json", `${ID.toUpperCase()}.json`, ".json"]) expect(resultFileId(bad)).toBeNull();
  });
});

describe("result and heartbeat files", () => {
  const ready = { v: 1, id: ID, status: "ready", width: 2048, height: 1536, blurhash: "L2Eo_P_3jb_3~qoLfQj]" };

  test("a ready result has the large size's dimensions and a blurhash", () => {
    expect(ResultFile.parse(ready)).toEqual(ready);
    expect(ResultFile.safeParse({ ...ready, width: MAX_SIDE + 1 }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(ResultFile.safeParse({ ...ready, width: 0 }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(ResultFile.safeParse({ ...ready, blurhash: "x" }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(ResultFile.safeParse({ ...ready, blurhash: "x".repeat(65) }).success).toBe(false);
  });

  test("a failed result names one of the known reasons", () => {
    expect(ResultFile.safeParse({ v: 1, id: ID, status: "failed", reason: "animated_not_supported" }).success).toBe(true);
    expect(ResultFile.safeParse({ v: 1, id: ID, status: "failed", reason: "because" }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(ResultFile.safeParse({ v: 1, id: ID, status: "failed" }).success).toBe(false);
  });

  test("results are parsed strictly: no other version, no extra keys, no other id shape", () => {
    expect(ResultFile.safeParse({ ...ready, v: 4 }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(ResultFile.safeParse({ ...ready, v: 0 }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(ResultFile.safeParse({ ...ready, path: "/etc/passwd" }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(ResultFile.safeParse({ ...ready, id: "../x" }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(ResultFile.safeParse("ready").success).toBe(false);
  });

  test("3d Task 6: version 2 is version 1 with v 2 and, on a ready result, the scorer's model and score and the PDQ hash", () => {
    const v2 = { ...ready, v: 2 };
    expect(ResultFile.parse(v2)).toEqual(v2);
    const scored = { ...v2, r1: { model: R1_TEST_MODEL, score: 1 }, pdq: { impl: 1, hash: "ab".repeat(32), quality: 100 } };
    expect(ResultFile.parse(scored)).toEqual(scored);
    expect(ResultFile.parse({ ...v2, r1: { model: R1_MODEL.name, score: 0 } }).v).toBe(2);
    expect(ResultFile.safeParse({ v: 2, id: ID, status: "failed", reason: "corrupt_image" }).success).toBe(true);
    // Version 1 as it stood takes neither member; a failed result of either version takes none.
    expect(ResultFile.safeParse({ ...ready, r1: { model: R1_TEST_MODEL, score: 1 } }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(ResultFile.safeParse({ v: 2, id: ID, status: "failed", reason: "corrupt_image", r1: { model: R1_TEST_MODEL, score: 1 } }).success).toBe(false);
    // Every range and member is held: a score outside 0 to 1, a model's name of other characters or too long, a hash that is
    // not 64 lower-case hex characters, a quality outside 0 to 100, a member more.
    for (const r1 of [{ model: R1_TEST_MODEL, score: 1.5 }, { model: R1_TEST_MODEL, score: -0.1 }, { model: "Model", score: 0 }, { model: "m".repeat(65), score: 0 }, { model: "a b", score: 0 }, { model: R1_TEST_MODEL, score: 0, extra: 1 }]) {
      expect(ResultFile.safeParse({ ...v2, r1 }).success, JSON.stringify(r1)).toBe(false);
    }
    for (const pdq of [{ impl: 0, hash: "ab".repeat(32), quality: 50 }, { impl: 1, hash: "AB".repeat(32), quality: 50 }, { impl: 1, hash: "ab".repeat(31), quality: 50 }, { impl: 1, hash: "ab".repeat(32), quality: 101 }]) {
      expect(ResultFile.safeParse({ ...v2, pdq }).success, JSON.stringify(pdq)).toBe(false);
    }
    expect(ResultFile.safeParse({ ...v2, score: 0.9 }).success).toBe(false);
  });

  test("3d Task 6: the classifier's identity is the research's model, whose weights no build of 3d carries", () => {
    expect(R1_MODEL).toEqual({ name: "marqo/nsfw-image-detection-384", bytes: 22_450_955, sha256: null });
    expect(R1_MODEL_NAME.test(R1_MODEL.name)).toBe(true);
    expect(R1_MODEL_NAME.test(R1_TEST_MODEL)).toBe(true);
    expect(R1_TEST_MODEL).not.toBe(R1_MODEL.name);
  });

  test("3d Task 6: the test scorer's marker is a block of one colour in the top left corner, read within its tolerance", () => {
    expect(R1_MARKER.side).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(64);
    const image = (width: number, height: number, corner: [number, number, number], channels = 3) => {
      const pixels = new Uint8Array(width * height * channels).fill(40);
      for (let y = 0; y < R1_MARKER.side && y < height; y++) {
        for (let x = 0; x < R1_MARKER.side && x < width; x++) pixels.set(corner, (y * width + x) * channels);
      }
      return pixels;
    };
    const magenta: [number, number, number] = [R1_MARKER.red, R1_MARKER.green, R1_MARKER.blue];
    expect(carriesR1Marker(image(200, 100, magenta), 200, 100, 3)).toBe(true);
    expect(carriesR1Marker(image(200, 100, magenta, 4), 200, 100, 4)).toBe(true);
    // A lossy source's few levels of noise pass; another colour, or a corner without the block, does not.
    expect(carriesR1Marker(image(200, 100, [250, 6, 249]), 200, 100, 3)).toBe(true);
    expect(carriesR1Marker(image(200, 100, [200, 30, 30]), 200, 100, 3)).toBe(false);
    expect(carriesR1Marker(new Uint8Array(200 * 100 * 3).fill(40), 200, 100, 3)).toBe(false);
    // An image smaller than the probe, a grey image and a buffer too short carry none.
    expect(carriesR1Marker(image(8, 8, magenta), 8, 8, 3)).toBe(false);
    expect(carriesR1Marker(image(200, 100, magenta, 1), 200, 100, 1)).toBe(false);
    expect(carriesR1Marker(new Uint8Array(10), 200, 100, 3)).toBe(false);

    expect(ResultFile.parse(v3)).toEqual(v3);
    expect(ResultFile.parse({ ...v3, width: 400, height: 400, avatar: true })).toEqual({ ...v3, width: 400, height: 400, avatar: true });
    const scored = { ...v3, avatar: true, r1: { model: R1_TEST_MODEL, score: 0.5 }, pdq: { impl: 1, hash: "ab".repeat(32), quality: 100 } };
    expect(ResultFile.parse(scored)).toEqual(scored);
    expect(ResultFile.safeParse({ v: 3, id: ID, status: "failed", reason: "corrupt_image" }).success).toBe(true);
    // The mark is only ever true, and only on a ready result of version 3: a failed result, and versions 1 and 2, carry none.
    expect(ResultFile.safeParse({ ...v3, avatar: false }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(ResultFile.safeParse({ v: 3, id: ID, status: "failed", reason: "corrupt_image", avatar: true }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(ResultFile.safeParse({ ...ready, avatar: true }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(ResultFile.safeParse({ ...ready, v: 2, avatar: true }).success).toBe(false);
    // Version 4 is refused, as every version a build does not know.
    expect(ResultFile.safeParse({ ...ready, v: 4 }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(ResultFile.safeParse({ ...ready, v: 4, avatar: true }).success).toBe(false);
  });

  test("2d Task 3: an avatar's job file is one line of JSON, its version and its crop, read strictly and bounded", () => {
    expect(AvatarJob.parse({ v: 1, crop: "centre" })).toEqual({ v: 1, crop: "centre" });
    for (const crop of ["start", "centre", "end"]) expect(AvatarJob.parse({ v: 1, crop }).crop).toBe(crop);
    for (const bad of [{ v: 1 }, { v: 2, crop: "centre" }, { v: 1, crop: "center" }, { v: 1, crop: "centre", size: 400 }, { crop: "centre" }, "centre", null]) {
      expect(AvatarJob.safeParse(bad).success, JSON.stringify(bad)).toBe(false);
    }
    expect(MAX_JOB_BYTES).toBe(256);
    expect(JSON.stringify({ v: 1, crop: "centre" }).length).toBeLessThan(MAX_JOB_BYTES);
  });

  test("the heartbeat is a version and a time", () => {
    expect(Heartbeat.parse({ v: 1, at: 1_789_000_000_000 })).toEqual({ v: 1, at: 1_789_000_000_000 });
    expect(Heartbeat.safeParse({ v: 1, at: -1 }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(Heartbeat.safeParse({ v: 1, at: 1, extra: true }).success).toBe(false);
  });
});
```

```sql
-- Everything below is written by hand (2d design, sections 6.4, 6.6 and 6.8; Task 3). The generated lines above add the
-- enum media_kind, created whole with the contracts' MEDIA_KINDS; post_media's kind, profile_id (the profile the row is the
-- avatar of, with no on delete clause: no profile row is ever deleted, and the purge deletes the rows) and avatar_sha256;
-- the CHECKs post_media_kind_place, post_media_avatar_owner and post_media_avatar_sha256 (an avatar's hash is 64 lowercase
-- hex characters, never null, a post's image has none); the unique index post_media_avatar_idx, one avatar a profile, which avatarsOf
-- reads; post_media_owner_avatar_idx, an owner's avatars; and the drop of profiles.avatar_path (decision 18), with which its
-- column grant of 0020 goes. As in 0049: every function is owned by the migrator, pins its search path to public and
-- pg_temp and has EXECUTE taken from PUBLIC; a refusal is a code word, under SQLSTATE 42501 where it guards a column; the
-- new enum and every other enum are compared as text in every body. Each replaced function is written in full from its
-- newest text, named at each, with the changes named there and no other; CREATE OR REPLACE keeps its owner and its revoked
-- EXECUTE, and every replacement states its definer flag and pinned search path again. A trigger whose columns change is
-- dropped and created again under its name, since the columns of an UPDATE OF trigger are part of the trigger.
--
-- Same-event row triggers fire in the order of their names. BEFORE UPDATE OF profile_id: post_media_avatar_guard, then
-- post_media_refused. So for the API's role the guard refuses an erased row's set (avatar_column) before the refusal reads
-- it; post_media_refused's erased arm is reached by a role the guard skips, the migrator, and activity-schema.test.ts tests
-- its three arms as the migrator, and the refusal's and the hold's arms as the API role too.

-- 1. The grants (6.6). profile_id under the guard below; kind and avatar_sha256 are written by the insert alone (INSERT is
-- a table privilege of the API role, 0001), never updated: no grant names them.
GRANT UPDATE ("profile_id") ON "public"."post_media" TO korbat_api;--> statement-breakpoint

-- 2. post_media_avatar_guard, plain, BEFORE UPDATE OF profile_id, for every role but the migrator (6.4): profile_id moves
-- only from a value to null (a detach, always allowed) or from null to the row's own owner_id, and only on a row of kind
-- avatar that is ready, visible and not erased, whose owner's profile is not deleted. Every other change is refused
-- avatar_column under SQLSTATE 42501. The account's standing is the writing statement's (setAvatar takes the acting row
-- through 3e's predicate first, 7.3); the guard does not read it. The profile is read in a statement of its own, after the
-- row's lock, so a purge that committed meanwhile is seen.
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."post_media_avatar_guard"() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
DECLARE
  v_live boolean;
BEGIN
  IF current_user = 'korbat_migrate' OR NEW.profile_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM OLD.profile_id OR NEW.profile_id IS NULL THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;
  IF OLD.profile_id IS NOT NULL OR NEW.profile_id <> NEW.owner_id OR NEW.kind::text <> 'avatar' OR NEW.status::text <> 'ready'
      OR NEW.moderation_state::text <> 'visible' OR NEW.erased_at IS NOT NULL THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'avatar_column' USING ERRCODE = '42501';
  END IF;
  SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.profiles p WHERE p.id = NEW.owner_id AND p.deleted_at IS NULL) INTO v_live;
  IF NOT v_live THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'avatar_column' USING ERRCODE = '42501';
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."post_media_avatar_guard"() FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint
CREATE TRIGGER "post_media_avatar_guard" BEFORE UPDATE OF "profile_id" ON "public"."post_media" FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION "public"."post_media_avatar_guard"();--> statement-breakpoint

-- 3. post_media_insert, replaced from its text in 0015_greedy_zuras (6.4): a row inserted with a profile_id is refused
-- (moderation_column, 42501), as one that names a post is, for every role. INSERT is a table privilege, and the guard above
-- fires only on UPDATE, so an inserted row could otherwise be an avatar before any check had seen it. Everything else is
-- 0015's: a row is born on no post, visible, unheld and unerased.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION "public"."post_media_insert"() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
BEGIN
  IF NEW.post_id IS NOT NULL OR NEW.profile_id IS NOT NULL THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'moderation_column' USING ERRCODE = '42501';
  END IF;
  NEW.moderation_state := 'visible';
  NEW.hold_until := NULL;
  NEW.erased_at := NULL;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;--> statement-breakpoint

-- 4. post_media_refused, replaced from its text in 0039_known_material (6.4, 7.3 step 2): it fires BEFORE UPDATE OF post_id
-- and profile_id, with the same refusal for either column going from null to a value: upload_refused while a row of
-- upload_refusals names the image, while the row is erased, or while its hold_until is infinity, the refusals read in a
-- statement of their own after the row's lock, as for a post's image. The API answers it avatar_not_ready for an avatar.
-- Still a definer: the API's role cannot read upload_refusals' every row.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION "public"."post_media_refused"() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
DECLARE
  v_refused boolean;
BEGIN
  IF NOT ((OLD.post_id IS NULL AND NEW.post_id IS NOT NULL) OR (OLD.profile_id IS NULL AND NEW.profile_id IS NOT NULL)) THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;
  SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.upload_refusals r WHERE r.media_id = OLD.id) INTO v_refused;
  IF v_refused OR OLD.erased_at IS NOT NULL OR OLD.hold_until = 'infinity'::timestamptz THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'upload_refused';
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;--> statement-breakpoint

CREATE TRIGGER "post_media_refused" BEFORE UPDATE OF "post_id", "profile_id" ON "public"."post_media" FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION "public"."post_media_refused"();--> statement-breakpoint

-- case about the account with a suspect item nobody answered. With no post, an avatar's row can be frozen by this arm
-- alone. post_media_keep reads it below, and the media repository's disposal (DISPOSABLE) reads it for an avatar on no
-- post, so that it does not take again, round after round, a row the trigger keeps: the API names frozen_for nowhere
-- (apps/api/test/architecture.test.ts). EXECUTE for the API role alone, as post_frozen's.
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."account_frozen"(account uuid) RETURNS boolean
LANGUAGE sql STABLE SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
  SELECT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM public.cases c
    JOIN public.intake_items i ON i.case_id = c.id AND i.suspect AND i.answered_by IS NULL
    WHERE c.closed_at IS NULL AND c.target_type = 'account' AND c.target_id = account_frozen.account)
$$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."account_frozen"(uuid) FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION "public"."account_frozen"(uuid) TO korbat_api;--> statement-breakpoint

-- 6. post_media_keep, replaced from its text in 0015_greedy_zuras (6.4): a row on no post is also retained while it is of
-- kind avatar and its owner has an account case frozen by a suspect report (account_frozen, frozen_for's second arm), read
-- in a statement of its own after the row's lock and refused outside READ COMMITTED as for a row on a post, so a delete
-- that waited for an intake's lock reads the suspect item it committed. Its owner's removal, a replacement, the sweeper
-- and the purge then skip such a row, as they skip a held one. An upload on no post that is no avatar still never reads
-- the predicate. Task 4 (avatar_moderation) adds the seal's arm. The rest is 0015's.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION "public"."post_media_keep"() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql VOLATILE SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
DECLARE
  retained boolean;
BEGIN
  IF OLD.post_id IS NULL THEN
    retained := coalesce(OLD.hold_until > now(), false);
    IF NOT retained AND OLD.kind::text = 'avatar' THEN
      IF current_setting('transaction_isolation') <> 'read committed' THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'read_committed_only' USING ERRCODE = '25000';
      END IF;
      SELECT public.account_frozen(OLD.owner_id) INTO retained;
    END IF;
  ELSE
    IF current_setting('transaction_isolation') <> 'read committed' THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'read_committed_only' USING ERRCODE = '25000';
    END IF;
    IF OLD.hold_until > now() THEN
      retained := true;
    ELSE
      SELECT public.frozen_for(OLD.post_id, OLD.owner_id) INTO retained;
    END IF;
  END IF;
  IF retained THEN
    IF pg_trigger_depth() > 1 THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'post_media row % is retained', OLD.id USING ERRCODE = '23001';
    END IF;
    RETURN NULL;
  END IF;
  RETURN OLD;
END $$;--> statement-breakpoint

-- 7. post_media_purge, replaced from its text in 0035_edge_purges (6.4, 7.6 "The edge"), with the same body and two
-- changes: a row counts as served when it was on a post or was an avatar (OLD.post_id or OLD.profile_id set), and a row
-- whose profile_id goes from a value to null writes cause state (an avatar replaced, removed or, in Task 4, reset). The
-- trigger fires on moderation_state, erased_at and profile_id, and on delete. So the purge's delete of a current avatar
-- writes deleted, its detach state, and an upload never set, or an avatar detached before, writes nothing. Task 4
-- (avatar_moderation) adds the released cause of an avatar.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION "public"."post_media_purge"() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
DECLARE
  v_cause text;
BEGIN
  IF (OLD.post_id IS NULL AND OLD.profile_id IS NULL) OR OLD.status::text <> 'ready' THEN
    RETURN NULL;
  END IF;
  IF TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN
    v_cause := 'deleted';
  ELSIF OLD.erased_at IS NULL AND NEW.erased_at IS NOT NULL THEN
    v_cause := CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.release_posts r WHERE r.post_id = OLD.post_id) THEN 'released' ELSE 'deleted' END;
  ELSIF OLD.moderation_state::text = 'visible' AND NEW.moderation_state::text <> 'visible' THEN
    v_cause := 'state';
  ELSIF OLD.profile_id IS NOT NULL AND NEW.profile_id IS NULL THEN
    v_cause := 'state';
  ELSE
    RETURN NULL;
  END IF;
  INSERT INTO public.edge_purges (media_id, cause) VALUES (OLD.id, v_cause);
  RETURN NULL;
END $$;--> statement-breakpoint
DROP TRIGGER "post_media_purge" ON "public"."post_media";--> statement-breakpoint
CREATE TRIGGER "post_media_purge" AFTER UPDATE OF "moderation_state", "erased_at", "profile_id" OR DELETE ON "public"."post_media" FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION "public"."post_media_purge"();
```

```json
        },

        }
      },
      "checkConstraints": {
        "decisions_rule_id": {
          "name": "decisions_rule_id",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"rule_id\" in ('R1', 'R2', 'R3', 'R4', 'R5', 'R6')"
        },
        "decisions_category": {
          "name": "decisions_category",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"category\" in ('STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ANIMAL_WELFARE', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CONSUMER_INFORMATION', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE_AGAINST_WOMEN', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_DATA_PROTECTION_AND_PRIVACY_VIOLATIONS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ILLEGAL_OR_HARMFUL_SPEECH', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_INTELLECTUAL_PROPERTY_INFRINGEMENTS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NEGATIVE_EFFECTS_ON_CIVIC_DISCOURSE_OR_ELECTIONS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_PROTECTION_OF_MINORS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_RISK_FOR_PUBLIC_SECURITY', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SCAMS_AND_FRAUD', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SELF_HARM', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_UNSAFE_AND_PROHIBITED_PRODUCTS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_VIOLENCE')"
        },
        "decisions_category_keyword": {
          "name": "decisions_category_keyword",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"category_keyword\" in ('KEYWORD_TERRORIST_CONTENT')"
        },
        "decisions_automated_decision": {
          "name": "decisions_automated_decision",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"automated_decision\" in ('fully', 'partially', 'not_automated')"
        },
        "decisions_territorial_scope": {
          "name": "decisions_territorial_scope",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"territorial_scope\" = 'worldwide'"
        },
        "decisions_review_target": {
          "name": "decisions_review_target",
          "value": "(\"decisions\".\"kind\" in ('review', 'correction')) = (\"decisions\".\"reviews_decision_id\" is not null) and (\"decisions\".\"kind\" = 'review') = (\"decisions\".\"appeal_id\" is not null)"
        },
        "decisions_interim": {
          "name": "decisions_interim",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"kind\" <> 'interim' or \"decisions\".\"through_seq\" = 0"
        },
        "decisions_ground_rule": {
          "name": "decisions_ground_rule",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"ground\" is distinct from 'incompatible' or \"decisions\".\"rule_id\" is not null"
        },
        "decisions_ground_law": {
          "name": "decisions_ground_law",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"ground\" is distinct from 'illegal' or \"decisions\".\"legal_reference_digest\" is not null or \"decisions\".\"kind\"::text = 'order'"
        },
        "decisions_restricted": {
          "name": "decisions_restricted",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"outcome\" <> 'restricted' or (\"decisions\".\"ground\" is not null and ((\"decisions\".\"facts_digest\" is not null and \"decisions\".\"reason_digest\" is not null) or \"decisions\".\"decided_by\" is null)) or \"decisions\".\"kind\"::text = 'order'"
        },
        "decisions_decider": {
          "name": "decisions_decider",
          "value": "(\"decisions\".\"decided_by\" is null) = (\"decisions\".\"automated_decision\" = 'fully') and (\"decisions\".\"decided_by\" is not null or \"decisions\".\"kind\"::text = 'interim')"
        },
        "decisions_match_answer_reason": {
          "name": "decisions_match_answer_reason",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"match_answer_reason\" in ('source_withdrew', 'counsel', 'other')"
        },
        "decisions_informed": {
          "name": "decisions_informed",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"informed_at\" is not null or \"decisions\".\"author_mail\"::text = 'none'"
        },
        "decisions_digests": {
          "name": "decisions_digests",
          "value": "(\"decisions\".\"facts_digest\" is null or \"decisions\".\"facts_digest\" ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$') and (\"decisions\".\"reason_digest\" is null or \"decisions\".\"reason_digest\" ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$') and (\"decisions\".\"legal_reference_digest\" is null or \"decisions\".\"legal_reference_digest\" ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$')"
        },
        "decisions_keyword": {
          "name": "decisions_keyword",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"category_keyword\" is null or \"decisions\".\"ground\" is not distinct from 'illegal'"
        },
        "decisions_law_no_rule": {
          "name": "decisions_law_no_rule",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"ground\" is distinct from 'illegal' or \"decisions\".\"rule_id\" is null"
        },
        "decisions_reversal_plain": {
          "name": "decisions_reversal_plain",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"kind\" not in ('review', 'correction') or (\"decisions\".\"ground\" is null and \"decisions\".\"rule_id\" is null and \"decisions\".\"category_keyword\" is null and \"decisions\".\"facts_digest\" is null and \"decisions\".\"legal_reference_digest\" is null)"
        }
      },
      "isRLSEnabled": true
    },

      "checkConstraints": {
        "intakes_ref": {
          "name": "intakes_ref",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"ref\" ~ '^N-[A-Z2-7]{10}$'"
        },
        "intakes_rule_id": {
          "name": "intakes_rule_id",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"rule_id\" in ('R1', 'R2', 'R3', 'R4', 'R5', 'R6')"
        },
        "intakes_category": {
          "name": "intakes_category",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"category\" in ('STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ANIMAL_WELFARE', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CONSUMER_INFORMATION', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE_AGAINST_WOMEN', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_DATA_PROTECTION_AND_PRIVACY_VIOLATIONS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ILLEGAL_OR_HARMFUL_SPEECH', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_INTELLECTUAL_PROPERTY_INFRINGEMENTS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NEGATIVE_EFFECTS_ON_CIVIC_DISCOURSE_OR_ELECTIONS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_PROTECTION_OF_MINORS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_RISK_FOR_PUBLIC_SECURITY', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SCAMS_AND_FRAUD', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SELF_HARM', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_UNSAFE_AND_PROHIBITED_PRODUCTS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_VIOLENCE')"
        },
        "intakes_category_keyword": {
          "name": "intakes_category_keyword",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"category_keyword\" in ('KEYWORD_CHILD_SEXUAL_ABUSE_MATERIAL', 'KEYWORD_CHILD_SEXUAL_ABUSE_MATERIAL_DEEPFAKE', 'KEYWORD_GROOMING_SEXUAL_ENTICEMENT_MINORS')"
        },
        "intakes_cited_law_len": {
          "name": "intakes_cited_law_len",
          "value": "char_length(\"intakes\".\"cited_law\") <= 300"
        },
        "intakes_explanation_len": {
          "name": "intakes_explanation_len",
          "value": "char_length(\"intakes\".\"explanation\") <= 2000"
        },
        "intakes_has_ground": {
          "name": "intakes_has_ground",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"rule_id\" is not null or \"intakes\".\"alleges_illegal\" or \"intakes\".\"csam\" or \"intakes\".\"kind\"::text = 'automated'"
        },
        "intakes_illegal_elements": {
          "name": "intakes_illegal_elements",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"kind\" <> 'user' or not \"intakes\".\"alleges_illegal\" or \"intakes\".\"csam\" or (\"intakes\".\"bona_fide\" and (\"intakes\".\"explanation\" is not null or \"intakes\".\"erased_at\" is not null))"
        },
        "intakes_finding_legal": {
          "name": "intakes_finding_legal",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"kind\" <> 'finding' or not \"intakes\".\"alleges_illegal\""
        },
        "intakes_illegal_not_tc": {
          "name": "intakes_illegal_not_tc",
          "value": "not \"intakes\".\"alleges_illegal\" or \"intakes\".\"category\" <> 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC'"
        },
        "intakes_csam": {
          "name": "intakes_csam",
          "value": "not \"intakes\".\"csam\" or (\"intakes\".\"category\" = 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_PROTECTION_OF_MINORS' and \"intakes\".\"reporter_id\" is null and \"intakes\".\"contact_id\" is null)"
        },
        "intakes_contact_signed_out": {
          "name": "intakes_contact_signed_out",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"contact_id\" is null or \"intakes\".\"channel\" = 'signed_out'"
        },
        "intakes_reporter_signed_in": {
          "name": "intakes_reporter_signed_in",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"reporter_id\" is null or \"intakes\".\"channel\" = 'signed_in'"
        },
        "intakes_finding": {
          "name": "intakes_finding",
          "value": "(\"intakes\".\"kind\" = 'finding') = (\"intakes\".\"finding_by\" is not null) and (\"intakes\".\"kind\" = 'finding') = (\"intakes\".\"channel\" = 'staff') and (\"intakes\".\"kind\"::text = 'automated') = (\"intakes\".\"channel\"::text = 'system')"
        },
        "intakes_lookup": {
          "name": "intakes_lookup",
          "value": "(\"intakes\".\"lookup_hash\" is not null) = (\"intakes\".\"channel\" = 'signed_out' or \"intakes\".\"csam\")"
        },
        "intakes_erased": {
          "name": "intakes_erased",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"erased_at\" is null or (\"intakes\".\"explanation\" is null and \"intakes\".\"cited_law\" is null)"
        },
        "intakes_r2_finding_only": {
          "name": "intakes_r2_finding_only",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"rule_id\" is distinct from 'R2' or \"intakes\".\"kind\"::text in ('finding', 'automated')"
        },

        },
        "authority_notifications_duties": {
          "name": "authority_notifications_duties",
          "value": "\"authority_notifications\".\"duties\" <@ array['dsa18_1', 'dsa18_2', 'tco14_5', 'voluntary']::text[]"

        "authority_notifications_sent_kinds": {

        },
        "authority_notifications_opened_via": {
          "name": "authority_notifications_opened_via",
          "value": "\"authority_notifications\".\"opened_via\" in ('system', 'cli')"
        },
        "authority_notifications_seal": {
          "name": "authority_notifications_seal",
          "value": "(\"authority_notifications\".\"opened_via\" = 'system') = (\"authority_notifications\".\"seal_action_id\" is not null)"
        },
        "authority_notifications_closed": {
          "name": "authority_notifications_closed",
          "value": "(\"authority_notifications\".\"state\" = 'owed') = (\"authority_notifications\".\"closed_at\" is null)"
        },
        "authority_notifications_declined": {
          "name": "authority_notifications_declined",
          "value": "(\"authority_notifications\".\"state\" = 'declined') = (\"authority_notifications\".\"declined_reason\" is not null)"
        },
        "authority_notifications_sent": {
          "name": "authority_notifications_sent",
          "value": "\"authority_notifications\".\"state\" <> 'sent' or (\"authority_notifications\".\"sent_at\" is not null and \"authority_notifications\".\"authority\" is not null and \"authority_notifications\".\"channel\" is not null and \"authority_notifications\".\"sent_kinds\" is not null and cardinality(\"authority_notifications\".\"duties\") > 0 and \"authority_notifications\".\"not_kept_version\" is not null)"
        },
        "authority_notifications_answered": {
          "name": "authority_notifications_answered",
          "value": "\"authority_notifications\".\"answer\" is null or \"authority_notifications\".\"answered_at\" is not null"
        },
        "authority_notifications_texts": {
          "name": "authority_notifications_texts",
          "value": "char_length(\"authority_notifications\".\"check_reason\") <= 500 and char_length(\"authority_notifications\".\"state_basis\") <= 500 and char_length(\"authority_notifications\".\"declined_reason\") <= 500 and char_length(\"authority_notifications\".\"checked_by\") <= 200 and char_length(\"authority_notifications\".\"sent_by\") <= 200 and char_length(\"authority_notifications\".\"authority\") <= 200 and char_length(\"authority_notifications\".\"channel\") <= 200 and char_length(\"authority_notifications\".\"receipt\") <= 500 and char_length(\"authority_notifications\".\"own_reference\") <= 200 and char_length(\"authority_notifications\".\"their_reference\") <= 200"
        }
      },
```

```ts
import type { Logger } from "pino";
import { ACTIVITY_DEFAULTS, OrderNoticeFacts, OrderTexts, STANDING_RULES, type Platform } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { ActivityExport, ReceivedEntry } from "../../activity";
import type { AccountExport } from "../../auth";
import type { ImportRecord } from "../../imports";
import type { ModerationExport } from "../../moderation";
import type { ProfileExport } from "../../social";
import { AccountError, type AccountDeps } from "../context";
import type { OpenFile, ZipWriter } from "../zip";

/** One export a day (1b design, section 10). */
export const EXPORTS_PER_WINDOW = 1;
export const EXPORT_WINDOW_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;

const exportLimitKey = (userId: string) => `export:${userId}`;

/** The entry an image has in the archive; export.json names it under the post's media. */
export function mediaEntry(id: string): string {

/** The download's name: the handle and the day, so several exports of one account sort by date. */

}

 * and the images, each behind the media module's checked open, go first, so `missingMedia` is complete
 * by the time the JSON that lists it is written.
 */
export interface ExportPlan {
  exportedAt: Date;
  /** The handle of the session that asked for the export: the id the auth module lists each session under. */
  currentSession: string;
  account: AccountExport;
  profile: ProfileExport;
  /** The decisions about the account that it was told of and its own reports, as the moderation module hands them over (3c design, section 7.11). */
  moderation: ModerationExport;
  /** 3b Task 6 (design, section 11.2): the account's imports, newest first, as the imports module hands them over. */
  imports: ImportRecord[];
  /** 2d (design, section 11.2): the seen marker and the rules, read at once, and the received entries, read in pages. */
  activity: ActivityExport;
  images: { id: string; open: OpenFile }[];
  /** 2d Task 3 (7.8, 11.2): the account's picture, its id and size, as the media module hands it over; null without one. */
  avatar: { id: string; width: number; height: number } | null;
  /** The images whose file the checked open refused or could not find, filled while the images are written. */
  missingMedia: string[];
}

/**
 * Counts one export of the account in the daily window and refuses once it is used up. Taken before
 * anything is built or streamed, so a stream that fails midway still counts; Retry-After says when the
 * window resets.
 */
export async function enforceExportLimit(deps: AccountDeps, userId: string): Promise<void> {
  let hit: { count: number; resetMs: number };
  try {
    hit = await deps.limits.hit(exportLimitKey(userId), EXPORT_WINDOW_MS);
  } catch {
    // Fails closed: an export that cannot be counted is not made, and the client is told to retry shortly.
    throw new AccountError("service_unavailable", 503, undefined, 30);
  }
  if (hit.count > EXPORTS_PER_WINDOW) throw new AccountError("rate_limited", 429, undefined, Math.max(1, Math.ceil(hit.resetMs / 1000)));
}

/**
 * Gives the day's export back after a failure before the archive's first byte (a pool timeout, a
 * restart): the owner received nothing, so the attempt must not use up the day. Best effort: when the
 * store cannot be reached, the export stays counted and a warning says so, which costs the owner a day
 * at worst.
 */
export async function giveBackExport(deps: AccountDeps, userId: string, log: Logger): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await deps.limits.release(exportLimitKey(userId));
  } catch (err) {
    log.warn({ err, userId }, "account export: the day's export could not be given back after a failure before the first byte");
  }
}

const iso = (at: Date): string => at.toISOString();
const isoOrNull = (at: Date | null): string | null => (at ? at.toISOString() : null);

/**
 * What an account module built without the moderation module writes: the member is part of the format, so it is always
 * there. Its reporting counts are empty over the standing rules' frame, the number the moderation module would read.
 */
const NO_MODERATION: ModerationExport = {
  decisions: [],
  reports: [],
  strikes: [],
  standing: [],
  replies: [],
  reporting: { frameDays: STANDING_RULES.reportFrameDays, days: [], marks: [], markedReports: 0 },
  uploads: [],
  releases: [],
};

/** What an account module built without the activity module writes: the member is part of the format, so it is always there. */
const NO_ACTIVITY: ActivityExport = {
  seenAt: null,
  settings: { ...ACTIVITY_DEFAULTS },
  received: {
    async *[Symbol.asyncIterator]() {

    },
  },
};

/**
 * Reads what is needed before the first byte: the account's facts, sessions, devices and events (one
 * read, bounded by the 90 days of events), the profile's own fields, the list of images, and the
 * moderation member (the decisions the account was told of and its own reports, both short lists). The
 * four modules are asked at once, so a read that fails costs the owner nothing: no byte was sent yet.
 * `currentSession` is the handle of the session asking, which marks its entry among the sessions.
 * `pageSize` is how many rows of each profile list are read at a time; tests lower it.
 */
export async function buildExport(deps: AccountDeps, userId: string, currentSession: string, now: Date, pageSize?: number): Promise<ExportPlan> {
  const [account, profile, images, avatar, moderation, imports, activity] = await Promise.all([
    deps.auth.exportAccount(userId),
    deps.social.exportProfile(userId, pageSize),
    deps.media.exportImages(userId),
    // 2d Task 3: the picture's file is one of the images, the 400 px square; this names it in the profile.
    deps.media.exportAvatar(userId),
    // The server always hands the moderation module over; a test of the other members may leave it out.
    deps.moderation ? deps.moderation.exportFor(userId) : NO_MODERATION,
    // 3b Task 6: and the imports module; without it the member is empty.
    deps.imports ? deps.imports.exportFor(userId) : Promise.resolve([]),
    // 2d (11.2): and the activity module; without it the member holds the defaults and no entry.
    deps.activity ? deps.activity.exportEntries(userId, pageSize) : Promise.resolve(NO_ACTIVITY),
  ]);

}

/** A list member of export.json, read in pages and written one element at a time. */
class Paged<T> {
  constructor(
    readonly pages: AsyncIterable<readonly T[]>,
    readonly element: (row: T) => unknown,
  ) {}
}

/** An object member written member by member, so that one of its members may be a list read in pages (2d's `activity`). */
class Members {
  constructor(readonly members: [string, unknown][]) {}
}

/** An array already in memory, as one page. */
function inMemory<T>(rows: readonly T[], element: (row: T) => unknown): Paged<T> {
  return new Paged(
    (async function* () {
      yield rows;
    })(),
    element,
  );
}

/** Fragments are gathered into pieces of about this many UTF-16 units, at most 3 bytes each in UTF-8: well under 64 KiB. */
const PIECE_CHARS = 16 * 1024;

/**
 * export.json in pieces, written exactly as JSON.stringify(document, null, 2) writes the whole

 * stringified on its own and indented to its depth (JSON.stringify's output holds line breaks only
 * between tokens; one inside a string is escaped, so indenting after every line break is exact). No list
 * is ever whole in memory: each is read page by page as it is written.

export async function* exportJson(plan: ExportPlan): AsyncGenerator<string> {

  for await (const fragment of documentFragments(plan)) {
    buffer += fragment;
    if (buffer.length >= PIECE_CHARS) {
      yield buffer;
      buffer = "";
    }
  }
  if (buffer.length > 0) yield buffer;
}

async function* objectFragments(members: [string, unknown][], pad: string): AsyncGenerator<string> {
  yield "{\n";
  for (const [index, [key, value]] of members.entries()) {
    yield `${index === 0 ? "" : ",\n"}${pad}  ${JSON.stringify(key)}: `;

  }
  yield `\n${pad}}`;

/** An object's members in the order of a format's shape, and no other member. */
function inShapeOrder<T extends object>(shape: object, value: T): T {
  const source = value as Record<string, unknown>;
  return Object.fromEntries(Object.keys(shape).map((key) => [key, source[key]])) as T;
}

/** The moderation member with every entry's members in the order of the format (ExportFormat in the contracts). */
function moderationMember(moderation: ModerationExport): ModerationExport {
  return {
    decisions: moderation.decisions.map((decision) => ({
      id: decision.id,
      decidedOn: decision.decidedOn,
      postId: decision.postId,
      kind: decision.kind,
      outcome: decision.outcome,
      ground: decision.ground,
      ruleId: decision.ruleId,
      rulesVersion: decision.rulesVersion,
      measures: decision.measures.map((measure) => ({ kind: measure.kind, mediaId: measure.mediaId, noEffect: measure.noEffect })),
      reversals: decision.reversals.map((reversal) => ({ kind: reversal.kind, mediaId: reversal.mediaId })),
      facts: decision.facts,
      reason: decision.reason,
      legalReference: decision.legalReference,
      appeal: decision.appeal === null ? null : decision.appeal.state === "pending" ? { state: "pending", result: null } : { state: "answered", result: decision.appeal.result },
      // 3f (W.7), and 3d review L14 (people12): an order's notice keeps its facts, the authority's words and the day of an

        ? {
            order: inShapeOrder(OrderNoticeFacts.shape, decision.order),
            ...(decision.orderTexts ? { orderTexts: inShapeOrder(OrderTexts.shape, decision.orderTexts) } : {}),
            erasedOn: decision.erasedOn ?? null,

      objection: decision.objection === null ? null : { text: decision.objection.text, createdAt: decision.objection.createdAt },

    reports: moderation.reports.map((report) => ({

      receivedAt: report.receivedAt,
      ground: report.ground,
      ruleId: report.ruleId,
      category: report.category,
      explanation: report.explanation,
      items: report.items.map((item) => ({ position: item.position, link: item.link, reexamines: item.reexamines, outcome: item.outcome, outcomeText: item.outcomeText, reexaminationOpen: item.reexaminationOpen })),
    })),
    // 3e (W.8): the strikes the account was given.
    strikes: moderation.strikes.map((strike) => ({ decisionId: strike.decisionId, postId: strike.postId, ruleId: strike.ruleId, givenAt: strike.givenAt, countsUntil: strike.countsUntil, overruledAt: strike.overruledAt })),
    // Then its suspensions, terminations and reporting measures, its replies to them, and its own reporting counts.
    standing: moderation.standing.map((entry) => ({
      decisionId: entry.decisionId,
      kind: entry.kind,
      basis: entry.basis,
      days: entry.days,
      announced: entry.announced,
      decidedAt: entry.decidedAt,
      earliestStart: entry.earliestStart,
      startsAt: entry.startsAt,
      endsAt: entry.endsAt,
      liftedAt: entry.liftedAt,
      liftedBy: entry.liftedBy,
      replaced: entry.replaced,
      basisEndedAt: entry.basisEndedAt,
      basisEndedBy: entry.basisEndedBy,
    })),
    replies: moderation.replies.map((reply) => ({ decisionId: reply.decisionId, filedAt: reply.filedAt, onTime: reply.onTime, text: reply.text, erasedAt: reply.erasedAt, answeredAt: reply.answeredAt, answeredBy: reply.answeredBy })),
    reporting: {
      frameDays: moderation.reporting.frameDays,
      days: moderation.reporting.days.map((entry) => ({ day: entry.day, reports: entry.reports })),
      marks: moderation.reporting.marks.map((mark) => ({ ref: mark.ref, position: mark.position, sentOn: mark.sentOn, markedAt: mark.markedAt, withdrawnAt: mark.withdrawnAt, counts: mark.counts })),
      markedReports: moderation.reporting.markedReports,
    },
    // 3d (W.10): the refused uploads as their notices read them, and the releases the account may be told of.
    uploads: moderation.uploads.map((upload) => ({

      matchKind: upload.matchKind,
      listedAs: upload.listedAs,

/** A member's array at the depth `pad` gives, as JSON.stringify writes it there: "[]" when empty, else one element per line group. */
async function* listFragments<T>(list: Paged<T>, pad: string): AsyncGenerator<string> {
  let first = true;
  for await (const page of list.pages) {
    for (const row of page) {
      yield `${first ? "[\n" : ",\n"}${pad}  ${indented(JSON.stringify(list.element(row), null, 2), `${pad}  `)}`;
      first = false;
    }
  }
  yield first ? "[]" : `\n${pad}]`;
}

const indented = (json: string, pad: string): string => json.replaceAll("\n", `\n${pad}`);

/**
 * Writes the archive: every image as a stored entry, then export.json, then the central directory.
 * export.json comes last so that missingMedia can name every image whose file the checked open refused
 * or did not find when its turn came (the sweeper may be between the row and the file), or that was no
 * longer the owner's to export by then: the media module reads each image's row again as it opens the
 * file, and opens none for an image deleted with its post, erased or sealed since the list was read.
 * The order of entries means nothing to a reader.
 */
export async function writeExport(writer: ZipWriter, plan: ExportPlan): Promise<void> {
  for (const image of plan.images) {
    if (!(await writer.addFile(mediaEntry(image.id), image.open))) plan.missingMedia.push(image.id);
  }
  await writer.addJsonPieces("export.json", exportJson(plan));
  await writer.end();
}
```

```ts
  /** Image uploads. Optional for the same reason; the server always wires it. */
  media?: Media;
  /** The account lifecycle (the data export). Optional for the same reason; the server always wires it. */
  account?: Account;
  /** The staff console's API. Mounted only while CONSOLE_ORIGIN is set; optional as the other modules are. */
  staff?: Staff;
  /** Reports and notices. Optional as the other modules are; the server always wires it, whether the console is on or off. */
  moderation?: Moderation;
  /** Checks that report a part being down without marking the API unhealthy, the image worker for one. */
  advisoryChecks?: HealthChecks;
  /** 3d: the public figures' two routes. Optional as the other modules are; the server always wires it. */
  transparency?: Transparency;
  /** 3b: import from other platforms. Optional as the other modules are; the server always wires it. */
  imports?: Imports;
  /** 2d: Activity. Optional as the other modules are; the server always wires it. */
  activity?: Activity;
}

export function createApp({ config, logger, rateLimitStore, healthChecks, auth, social, media, account, staff, moderation, advisoryChecks, transparency, imports, activity }: AppDeps) {
  const app = new Hono<AppEnv>();

  app.use(observability(logger));
  app.use(auth.clientIdentity);
  app.use(securityHeaders, noStore);
  const appCors = cors({ origin: config.TRUSTED_ORIGINS, credentials: true });
  app.use((c, next) => (isStaffPath(c.req.path) ? next() : appCors(c, next)));
  const jsonBodies = bodyLimit({
    maxSize: JSON_BODY_LIMIT_BYTES,
    onError: (c) => c.json(errorBody("payload_too_large", "The request body is too large", (c as typeof c & { get(key: "requestId"): string }).get("requestId")), 413),
  });
  app.use((c, next) => (isRawUpload(c.req.method, c.req.path) ? next() : jsonBodies(c, next)));
  // Image files come before the global limit and session resolution: they have their own bucket,
  // and a public image needs no session. Everything else under /api/media falls through to below.
  if (media) app.route("/api/media", media.fileRoutes);
  app.use(rateLimit({ name: "global", store: rateLimitStore, limit: 300, windowMs: 60_000, key: clientIpKey }));
  // 3f (design, section 7.12): the status of a post's page, which Caddy asks for every view of /post/*, with the visitor's
  // cookies: after the global limit, which counts it against the visitor, and before the session's resolution, so it
  // reads no session. Every other path falls through to below.
  if (social) app.route("/api", social.statusRoutes);
  // 3d (design, sections 9.1 and 10.6): GET /api/public/facts and /api/public/transparency, at the same place and for the
  // same reasons: counted against the visitor by the global limit, and answered before any session is read. Each sets its
  // own Cache-Control, which noStore leaves alone.
  if (transparency) app.route("/api", transparency.routes);
  app.use((c, next) => (isStaffPath(c.req.path) ? next() : auth.resolveSession(c, next)));

  app.route("/api/health", healthRoutes(healthChecks, config.KORBAT_VERSION, advisoryChecks));
  app.route("/api/auth", auth.routes);
  // 3e (design, section 7.12): /api/me from the auth module's meFor and the moderation module's standingFor, read at
  // every request; null without the moderation module (an app built for some tests) or without a profile. 2d Task 3 (9.3):
  // the account's own picture from the media module's avatarsOf, the same way: null without the media module or a profile.
  app.get("/api/me", auth.requireOnboarding, async (c) => {
    const session = c.get("session")!;
    const base = await auth.meFor(session);
    const standing = moderation && base.profile !== null ? await moderation.standingFor(session.userId) : null;
    const avatar = media && base.profile !== null ? ((await media.forPosts.avatarsOf([session.userId], session.userId)).get(session.userId) ?? null) : null;
    return c.json({ ...base, standing, avatar } satisfies MeResponse);
  });
  if (media) app.route("/api/media", media.routes);
  // 3b (design, section 9.1): every route behind the auth module's requireSession, CSRF included, like the social routes.
  if (imports) app.route("/api/imports", imports.routes);
  // 2d (design, section 9.2): every route behind the auth module's requireSession, CSRF included for the two writes.
  if (activity) app.route("/api/activity", activity.routes);
  if (account) app.route("/api/account", account.routes);
  // The console is off while CONSOLE_ORIGIN is unset: nothing is mounted, and every staff path is the unknown route below.
  if (staff && config.CONSOLE_ORIGIN !== undefined) app.route("/api/staff", staff.routes(config.CONSOLE_ORIGIN));
  // Reports and notices are taken, kept and given receipts whether or not the console is on: anyone may send one, signed
  // in or not, so these routes stand after session resolution and behind no session guard of their own.
  if (moderation) app.route("/api", moderation.routes);
  if (social) app.route("/api", social.routes);

  app.notFound((c) => c.json(errorBody("not_found", "No such route", c.get("requestId")), 404));
  app.onError((err, c) => {
    if (err instanceof AuthError) {
      if (err.retryAfterSeconds) c.header("Retry-After", String(err.retryAfterSeconds));
      return c.json(errorBody(err.code, err.message, c.get("requestId"), err.details), err.status);
    }
    if (err instanceof HTTPException) return c.json(errorBody("invalid_request", err.message, c.get("requestId")), err.status);
    if (err instanceof MediaError) return c.json(errorBody(err.code, err.message, c.get("requestId")), err.status);
    // 3b (design, sections 9.1 and 9.4): every refusal of an import with its status, never 500; wrong_offset carries the
    // stored size, so the app goes on from there.
    if (err instanceof ImportError) {
      if (err.retryAfterSeconds) c.header("Retry-After", String(err.retryAfterSeconds));
      return c.json(errorBody(err.code, err.message, c.get("requestId"), err.details), err.status);
    }
    if (err instanceof SocialError) {
      if (err.retryAfterSeconds) c.header("Retry-After", String(err.retryAfterSeconds));
      return c.json(errorBody(err.code, err.message, c.get("requestId")), err.status);
    }
    // 2d: a cursor of Activity that names no place; the limits of its two writes are the social module's (above).
    if (err instanceof ActivityError) return c.json(errorBody(err.code, err.message, c.get("requestId")), err.status);
    // The account routes render nothing themselves: their own errors and those of the three modules they call all land here.
    if (err instanceof AccountError) {
      if (err.retryAfterSeconds) c.header("Retry-After", String(err.retryAfterSeconds));
      return c.json(errorBody(err.code, err.message, c.get("requestId")), err.status);
    }
    // A moderation flow's refusal, from the app's routes or from the console's case routes.
    if (err instanceof ModerationError) {
      if (err.retryAfterSeconds) c.header("Retry-After", String(err.retryAfterSeconds));
      return c.json(errorBody(err.code, err.message, c.get("requestId"), err.details), err.status);
    }
    c.get("log").error({ err }, "unhandled error");
    return c.json(errorBody("internal", "Internal error", c.get("requestId")), 500);
  });

  return app;
}
```

```ts
import type { MeResponse, SessionsResponse } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { AuthError, type AuthDeps } from "../context";
import type { Session } from "../sessions";
import { notifyAccount } from "./notify";

/**
 * /api/me without the account's standing, which the moderation module reads (3e design, section 7.12), and (2d Task 3)
 * without its avatar, which the media module reads: app.ts composes the route from the three.
 */
export type MeWithoutStanding = Omit<MeResponse, "standing" | "avatar">;

/**
 * The signed-in account. The only response in the API that contains the email address. 3e: everything of /api/me but
 * the standing, which this module cannot read (it names no public table); the app composes the route from this and the
 * moderation module's standingFor.
 */
export async function me(deps: AuthDeps, session: Session): Promise<MeWithoutStanding> {
  const user = await deps.repo.findUserById(session.userId);
  if (!user) throw new AuthError("invalid_credentials", 401);
  return {
    user: {
      id: user.id,
      email: user.email,
      role: user.role,
      onboarded: user.onboardedAt !== null,
      mfaEnabled: user.totpEnabledAt !== null,
      hasPassword: user.passwordHash !== null,
      // The count only (1c design, section 7.5); the Security list is where the passkeys themselves are read.
      passkeys: await deps.repo.countPasskeys(user.id),
    },
    profile: await deps.profiles.find(user.id),
  };
}

/** The user's live sessions, each under its handle: the id that stays while the session's token rotates. */
export async function listSessions(deps: AuthDeps, session: Session): Promise<SessionsResponse> {
  return { sessions: await deps.sessions.list(session.userId, session.handle) };
}

/**
 * Revokes one of the user's own sessions, named by the handle the list gave, so a session that re-authenticated since
 * it was listed (its token rotated) is still revoked. False when no such live session belongs to them.
 */
export async function revokeSession(deps: AuthDeps, session: Session, handle: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const revoked = await deps.sessions.revoke(handle, session.userId);
  if (revoked) await deps.repo.appendEvent({ userId: session.userId, type: "session_revoked", deviceId: session.deviceId, metadata: { handle } });
  return revoked;
}

/** Signs out every session of the account, including the current one (the route requires fresh auth). */
export async function revokeAllSessions(deps: AuthDeps, session: Session): Promise<number> {
  const user = await deps.repo.findUserById(session.userId);
  const count = await deps.sessions.revokeAll(session.userId);
  await deps.repo.appendEvent({ userId: session.userId, type: "sessions_revoked_all", deviceId: session.deviceId, metadata: { count } });
  if (user) await notifyAccount(deps, user.email, "sessions_revoked_all", { count: String(count) });
  return count;
}

export async function signOut(deps: AuthDeps, session: Session): Promise<void> {
  await deps.sessions.revoke(session.handle, session.userId);
  await deps.repo.appendEvent({ userId: session.userId, type: "session_revoked", deviceId: session.deviceId, metadata: { signOut: true } });
}
```

```ts
export interface StoredFile {

/** 3d Task 7: the three digests of an upload's bytes as received (design, section 7.8 step 1). */
export interface ReceivedHashes {

  sha1: Buffer;
  md5: Buffer;

const READ_FLAGS = constants.O_RDONLY | (constants.O_NOFOLLOW ?? 0) | (constants.O_NONBLOCK ?? 0);

export function createMediaFiles(options: MediaFilesOptions) {
  const uploads = uploadsLayout(options.uploadsDir);
  const store = storeLayout(options.storeDir);
  const { log } = options;

   * Opens a file of the store for reading. Returns null unless the open handle is a regular file,

   */
  async function openStored(file: string, maxBytes: number): Promise<StoredFile | null> {
    // Looked at before it is opened, so that nothing but a plain file is ever opened; the handle is checked again after.
    try {
      const entry = await lstat(file);
      if (!entry.isFile()) {
        log.error({ file: path.basename(file), directory: entry.isDirectory(), symlink: entry.isSymbolicLink(), fifo: entry.isFIFO() }, "media store: refused an entry that is not a plain file");
        return null;
      }
    } catch (err) {
      if ((err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code !== "ENOENT") log.warn({ file: path.basename(file), code: (err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code }, "media store: a file could not be inspected");
      return null;
    }
    let handle: FileHandle;
    try {
      handle = await open(file, READ_FLAGS);
    } catch (err) {
      if ((err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code !== "ENOENT") log.warn({ file: path.basename(file), code: (err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code }, "media store: a file could not be opened");
      return null;
    }
    try {
      const stats = await handle.stat();
      if (stats.isFile() && stats.dev === (await device()) && stats.size <= maxBytes) return { handle, size: stats.size };
      log.error({ file: path.basename(file), regular: stats.isFile(), size: stats.size }, "media store: refused a file that is not a plain file of the store");
    } catch (err) {
      log.error({ err }, "media store: could not inspect an open file");
    }
    await handle.close();
    return null;
  }

  async function readStored(file: string, maxBytes: number): Promise<string | null> {
    const stored = await openStored(file, maxBytes);
    if (!stored) return null;
    try {
      return await stored.handle.readFile("utf8");
    } finally {
      await stored.handle.close();
    }

  async function receiveInto(

  /** Writes a small file under tmp/, flushed, then renames it into place: the reader never sees half of it. */
  async function writeRenamed(temp: string, target: string, text: string): Promise<void> {

      await handle.sync();

      await handle.close();

    await rename(temp, target);

  return {
    uploads,
    store,

    /** Creates the uploads volume's directories and forgets bodies a crash left half received. */
    async prepare(): Promise<void> {
      await rm(uploads.tmp, { recursive: true, force: true });
      for (const dir of [uploads.tmp, uploads.incoming, uploads.deletions, uploads.owed]) await mkdir(dir, { recursive: true });
    },

    /**
     * Streams a request body to tmp/<id>.part. `accept` sees the first bytes before anything is
     * written and throws to refuse them. Bytes are counted here while they arrive, because a
     * declared length can be absent or wrong; one byte over `maxBytes` ends the upload.
     */
    async receive(id: string, body: ReadableStream<Uint8Array> | null, maxBytes: number, accept: (head: Uint8Array) => void): Promise<number> {
      return (await receiveInto(id, body, maxBytes, accept, "none")).bytes;
    },

    /**
     * 3d Task 7 (design, sections 2 row 33 and 7.8 step 1): receive, and while it writes, every chunk is fed to three
     * hashers of node:crypto, SHA-256, SHA-1 and MD5, whose digests it answers with the byte count. The hashes are of the
     * file as received, before anything else touches it: the store keeps only korbat's own re-encoded sizes, which no list
     * knows. Only called while the comparison is on; with MEDIA_MATCH=off nothing is hashed.
     */
    async receiveHashed(id: string, body: ReadableStream<Uint8Array> | null, maxBytes: number, accept: (head: Uint8Array) => void): Promise<{ bytes: number; hashes: ReceivedHashes }> {
      const received = await receiveInto(id, body, maxBytes, accept, "all");
      return { bytes: received.bytes, hashes: threeHashes(received.digests) };
    },

    /**
     * 2d Task 3 (design, sections 7.2 and 7.7): an avatar's upload, received as any upload, with its SHA-256 always, in
     * lowercase hex, which its row keeps so that a picture a moderator reset is known again; and the three hashes of the
     * comparison only while it is on (`matching`), of which the SHA-256 is the same digest.
     */
    async receiveAvatar(id: string, body: ReadableStream<Uint8Array> | null, maxBytes: number, accept: (head: Uint8Array) => void, matching: boolean): Promise<{ bytes: number; sha256: string; hashes: ReceivedHashes | null }> {
      const received = await receiveInto(id, body, maxBytes, accept, matching ? "all" : "sha256");
      return { bytes: received.bytes, sha256: received.digests[0]!.toString("hex"), hashes: matching ? threeHashes(received.digests) : null };
    },

    /**
     * 3b Task 5 (design, sections 7.4 and 8.1): receive, with the bytes read from an image of import-work that the imports
     * module opened through openWorkFile: the same sniff, the same cap counted as the bytes arrive, and the three hashes
     * while the comparison is on, into the same tmp/<id>.part, and nothing but that descriptor is read. The caller keeps
     * the handle and closes it. A part a crash left under the same id is the caller's to discard first ("wx" refuses one).
     */
    async receiveWorkFile(id: string, file: { handle: FileHandle; size: number }, maxBytes: number, accept: (head: Uint8Array) => void, hash: boolean): Promise<{ bytes: number; hashes: ReceivedHashes | null }> {
      const body = Readable.toWeb(file.handle.createReadStream({ start: 0, autoClose: false })) as ReadableStream<Uint8Array>;
      const received = await receiveInto(id, body, maxBytes, accept, hash ? "all" : "none");
      return { bytes: received.bytes, hashes: hash ? threeHashes(received.digests) : null };
    },

    /** 3b Task 5: removes tmp/<id>.part alone, never a complete upload in incoming/, which may be in the worker's hands. */
    discardPart: (id: string): Promise<void> => rm(uploads.part(id), { force: true }),

    /**
     * 3b Task 5 (design, section 7.4 step 1): the uploads in incoming/ that have no result in the store yet, the ones the
     * worker has still to take or is taking; and whether one id has a result.
     */
    async waitingUploads(): Promise<string[]> {
      const waiting: string[] = [];
      for (const id of (await namesIn(uploads.incoming)).filter(isMediaId)) {
        if (!(await lstat(store.result(id)).then(() => true, () => false))) waiting.push(id);
      }
      return waiting;
    },
    hasResult: (id: string): Promise<boolean> => lstat(store.result(id)).then(() => true, () => false),

    /**
     * The upload becomes visible to the worker. A rename inside one volume is atomic. 2d Task 3 (design, section 7.2): for
     * an avatar, its job file (AvatarJob, one line of JSON) is written first, through tmp/ and a rename, so the worker never
     * sees an avatar's upload without its crop; a crash between the two leaves the job file alone, which the reconcile
     * pass removes (storedUploads lists it).
     */
    async commit(id: string, job?: { avatar: AvatarCrop }): Promise<void> {
      if (job !== undefined) {
        const line: AvatarJob = { v: 1, crop: job.avatar };
        await writeRenamed(path.join(uploads.tmp, `${id}.avatar`), uploads.avatarJob(id), `${JSON.stringify(line)}${String.fromCharCode(10)}`);
      }
      await rename(uploads.part(id), uploads.upload(id));
    },

    /**
     * Removes an upload, complete or not. A file the worker still holds open on Windows is left for the sweeper. 2d Task 3:
     * and an avatar's job file beside it.
     */
    async discardUpload(id: string): Promise<void> {
      for (const file of [uploads.part(id), uploads.upload(id), uploads.avatarJob(id)]) {
        await rm(file, { force: true }).catch((err: unknown) => log.warn({ id, code: (err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code }, "media uploads: an upload could not be removed yet"));
      }
    },

    /** The worker's verdict on an upload, or null while there is none. A result that does not parse is ignored and logged. */
    async readResult(id: string): Promise<ResultFile | null> {
      const text = await readStored(store.result(id), MAX_RESULT_BYTES);
      if (text === null) return null;
      try {
        const parsed = ResultFile.safeParse(JSON.parse(text));
        if (parsed.success && parsed.data.id === id) return parsed.data;
      } catch {
        // falls through to the log line below
      }
      log.error({ id }, "media store: ignored a result file that does not follow the protocol");
      return null;
    },

    /** An image file to stream. The caller closes the handle. */
    openImage: (id: string, size: MediaSize): Promise<StoredFile | null> => openStored(store.image(id, size), MAX_VARIANT_BYTES),

    /** Asks the worker to delete images. The request is an empty file named after the id. */
    async requestDeletion(ids: readonly string[]): Promise<void> {
      for (const id of ids) await (await open(uploads.deletion(id), "w")).close();
    },

    /**
     * Notes that a request to delete these images is owed: an empty file named after each id, in a directory the worker
     * never reads. Whoever deletes image rows in a transaction writes this inside it, before the commit, and writes the
     * request itself only after the commit: a transaction that does not commit has then asked the worker for nothing
     * (its rows are back, and a report may freeze them the next moment), and a commit whose request is lost or cannot
     * be written leaves the note, from which the request is written later. Where the note cannot be written this throws,
     * the caller's transaction fails with it, and no row goes whose files could not be found again.
     */
    async oweDeletion(ids: readonly string[]): Promise<void> {
      for (const id of ids) await (await open(uploads.owedDeletion(id), "w")).close();
    },

    /** The deletions that are owed, each with the age of its note. */
    async owedDeletions(now: number): Promise<{ id: string; ageMs: number }[]> {
      const found: { id: string; ageMs: number }[] = [];
      for (const id of (await namesIn(uploads.owed)).filter(isMediaId)) {
        const stats = await stat(uploads.owedDeletion(id)).catch(() => null);
        if (stats) found.push({ id, ageMs: now - stats.mtimeMs });
      }
      return found;
    },

    /** Removes the notes of these ids: their request stands, or their rows turned out to be kept. */
    async settleOwed(ids: readonly string[]): Promise<void> {
      for (const id of ids) await rm(uploads.owedDeletion(id), { force: true });
    },

    /** Ids with a deletion request. */
    async deletionRequests(): Promise<string[]> {
      return (await namesIn(uploads.deletions)).filter(isMediaId);
    },

    /** Deletion requests with their age, for the sweeper, which only withdraws one after a grace period. */
    async deletionRequestAges(now: number): Promise<{ id: string; ageMs: number }[]> {
      const found: { id: string; ageMs: number }[] = [];
      for (const id of (await namesIn(uploads.deletions)).filter(isMediaId)) {
        const stats = await stat(uploads.deletion(id)).catch(() => null);
        if (stats) found.push({ id, ageMs: now - stats.mtimeMs });
      }
      return found;
    },

    withdrawDeletion: (id: string): Promise<void> => rm(uploads.deletion(id), { force: true }),

    /**
     * 3d (design, section 7.1): whether both stored sizes of the image are in the store. A visible image whose files are
     * not, after its seal was lifted, is in the quarantine waiting to return, or lost; only then is the database asked.
     */
    async imageFilesPresent(id: string): Promise<boolean> {
      for (const size of MEDIA_SIZES) {
        const found = await lstat(store.image(id, size)).catch(() => null);
        if (!found?.isFile()) return false;
      }
      return true;
    },

    /** Whether the worker still holds anything for this id. */
    async imageRemains(id: string): Promise<boolean> {
      for (const target of [store.imageDir(id), store.result(id)]) {
        if (await stat(target).then(() => true, () => false)) return true;
      }
      return false;
    },

    /** Every image folder in the store with its age, for the reconcile pass. */
    async storedImages(now: number): Promise<{ id: string; ageMs: number }[]> {
      const found: { id: string; ageMs: number }[] = [];
      for (const shard of await namesIn(store.files)) {
        if (!/^[0-9a-f]{2}$/.test(shard)) continue;
        for (const id of await namesIn(path.join(store.files, shard))) {
          if (!isMediaId(id) || !id.startsWith(shard)) continue;
          const stats = await stat(store.imageDir(id)).catch(() => null);
          if (stats) found.push({ id, ageMs: now - stats.mtimeMs });
        }
      }
      return found;
    },

    /** Every upload on disk, complete or partial, with its age, for the reconcile pass. */
    async storedUploads(now: number): Promise<{ id: string; ageMs: number }[]> {
      const found: { id: string; ageMs: number }[] = [];
      const add = async (id: string, file: string) => {
        if (!isMediaId(id)) return;
        const stats = await stat(file).catch(() => null);
        if (stats) found.push({ id, ageMs: now - stats.mtimeMs });
      };
      // 2d Task 3 (design, section 7.2): an avatar's job file is listed under its upload's id, so that one left alone by a
      // crash between its write and the upload's rename is removed with the upload's other files.
      for (const name of await namesIn(uploads.incoming)) await add(name.endsWith(".avatar") ? name.slice(0, -".avatar".length) : name, path.join(uploads.incoming, name));
      for (const name of await namesIn(uploads.tmp)) if (name.endsWith(".part")) await add(name.slice(0, -".part".length), path.join(uploads.tmp, name));
      return found;
    },

    /** Milliseconds since the worker's last heartbeat, or null when there is none to read. */
    async heartbeatAge(now: number): Promise<number | null> {
      const text = await readStored(store.heartbeat, 1024);
      if (text === null) return null;
      try {
        const beat = Heartbeat.safeParse(JSON.parse(text));
        return beat.success ? now - beat.data.at : null;
      } catch {
        return null;
      }
    },

    /** Free space on the volume with less of it. The volumes share a disk with Postgres, so running out would stop the database. */
    async freeBytes(): Promise<number> {
      const sizes = await Promise.all([uploads.root, store.root].map(async (dir) => {
        const fs = await statfs(dir);
        return fs.bavail * fs.bsize;
      }));
      return Math.min(...sizes);
    },
  };
}

export type MediaFiles = ReturnType<typeof createMediaFiles>;
```

```ts
import { EDGE_CACHE, type MediaSize } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { MediaDeps } from "../context";
import type { StoredFile } from "../files";

/**
 * Visible images of visible posts are cacheable by anyone, on the 200 and on the 304 (3d design, section 2 row 12 and
 * 7.4): a browser keeps a copy at most EDGE_CACHE.browserSeconds and an edge at most EDGE_CACHE.edgeSeconds, both
 * revalidate once it is stale, and an edge serves no stale copy when the API errs, so a hidden image's copy is bounded
 * by these two numbers even without an accepted purge. Everything else depends on who asks and is never cached: an
 * author's own hidden image is PRIVATE_CACHE, and every other answer of the API is no-store (security-headers.ts).
 */
export const PUBLIC_CACHE = `public, max-age=${EDGE_CACHE.browserSeconds}, s-maxage=${EDGE_CACHE.edgeSeconds}, must-revalidate, stale-if-error=0`;
export const PRIVATE_CACHE = "private, no-store";

export type Served =
  | { kind: "file"; file: StoredFile; cacheControl: string; etag: string }
  | { kind: "not_modified"; cacheControl: string; etag: string }
  | { kind: "not_found" };

export interface ServeRequest {
  id: string;
  size: MediaSize;
  ifNoneMatch: string | undefined;
  /** Resolves the session. Only called when the answer depends on who asks, so public images cost one query. */
  viewer: () => Promise<string | null>;
}

/** The states in which a post or an image is still shown to someone: to everyone, or to its author alone. */
const isShown = (state: string): state is "visible" | "withheld" | "removed" => state === "visible" || state === "withheld" || state === "removed";

/**
 * Decides whether an image file may be sent. An image follows its post and its own moderation state
 * (3c design, section 7.10). When both are `visible` it is public, as 2a made it, so blocks are not
 * checked here. When either is `withheld` or `removed` it goes to its author only and is never cached.
 * Everything else is not found for everyone: an image without a post or not ready; a sealed image; an
 * image of a deleted post, whose row a case or a freeze may have kept; an image whose content, or whose
 * post's, was erased; and any state this reader has not been taught. Those are tested before the
 * author's branch, so a sealed image of a withheld or removed post is not found for its author too.
 */
export async function serve(deps: MediaDeps, request: ServeRequest): Promise<Served> {
  const access = await deps.repo.fileAccess(request.id);
  if (!access || access.status !== "ready") return { kind: "not_found" };

  let cacheControl = PUBLIC_CACHE;
  if (access.kind === "avatar") {
    // 2d Task 3 (design, sections 7.5 and 7.8; decision 29): an avatar is served, to anyone and under the public header,
    // exactly while it is a live profile's picture, visible and not erased; every other avatar row (an upload not set yet,
    // a replaced or removed one, one a hold keeps, one of a deleted account, a sealed one) is not found for everyone, its
    // owner included. The viewer is never asked. Task 4 adds the owner's own picture while R1's review withholds it.
    if (access.profileId === null || access.profileDeleted || access.mediaState !== "visible" || access.erased) return { kind: "not_found" };
  } else {
    if (!access.postState) return { kind: "not_found" };
    if (access.erased || !isShown(access.mediaState) || !isShown(access.postState)) return { kind: "not_found" };
    if (access.postState !== "visible" || access.mediaState !== "visible") {
      if ((await request.viewer()) !== access.authorId) return { kind: "not_found" };
      cacheControl = PRIVATE_CACHE;
    }
  }

  // The files of an id never change, so the id and the size identify the bytes.
  const etag = `"${request.id}-${request.size}"`;
  if (request.ifNoneMatch?.split(",").some((candidate) => candidate.trim() === etag)) return { kind: "not_modified", cacheControl, etag };

  const file = await deps.files.openImage(request.id, request.size);
  if (!file) {
    // 3d (design, sections 6.1 and 7.1): a visible image whose seal was lifted has its files in the quarantine until they
    // are returned, or korbat recorded them as lost: the same 404, and an info line, since nothing is broken. Only an
    // image that is neither has lost its file unexpectedly.
    const custody = access.mediaState === "visible" ? await deps.repo.custody(request.id) : { quarantined: false, lost: false };
    if (custody.quarantined || custody.lost) {
      deps.log.info({ id: request.id, size: request.size, custody: custody.lost ? "lost" : "quarantine" }, "media: a visible image's files are not in the store: being restored, or lost");
    } else {
      deps.log.error({ id: request.id, size: request.size }, "media: a ready image has no usable file in the store");
    }
    return { kind: "not_found" };
  }
  return { kind: "file", file, cacheControl, etag };
}
```
