import { MediaFailure, type MediaStatusResponse } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { MediaError, type MediaDeps } from "../context";
import { askSource, storeVerdict, tellMatched } from "../match";
import type { MediaRow } from "../repo";

/**
 * Records the worker's verdict for an upload, if there is one, and removes the upload file, which
 * is how the worker learns that its result was read. Safe to repeat: only a row that is still
 * processing changes.
 *
 * 3d Task 7 (design, section 7.8 step 3): while the comparison with known material is on and the upload has hashes, a ready
 * verdict is stored only with its check: the source is asked once, bounded in time, and its answer is written in the
 * verdict's transaction (clear, unchecked, or matched with its record and, for an acting match, its refusal and hold). So
 * an image is ready only once its check was answered or timed out, and an upload with an acting match is never ready
 * without its refusal. Over the limit on refusals an hour the row stays processing with its check capped and its upload
 * file and result kept, for match-retry to ask again. After the commit the moderation module is told what was stored.
 */
export async function finalize(deps: MediaDeps, id: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const result = await deps.files.readResult(id);
  if (!result) return false;
  // 3d Task 6: a ready result of version 2 may carry the scorer's model and score. The score is kept only from this
  // server's own model; another model's is dropped, with the image, which is ready all the same, left unscored. The score
  // itself is never logged. 2d Task 3: version 3 carries them as version 2 does, and its avatar mark, which both writers of
  // the verdict (repo.finalize and storeVerdict) hold against the row's kind.
  const r1 = (result.v === 2 || result.v === 3) && result.status === "ready" ? result.r1 : undefined;
  if (r1 !== undefined && r1.model !== deps.r1Model) deps.log.error({ id, model: r1.model }, "media store: dropped a score from a model this server does not run");
  const score = r1 !== undefined && r1.model === deps.r1Model ? r1.score : null;
  // 3d review L3: a ready result without a score while this server's check is on: the worker does not score (it was left
  // behind, or set otherwise). The image is ready, unscored, and the operator is told here and by automation-status.
  if (deps.r1Model !== null && result.status === "ready" && r1 === undefined) deps.log.warn({ id }, "media store: a ready result carries no score while the R1 check is on; the worker does not score");
  const hashed = deps.match.mode !== "off" && result.status === "ready" ? await deps.matches.hashed(deps.matches.db, id) : null;
  if (hashed !== null && hashed.status === "processing") {
    const answer = await askSource(deps, hashed);
    const stored = await storeVerdict(deps, id, result, score, hashed, answer);
    // A capped upload keeps its upload file, so the worker keeps its result for the next question.
    if (stored.stored !== "capped") await deps.files.discardUpload(id);
    await tellMatched(deps, stored.events);
    return true;
  }
  await deps.repo.finalize(id, result, score);
  await deps.files.discardUpload(id);
  return true;
}

function statusOf(row: MediaRow): MediaStatusResponse {
  if (row.status === "ready" && row.width !== null && row.height !== null) {
    // A sealed image is shown to nobody, its owner included: its status says that it is ready and how large it is, never
    // the blurhash, which is made from the image and which the repository did not hand over.
    if (row.moderationState === "sealed") return { id: row.id, status: "ready", width: row.width, height: row.height };
    if (row.blurhash !== null) return { id: row.id, status: "ready", width: row.width, height: row.height, blurhash: row.blurhash };
  }
  if (row.status === "failed") {
    const reason = MediaFailure.safeParse(row.error);
    return { id: row.id, status: "failed", error: reason.success ? reason.data : "processing_failed" };
  }
  return { id: row.id, status: "processing" };
}

/**
 * The state of one upload, for its owner only. Whoever asks first finalizes it. 3d (design, sections 7.1 and 9.6): a
 * ready image on a post whose state is visible and whose files are not in the store says `lost` when korbat recorded
 * them as lost, and `restoring` while they wait in the quarantine to be returned; the app asks this after a failed load
 * of the viewer's own image. Only then is the store looked at and the database asked.
 *
 * 3d Task 7 (design, sections 7.8 step 5 and 10.2): an upload korbat refused answers `refused` with the refusal's id and
 * nothing else, no blurhash and no size, also once its row is gone; one whose check is capped answers processing and is
 * left to match-retry, so a composer's polling never asks the source again.
 */
export async function status(deps: MediaDeps, ownerId: string, id: string): Promise<MediaStatusResponse> {
  const refusalId = await deps.matches.refusalOfImage(id, ownerId);
  if (refusalId !== null) return { id, status: "refused", refusalId };
  let row = await deps.repo.find(id);
  if (!row || row.ownerId !== ownerId) throw new MediaError("not_found", 404);
  if (row.status === "processing" && !(await deps.matches.capped([id])).has(id) && (await finalize(deps, id))) {
    const refused = await deps.matches.refusalOfImage(id, ownerId);
    if (refused !== null) return { id, status: "refused", refusalId: refused };
    row = (await deps.repo.find(id)) ?? row;
  }
  const answer = statusOf(row);
  if (answer.status === "ready" && row.moderationState === "visible" && row.postId !== null && !(await deps.files.imageFilesPresent(id))) {
    const custody = await deps.repo.custody(id);
    if (custody.lost) return { ...answer, lost: true };
    if (custody.quarantined) return { ...answer, restoring: true };
  }
  return answer;
}

import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import type { FileHandle } from "node:fs/promises";
import { MEDIA_ACCEPTED_TYPES, MEDIA_MAX_BYTES, type AvatarCrop, type MediaAcceptedType, type UploadResponse } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { DbTx } from "@korbat/db";
import { sniffImage, type MediaFormat } from "@korbat/media-protocol";
import { HEIC_MESSAGE, MAX_PENDING_UPLOADS, MediaError, type MediaDeps } from "../context";
import type { ReceivedHashes } from "../files";
import { ImportMovedOn } from "../repo";

const FORMAT_OF: Record<MediaAcceptedType, MediaFormat> = {
  "image/jpeg": "jpeg",
  "image/png": "png",
  "image/webp": "webp",
  "image/avif": "avif",
  "image/gif": "gif",
};

export interface UploadRequest {
  contentType: string | undefined;
  contentLength: string | undefined;
  body: ReadableStream<Uint8Array> | null;
  /** 2d Task 3 (design, section 7.2): an avatar's upload, from the query's kind=avatar and its crop; absent for a post's. */
  avatar?: { crop: AvatarCrop };
}

/** `image/jpeg; charset=binary` to `image/jpeg`. */
const mediaType = (header: string | undefined): string => (header ?? "").split(";")[0]!.trim().toLowerCase();

/** The declared type is checked and then forgotten: nothing of it is stored, and the bytes decide what the file is. */
function checkDeclaredType(deps: MediaDeps, header: string | undefined): void {
  const type = mediaType(header);
  if (type === "image/heic" || type === "image/heif") throw new MediaError("unsupported_media_type", 415, HEIC_MESSAGE);
  const format = (MEDIA_ACCEPTED_TYPES as readonly string[]).includes(type) ? FORMAT_OF[type as MediaAcceptedType] : null;
  if (!format || !deps.formats.includes(format)) throw new MediaError("unsupported_media_type", 415);
}

/** Runs on the first bytes, before anything is written to disk. 3b Task 5: an imported image's too. */
export function checkFirstBytes(deps: MediaDeps, head: Uint8Array): void {
  const sniffed = sniffImage(head);
  if (sniffed.kind === "heic") throw new MediaError("unsupported_media_type", 415, HEIC_MESSAGE);
  if (sniffed.kind === "animated") throw new MediaError("unsupported_media_type", 415, "Animated images are not supported yet. Use a still image.");
  if (sniffed.kind !== "image" || !deps.formats.includes(sniffed.format)) throw new MediaError("unsupported_media_type", 415);
}

/**
 * Takes one image from its owner and hands it to the worker. Cheap refusals come first; the body
 * is only read once the account may upload. The row is written before the file becomes visible to
 * the worker, so the worker never processes an upload nobody owns.
 */
export async function upload(deps: MediaDeps, ownerId: string, request: UploadRequest): Promise<UploadResponse> {
  checkDeclaredType(deps, request.contentType);
  const declaredLength = Number(request.contentLength);
  if (Number.isFinite(declaredLength) && declaredLength > MEDIA_MAX_BYTES) throw new MediaError("file_too_large", 413);

  const createdAt = await deps.repo.accountCreatedAt(ownerId);
  if (!createdAt) throw new MediaError("not_found", 404);
  await deps.enforceUploadLimit(ownerId, createdAt, deps.now());
  if ((await deps.repo.pendingCount(ownerId)) >= MAX_PENDING_UPLOADS) throw new MediaError("too_many_pending_uploads", 409);
  if ((await deps.files.freeBytes()) < deps.minFreeBytes) {
    deps.log.error({ minFreeBytes: deps.minFreeBytes }, "media: uploads refused, free space is under the floor");
    throw new MediaError("uploads_unavailable", 503);
  }

  const id = randomUUID();
  // 3d Task 7 (design, section 7.8 step 1): while the comparison with known material is on, the three hashes of the file
  // as received are taken while it streams, and stored with the image row in one transaction; while it is off, nothing is
  // hashed and no row of media_hashes is written. 2d Task 3 (7.2): an avatar's SHA-256 is taken always, one hash of at
  // most MEDIA_MAX_BYTES, and kept on its row as avatar_sha256.
  const accept = (head: Uint8Array) => checkFirstBytes(deps, head);
  const matching = deps.match.mode !== "off";
  let hashes: ReceivedHashes | undefined;
  let avatar: { sha256: string } | undefined;
  if (request.avatar !== undefined) {
    const received = await deps.files.receiveAvatar(id, request.body, MEDIA_MAX_BYTES, accept, matching);
    hashes = received.hashes ?? undefined;
    avatar = { sha256: received.sha256 };
  } else if (matching) {
    hashes = (await deps.files.receiveHashed(id, request.body, MEDIA_MAX_BYTES, accept)).hashes;
  } else {
    await deps.files.receive(id, request.body, MEDIA_MAX_BYTES, accept);
  }
  try {
    await deps.repo.insertProcessing({ id, ownerId, now: deps.now(), hashes, avatar });
    // An avatar's job file goes into incoming/ before the upload does (files.commit).
    await deps.files.commit(id, request.avatar === undefined ? undefined : { avatar: request.avatar.crop });
  } catch (err) {
    await deps.repo.deleteRow(id).catch(() => undefined);
    await deps.files.discardUpload(id);
    throw err;
  }
  return { id, status: "processing" };
}

/** 3b Task 5: what feeding one imported image came to (3b design, section 7.4 step 4). */
export type ImportedReceipt =
  /** The row is written and the file is in incoming/ for the worker; the import's cursor moved with the row. */
  | "fed"
  /** The first bytes are no still image of a format this site takes (the sniff of any upload), never retried. */
  | "unsupported"
  /** Over MEDIA_MAX_BYTES as its bytes arrived. */
  | "too_large"
  /** The import was no longer preparing at its cursor: nothing was written. */
  | "stopped"
  /** The owner's suspension runs, by the one predicate: nothing was written, and the import waits. */
  | "suspended"
  /** A row with this id exists already: the image was fed before (a plan that an earlier process built differently). */
  | "already";

/** Whether an error is the primary key of post_media refusing a second row of an id. */
function duplicateRow(err: unknown): boolean {
  let current: unknown = err;
  for (let depth = 0; depth < 5 && current; depth++) {
    const found = current as { code?: unknown; constraint_name?: unknown; constraint?: unknown };
    if (typeof current === "object" && found.code === "23505") return found.constraint_name === "post_media_pkey" || found.constraint === "post_media_pkey";
    current = (current as { cause?: unknown }).cause;
  }
  return false;
}

/**
 * 3b Task 5 (design, sections 7.4 step 4 and 8.1): one imported image enters through this module's own receive path, as an
 * upload of its owner's: the bytes come from a work file the imports module opened through openWorkFile (the importer's
 * output is hostile, so nothing else of import-work is read), the first bytes are sniffed as any upload's, the bytes are
 * counted against MEDIA_MAX_BYTES as they arrive and hashed while the comparison is on, the row is written by
 * insertProcessing with the import (its claim moves the import's cursor in the same transaction), and the file is
 * committed to incoming/ for the unchanged worker. Neither the upload limits, nor the pending count, nor the route's
 * declared type apply: no route of the person's sent it (decision 21).
 */
export async function receiveImported(
  deps: MediaDeps,
  input: { id: string; ownerId: string; file: { handle: FileHandle; size: number }; now: Date; importJob: { id: string; claim: (tx: DbTx) => Promise<boolean> } },
): Promise<ImportedReceipt> {
  if (input.file.size > MEDIA_MAX_BYTES) return "too_large";
  // A part a crash left under this derived id is discarded first: receive opens tmp/<id>.part with "wx". A complete upload
  // in incoming/ is never touched here: a row of the id may own it.
  await deps.files.discardPart(input.id);
  let hashes: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof deps.files.receiveWorkFile>>["hashes"];
  try {
    hashes = (await deps.files.receiveWorkFile(input.id, input.file, MEDIA_MAX_BYTES, (head) => checkFirstBytes(deps, head), deps.match.mode !== "off")).hashes;
  } catch (err) {
    if (err instanceof MediaError && err.code === "unsupported_media_type") return "unsupported";
    if (err instanceof MediaError && err.code === "file_too_large") return "too_large";
    throw err;
  }
  try {
    await deps.repo.insertProcessing({ id: input.id, ownerId: input.ownerId, now: input.now, hashes: hashes ?? undefined, importJob: input.importJob });
  } catch (err) {
    await deps.files.discardPart(input.id);
    if (err instanceof ImportMovedOn) return "stopped";
    if (err instanceof MediaError && err.code === "account_suspended") return "suspended";
    if (duplicateRow(err)) return "already";
    throw err;
  }
  // The row is committed with the cursor; a rename that fails leaves a row the worker never answers, which the import
  // settles as not checked after IMPORT_RULES.checkHours (the orchestrator's ruling), as it settles any unanswered one.
  await deps.files.commit(input.id).catch((err: unknown) => deps.log.error({ id: input.id, code: (err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code }, "media: an imported image could not be handed to the worker"));
  return "fed";
}

/** A post sealed for good whose image rows now are not as many as a seal of it recorded. */

  postId: string;

/**
 * 3d (design, sections 5, 6.1, 7.1 and 8.10): the quarantine's plan joined to the store's naming rule, for staff.js
 * quarantine-list, through the caller's transaction, which reads as the migrator: quarantine_plan() is executable by
 * nobody else, and the command line cannot build the module (F 5), nor may any file outside it name the image table.
 *
 * An image to move in names each of its files that is not in the quarantine already (a lost file counts as there: nothing
 * of it is left to move); an image to return, to destroy or for the operator names each of its files whose row has no end.
 * For every post sealed for good, its image rows now, erased or not, are compared with the count each of its seals
 * recorded (seal_posts.images): a post whose rows differ gets no line and is answered among `mismatched`, so the command
 * names it and still prints every other post's lines. A list that missed a row would leave a sealed file in the store.
 */
export async function quarantineNames(q: Db | DbTx): Promise<{ lines: QuarantineLine[]; mismatched: QuarantineMismatch[] }> {
  const repo = createMediaRepo(q as Db);
  const mismatched = (await repo.sealedForGoodCounts(q)).filter((post) => post.images.some((images) => images !== post.rows));
  const left = new Set(mismatched.map((post) => post.postId));
  const lines: QuarantineLine[] = [];
  for (const image of await repo.quarantinePlan(q)) {
    if (image.postId !== null && left.has(image.postId)) continue;
    const names = MEDIA_SIZES.map((size) => storedImageName(image.mediaId, size));
    const files = image.direction === "in" ? names.filter((name) => !image.kept.includes(name)) : names.filter((name) => image.open.includes(name));
    if (files.length > 0) lines.push({ direction: image.direction as QuarantineDirection, mediaId: image.mediaId, postId: image.postId, files });
  }
  return { lines, mismatched };

             where h.check_state = 'unchecked' and m.created_at > now() - make_interval(hours => r.match_retry_hours)) as unchecked,
           (select to_char(min(m.created_at) at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.MS"Z"') from public.media_hashes h join public.post_media m on m.id = h.media_id
             where h.check_state = 'unchecked' and m.created_at > now() - make_interval(hours => r.match_retry_hours)) as oldest,

  return { unchecked: row!.unchecked, oldestUnchecked: row!.oldest, refusalsHour: row!.refusals_hour };

  requestDeletion(ids: readonly string[]): Promise<void>;

  exportAvatar(ownerId: string): Promise<{ id: string; width: number; height: number } | null>;

 * files only when its row went: an upload still in incoming/ is removed first, as the sweeper removes one it gives up on.
 */
export function mediaForPosts(deps: MediaDeps): MediaForPosts {
  return {
    attach: (tx, input) => deps.repo.attach(tx, input),
    detachAll: (tx, postId) => deps.repo.detachAll(tx, postId),
    requestDeletion: (ids) => deps.files.requestDeletion(ids),
    forPosts: (postIds) => deps.repo.forPosts(postIds),
    attachAvatar: (tx, accountId, mediaId) => deps.repo.attachAvatar(tx, accountId, mediaId),
    detachAvatar: (tx, accountId) => deps.repo.detachAvatar(tx, accountId),
    async dropFormerAvatar(id) {
      if (id === null || !(await deps.repo.deleteFormerAvatar(id))) return;
      await deps.files.discardUpload(id);
      await deps.files.requestDeletion([id]);
    },
    avatarsOf: (profileIds, viewer) => deps.repo.avatarsOf(profileIds, viewer),
  };
}

/** The account module's interface over this module's dependencies, as createMedia hands it out; the integration tests build it the same way. */
export function mediaForAccount(deps: MediaDeps): MediaForAccount {
  return {
    exportAvatar: (ownerId) => deps.repo.exportAvatar(ownerId),
    async purgeOwner(tx, ownerId) {
      const ids = await deps.repo.purgeOwner(tx, ownerId);
      await deps.files.oweDeletion(ids);
      return ids;
    },
    async requestDeletion(ids) {
      for (const id of ids) await deps.files.discardUpload(id);
      await deps.files.requestDeletion(ids);
      await deps.files.settleOwed(ids);
    },
    exportImages: async (ownerId) =>
      (await deps.repo.readyImages(ownerId)).map((id) => ({
        id,
        // The row is read again, with the list's own condition, right before the file is opened.
        open: async () => ((await deps.repo.isExportable(ownerId, id)) ? deps.files.openImage(id, "large") : null),
      })),
  };
}

/**
 * What the imports module needs from this one (3b design, sections 6.5, 7.4, 8.1 and 8.2): the feeder's three conditions,
 * one image's way in through this module's own receive path, the settling of the import's images, the deletion of its
 * rows on no post and of their files, and the refusal its view links to. The imports module names neither post_media,
 * media_hashes, upload_refusals nor the request to delete a file: it reaches each through here.
 */
export interface MediaForImports {
  /** The comparison with known material is on (MEDIA_MATCH): images are imported only then (decision 15). */
  readonly matching: boolean;
  /** An upload that is no imported image's waits in incoming/ for the worker (7.4 step 1): a person's own goes first. */
  ownUploadWaiting(): Promise<boolean>;
  /** The imported images on the site that are processing without a result yet (7.4 step 2). */
  importedInFlight(): Promise<number>;
  /** Whether the volumes have the free space any upload needs (MEDIA_MIN_FREE_BYTES). */
  hasRoom(): Promise<boolean>;
  /** One image of the import in, from its work file (receiveImported). The caller closes the file's handle. */
  receive(input: Parameters<typeof receiveImported>[1]): Promise<ImportedReceipt>;
  /**
   * The import's rows on no post after its images still processing were finalized here (the sweeper's own step, so a
   * verdict the worker wrote is read within the round, with the check of known material and a refusal's notice).
   */
  settleRows(jobId: string): Promise<ImportImageRow[]>;
  /**
   * The import's rows on no post as they stand, finalizing nothing: Task 6's attach takes the kept ones (status ready,
   * check clear) for the posts of their lines.
   */
  importRows(jobId: string): Promise<ImportImageRow[]>;
  /**
   * Deletes the import's rows on no post, or these of them, in the caller's transaction (the keep trigger leaves a held
   * one), and notes there that their files are owed a request, as the account's purge does; answers the ids that went.
   */
  deleteImportLeftovers(tx: DbTx, jobId: string, ids?: readonly string[]): Promise<string[]>;
  /** After that transaction's commit: their uploads removed, their files' deletion asked of the worker, the notes settled. */
  releaseFiles(ids: readonly string[]): Promise<void>;
  /** The imports that still have rows on no post that no hold keeps. */
  importsWithLeftovers(): Promise<string[]>;
  /** The refusal of one of the import's images, the earliest; null when none. */
  refusalOf(jobId: string): Promise<string | null>;
}

/** The imports module's interface over this module's dependencies, as createMedia hands it out; the integration tests build it the same way. */
export function mediaForImports(deps: MediaDeps): MediaForImports {
  return {
    matching: deps.match.mode !== "off",
    async ownUploadWaiting() {
      const waiting = await deps.files.waitingUploads();
      const imported = await deps.repo.importedAmong(waiting);
      return waiting.some((id) => !imported.has(id));
    },
    async importedInFlight() {
      let count = 0;
      for (const id of await deps.repo.importedProcessing()) if (!(await deps.files.hasResult(id))) count++;
      return count;
    },
    hasRoom: async () => (await deps.files.freeBytes()) >= deps.minFreeBytes,
    receive: (input) => receiveImported(deps, input),
    async settleRows(jobId) {
      const before = await deps.repo.importRows(jobId);
      const capped = await deps.matches.capped(before.filter((row) => row.status === "processing").map((row) => row.id));
      // A capped upload waits for match-retry, which asks the source again; finalizing it here would ask every round.
      for (const row of before) if (row.status === "processing" && !capped.has(row.id)) await finalize(deps, row.id);
      return deps.repo.importRows(jobId);
    },
    importRows: (jobId) => deps.repo.importRows(jobId),
    async deleteImportLeftovers(tx, jobId, ids) {
      const gone = await deps.repo.deleteImportLeftovers(tx, jobId, ids);
      await deps.files.oweDeletion(gone);
      return gone;
    },
    async releaseFiles(ids) {
      for (const id of ids) await deps.files.discardUpload(id);
      await deps.files.requestDeletion(ids);
      await deps.files.settleOwed(ids);
    },
    importsWithLeftovers: () => deps.repo.importsWithLeftovers(),
    refusalOf: (jobId) => deps.repo.importRefusal(jobId),
  };
}

export interface CreateMediaOptions {
  /** The korbat_api pool. The module never sees the auth pool. */
  apiDb: Db;
  /** The uploads volume, which the API writes, and the store volume, which it only reads. */
  uploadsDir: string;
  storeDir: string;
  formats: readonly MediaFormat[];
  minFreeBytes: number;
  /** See MEDIA_RECONCILE; defaults to `on`. */
  reconcile?: "on" | "off" | "force";
  logger: Logger;
  /** The auth module's requireSession: an onboarded account with CSRF and Origin checked. */
  requireSession: MiddlewareHandler<AppEnv>;
  /** The auth module's resolveSession. The file routes run it themselves, and only when they must. */
  resolveSession: MiddlewareHandler<AppEnv>;
  /** Image requests have their own per-IP bucket in the store the other limits use. */
  rateLimitStore: RateLimitStore;
  /** Built from the social module's write limits, so every per-account limit lives in one table. */
  enforceUploadLimit: MediaDeps["enforceUploadLimit"];
  now?: () => Date;
  /** 3d Task 3: the edge's purge adapter, built from EDGE_PURGE; off when none is given. */
  edge?: EdgeAdapter;
  /** 3d Task 6: the scorer's model whose scores finalize keeps (the test scorer's under R1_CLASSIFIER=test); none when absent. */
  r1Model?: string | null;
  /** 3d Task 7: the comparison with known material, built from MEDIA_MATCH; off when none is given. */
  match?: MatchAdapter;
}

export function createMedia(options: CreateMediaOptions) {
  const deps: MediaDeps = {
    repo: createMediaRepo(options.apiDb),
    files: createMediaFiles({ uploadsDir: options.uploadsDir, storeDir: options.storeDir, log: options.logger }),
    formats: options.formats,
    minFreeBytes: options.minFreeBytes,
    reconcileMode: options.reconcile ?? "on",
    enforceUploadLimit: options.enforceUploadLimit,
    log: options.logger,
    now: options.now ?? (() => new Date()),
    r1Model: options.r1Model ?? null,
    match: options.match ?? matchAdapterFrom({ MEDIA_MATCH: "off", APP_SITE: "open" }),
    matches: createMatchRepo(options.apiDb),
    matched: { handler: null },
  };
  const forPosts = mediaForPosts(deps);
  const forAccount = mediaForAccount(deps);
  const forCases = mediaForCases(deps);
  const forImports = mediaForImports(deps);
  const edge = options.edge ?? edgeAdapterFrom({ EDGE_PURGE: "off", APP_SITE: "open" });
  return {
    deps,
    /** The interface the social module uses to put images on posts and read them back. */
    forPosts,
    /** The interface the account module uses. */
    forAccount,
    /** The interface the moderation module uses: an intake's holds, what a case reaches, the staff's image, the disposal. */
    forCases,
    /** 3b Task 5: the interface the imports module uses. */
    forImports,
    /** Creates the uploads volume's directories. Call once before serving. */
    prepare: () => deps.files.prepare(),
    routes: mediaRoutes(deps, options.requireSession),
    /** Mounted before the global rate limit and session resolution. */
    fileRoutes: mediaFileRoutes(deps, { resolveSession: options.resolveSession, rateLimitStore: options.rateLimitStore }),
    /** One pass of housekeeping at the given time. The server runs it on a timer; tests call it directly. */
    sweep: (now: Date, options: { reconcile: boolean }) => sweep(deps, now, options),
    /** Starts sweeping every thirty seconds under the shared job lock, and returns the function that stops it. */
    startSweeper: (lock: JobLock) => createSweeper(deps, lock).start(),
    /**
     * 3d Task 3 (design, sections 7.4 and 7.14): starts the edge's job, edge-purge, under the shared job lock, a round
     * fifteen seconds after the last ended, and returns the function that stops it. With the adapter off it closes every
     * outbox row as off.
     */
    startEdge: (lock: JobLock) => createEdgeJob({ repo: deps.repo, adapter: edge, log: deps.log }, lock).start(),
    /**
     * 3d Task 7 (design, sections 5 and 7.8): hands the module the moderation module's handler of a stored refusal or of a
     * match on a posted image (moderation.matched), once that module is built, which is after this one.
     */
    onMatch: (handler: NonNullable<MediaDeps["matched"]["handler"]>) => {
      deps.matched.handler = handler;
    },
    /** 3d Task 7 (7.8 step 6, 7.14): one round of match-retry now; the server runs it on a timer. */
    matchRetry: () => matchRetryRound(deps, finalize),
    /**
     * 3d Task 7: starts match-retry under the shared job lock, a round a minute after the last ended, and returns the
     * function that stops it. With the comparison off a round reads nothing.
     */
    startMatchRetry: (lock: JobLock) => createMatchRetryJob(deps, finalize, lock).start(),
    /** An advisory health check: the worker's heartbeat is fresh and the volumes have room. */
    async healthCheck(): Promise<void> {
      const age = await deps.files.heartbeatAge(deps.now().getTime());
      if (age === null || age > HEARTBEAT_STALE_MS) throw new Error("the image worker's heartbeat is missing or stale");
      if ((await deps.files.freeBytes()) < deps.minFreeBytes) throw new Error("free space on the media volumes is under the floor");
    },
  };
}

export type Media = ReturnType<typeof createMedia>;

 * source once, bounded in time, and storing its answer with the worker's verdict; the record of a match, and for an acting
 * match on an upload that is on no post its refusal and hold, which the database forces; and the job match-retry, which

 * upload_refusals_hold holds the image and the uploader's address. After the commit the moderation module is told through
 * media.onMatch: a refusal, for the uploader's notice and the urgent alert; a match on a posted image, for the automated
 * step; an upload over the limit, for matcher_down at once.

export const MATCH_RETRY_JOB = "match-retry";
export const MATCH_RETRY_INTERVAL_MS = 60_000;

/** The message of an exception a trigger or a function raised as its code (SQLSTATE P0001); null for anything else. */
function raised(err: unknown): string | null {
  let current: unknown = err;
  for (let depth = 0; depth < 5 && current; depth++) {
    const code = (current as { code?: unknown }).code;
    if (typeof current === "object" && code === "P0001") {
      const message = (current as { message?: unknown }).message;
      return typeof message === "string" ? message : null;
    }

export interface StoredCheck {

/**

export async function tellMatched(deps: Pick<MediaDeps, "matched" | "log">, events: readonly MatchEvent[]): Promise<void> {
  const handler = deps.matched.handler;
  if (handler === null) return;
  for (const event of events) {
    try {
      await handler(event);
    } catch (err) {
      deps.log.error({ err, event: event.kind }, "known material: the moderation module was not told of a stored match; its sweep or its dispatch round finds it");

/** What one round of match-retry did. */
export interface MatchRetryReport {
  asked: number;
  clear: number;
  matched: number;
  unchecked: number;
  capped: number;
  failed: number;
}

/**
 * One round of match-retry (7.8 step 6, 7.14): with the comparison on, at most MATCH_RETRY_BATCH uploads whose check is
 * unchecked or capped and whose image row is younger than AUTOMATION_RULES.matchRetryHours, oldest first. A capped
 * upload is still processing, with its result in the store: finalize asks again and stores the verdict, or leaves it
 * capped while the hour's count does not allow a refusal. An unchecked one is ready: its late answer is stored as above.
 * Each upload in a try of its own. After matchRetryHours a row stays unchecked for good, and the sweeper's bound fails a
 * capped one.
 */
export async function matchRetryRound(deps: MediaDeps, finalize: (deps: MediaDeps, id: string) => Promise<boolean>): Promise<MatchRetryReport> {
  const report: MatchRetryReport = { asked: 0, clear: 0, matched: 0, unchecked: 0, capped: 0, failed: 0 };
  if (deps.match.mode === "off") return report;
  for (const id of await deps.matches.retryDue(MATCH_RETRY_BATCH, AUTOMATION_RULES.matchRetryHours)) {
    try {
      const hashed = await deps.matches.hashed(deps.matches.db, id);
      if (hashed === null) continue;
      report.asked++;
      if (hashed.checkState === "capped") {
        await finalize(deps, id);
        const after = await deps.matches.hashed(deps.matches.db, id);
        const state = after?.checkState;
        if (state === "matched") report.matched++;
        else if (state === "clear") report.clear++;
        else if (state === "capped") report.capped++;
        else report.unchecked++;
        continue;
      }
      const answer = await askSource(deps, hashed);
      const stored = await storeLateAnswer(deps, hashed, answer);
      if (stored.stored === "matched") report.matched++;
      else if (stored.stored === "clear") report.clear++;
      else report.unchecked++;
      await tellMatched(deps, stored.events);
    } catch (err) {
      report.failed++;
      deps.log.error({ err, id }, "match-retry: an upload's check could not be asked again; the next round tries it");
    }
  }
  return report;
}

/** The job under the shared lock: a round MATCH_RETRY_INTERVAL_MS after the last one ended, on one instance at a time. */
export function createMatchRetryJob(deps: MediaDeps, finalize: (deps: MediaDeps, id: string) => Promise<boolean>, lock: JobLock) {
  return createJob({ name: MATCH_RETRY_JOB, intervalMs: MATCH_RETRY_INTERVAL_MS, lockTtlMs: MATCH_RETRY_INTERVAL_MS * 2, lock, log: deps.log, run: () => matchRetryRound(deps, finalize) });
}

import { and, eq, gt, inArray, isNotNull, isNull, lt, ne, or, sql, type SQL } from "drizzle-orm";
import { ALERT_KINDS, AUTOMATION_RULES, EDGE_RULES, mediaPath, type AvatarView, type EdgePurgeView, type MediaKind } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { postMedia, posts, profiles, type Db, type DbTx } from "@korbat/db";
import type { ResultFile } from "@korbat/media-protocol";
import { WRITE_CLOCK, closingJudgment, liveNotSuspended } from "../lib/standing";
import { MediaError, type PostImage } from "./context";
import type { ReceivedHashes } from "./files";
