```ts
import type { Author, AvatarView, HiddenMedia, MediaView, PostCounts, PostView, TimelineItem, Tombstone } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { PostImage } from "../media";
import type { SocialDeps, ViewerId } from "./context";
import { encodeCursor } from "./cursor";
import type { ListRow, PostRow, ProfileRow } from "./repo";
import { postAccess, tombstone } from "./visibility";

/** Where views come from: the posts, their images through the media module, and the chip's facts through the moderation module. */
export type ViewSource = Pick<SocialDeps, "repo" | "media" | "moderation">;

/** What a post id resolves to for a viewer: the view, or a tombstone when the viewer may not see it. */
export type LoadedPost = PostView | Tombstone;

export function isTombstone(loaded: LoadedPost): loaded is Tombstone {
  return !("author" in loaded);
}

/** 2d Task 3 (7.5): with the profile's avatar as avatarsOf answered it for the page, null for the monogram. */
export function authorOf(profile: ProfileRow, avatar: AvatarView | null): Author {
  return { id: profile.id, handle: profile.handle, displayName: profile.displayName, verified: profile.verified, avatar };
}

/**
 * One image of a post as this viewer gets it (3c design, section 7.10). A visible image is the image. A withheld or
 * removed one stays with its author, who gets it with that state; anyone else gets a placeholder in its place, the same
 * for both states, with nothing of the image in it. A sealed image is that placeholder for every viewer, its author
 * included, who alone is told that it is sealed.
 */
export function mediaFor(viewer: ViewerId, authorId: string, image: PostImage): MediaView | HiddenMedia {
  const own = viewer !== null && viewer === authorId;
  if (image.state === "sealed") return own ? { id: image.id, hidden: true, sealed: true } : { id: image.id, hidden: true };
  const { state, ...view } = image;
  if (state === "visible") return view;
  return own ? { ...view, moderation: state } : { id: image.id, hidden: true };
}

/**
 * 2d (decision 26, 9.3): a post's counts as this reader gets them, the one rule for every answer that carries counts (a
 * view, a quoted embed, and the engagement answer of flows/engagement.ts): likes and reposts are null exactly when the
 * author hid them and the reader is not the author; replies and quotes are always numbers. So nobody but the author
 * learns a hidden count, by reading it or by liking and unliking.
 */
export function countsFor(viewer: ViewerId, row: PostRow): PostCounts {
  const hidden = row.hideCounts && viewer !== row.authorId;
  return { likes: hidden ? null : row.likeCount, reposts: hidden ? null : row.repostCount, replies: row.replyCount, quotes: row.quoteCount };
}

/**
 * Turns post ids into views for one viewer: loads the rows and, one level deep, the posts they
 * quote; decides access for every row with the visibility rule and the viewer's blocks; attaches
 * the viewer's like, repost and bookmark state, and every post's images, each as this viewer gets it
 * (mediaFor). Ids that resolve to nothing become tombstones, and tombstones carry no images. The
 * viewer's own visible posts that the current Explore ranking holds, while their switch is on, carry
 * the author's chip (2c design, section 8):
 * asked in one query, and only when the viewer wrote some of the posts; a quoted embed never carries it.
 * The viewer's own withheld and removed posts carry the decision behind their state (3c design, section 7.6), which the
 * moderation module names: asked the same way, once for the page and only when the viewer wrote such a post.
 * 2d (4.3): each post it shows carries the mentions that link for this viewer, read for the page's shown posts in one
 * statement (mentionsFor); a quoted embed carries none. Counts go through countsFor. 2d Task 3 (7.5): every author's
 * avatar, the quoted posts' authors' too, from one avatarsOf of the media module for the whole page.
 */
export async function loadPostViews({ repo, media, moderation }: ViewSource, viewer: ViewerId, ids: string[]): Promise<Map<string, LoadedPost>> {
  const unique = [...new Set(ids)];
  const primary = await repo.findPosts(unique);
  const quoteIds = [...new Set([...primary.values()].map((row) => row.quoteOfId).filter((id): id is string => id !== null && !primary.has(id)))];
  const quoted = await repo.findPosts(quoteIds);
  const all = new Map([...primary, ...quoted]);
  const authorIds = [...new Set([...all.values()].flatMap((row) => (row.replyToAuthorId ? [row.authorId, row.replyToAuthorId] : [row.authorId])))];
  const blocked = viewer ? await repo.blockedEitherWay(viewer, authorIds) : new Set<string>();
  const states = viewer ? await repo.viewerPostStates(viewer, [...all.keys()]) : null;
  const images = await media.forPosts([...all.keys()]);
  const avatars = await media.avatarsOf([...new Set([...all.values()].map((row) => row.authorId))], viewer);
  // A withheld or removed post is never in Explore for anyone, its author included, so only visible ones are asked about.
  // Whether the author is suspended when this reads is listedInExplore's to judge (3e), so the chip goes with the page.
  const own = viewer ? [...primary.values()].filter((row) => row.authorId === viewer && row.state === "visible").map((row) => row.id) : [];
  const inExplore = viewer && own.length > 0 ? await repo.listedInExplore(viewer, own) : new Set<string>();
  // The chip of a withheld or removed post is its author's alone, so only the viewer's own such posts are asked about.
  const restricted = viewer ? [...primary.values()].filter((row) => row.authorId === viewer && (row.state === "withheld" || row.state === "removed")).map((row) => row.id) : [];
  const decisions = viewer && moderation && restricted.length > 0 ? await moderation.authorFacts(viewer, restricted) : null;

  const access = (row: PostRow) => postAccess(viewer, row, blocked.has(row.authorId));
  // Only the posts this viewer is shown: a hidden or deleted post's mentions are never read.
  const mentioned = await repo.mentionsFor(viewer, [...primary.values()].filter((row) => access(row) === "shown").map((row) => row.id));
  /** The parent's handle only when the viewer could open the parent; a block either way, or a hidden or deleted parent, gives null. */
  const parentHandle = (row: PostRow): string | null =>
    row.replyToAuthorId && row.replyToState && postAccess(viewer, { authorId: row.replyToAuthorId, state: row.replyToState }, blocked.has(row.replyToAuthorId)) === "shown"
      ? row.replyToHandle
      : null;
  const base = (row: PostRow) => ({
    id: row.id,
    author: { ...row.author, avatar: avatars.get(row.authorId) ?? null },
    body: row.body,
    createdAt: row.createdAt.toISOString(),
    state: row.state as PostView["state"],
    replyTo: row.replyToId ? { id: row.replyToId, authorHandle: parentHandle(row) } : null,
    counts: countsFor(viewer, row),
    media: (images.get(row.id) ?? []).map((image) => mediaFor(viewer, row.authorId, image)),
    ...(states ? { viewer: states.get(row.id)! } : {}),
  });
  const quoteOf = (id: string | null): PostView["quoteOf"] => {
    if (id === null) return null;
    const row = all.get(id);
    if (!row) return tombstone(id, "hidden");
    const a = access(row);
    // 3b: a quoted post carries its provenance label too, last, for the embed's short line (10.6).
    return a === "shown" ? { ...base(row), quoteOf: null, imported: row.imported } : tombstone(id, a);
  };

  const out = new Map<string, LoadedPost>();
  for (const id of unique) {
    const row = primary.get(id);
    if (!row) {
      out.set(id, tombstone(id, "hidden"));
      continue;
    }
    const a = access(row);
    const decision = decisions?.get(id);
    // 3b (9.3): the provenance label, from the post's own columns: the archive's day, never its second. 2d (9.3): then the
    // mentions that link for this viewer and the author's hidden-counts switch, last.
    out.set(
      id,
      a === "shown"
        ? {
            ...base(row),
            ...(inExplore.has(id) ? { inExplore: true as const } : {}),
            ...(decision ? { moderation: decision } : {}),
            quoteOf: quoteOf(row.quoteOfId),
            imported: row.imported,
            mentions: mentioned.get(id) ?? [],
            countsHidden: row.hideCounts,
          }
        : tombstone(id, a),
    );
  }
  return out;
}

/** One post as the viewer sees it, or null when they may not. */
export async function postView(source: ViewSource, viewer: ViewerId, id: string): Promise<PostView | null> {
  const loaded = (await loadPostViews(source, viewer, [id])).get(id)!;
  return isTombstone(loaded) ? null : loaded;
}

/** Views for list rows, in list order, dropping anything the viewer may not see. */
export async function postViews(source: ViewSource, viewer: ViewerId, rows: ListRow[]): Promise<PostView[]> {
  const loaded = await loadPostViews(source, viewer, rows.map((row) => row.postId));
  return rows.map((row) => loaded.get(row.postId)!).filter((view): view is PostView => !isTombstone(view));
}

/** Timeline items for list rows, with the reposter attached to repost rows. */
export async function timelineItems(source: ViewSource, viewer: ViewerId, rows: ListRow[]): Promise<TimelineItem[]> {
  const loaded = await loadPostViews(source, viewer, rows.map((row) => row.postId));
  const reposterIds = [...new Set(rows.map((row) => row.reposterId).filter((id): id is string => id !== null))];
  const reposters = await source.repo.findProfiles(reposterIds);
  // 2d Task 3: the reposters' avatars, one more statement only for a page that holds a repost.
  const avatars = reposterIds.length > 0 ? await source.media.avatarsOf(reposterIds, viewer) : new Map<string, AvatarView>();
  const items: TimelineItem[] = [];
  for (const row of rows) {
    const view = loaded.get(row.postId)!;
    if (isTombstone(view)) continue;
    const reposter = row.reposterId ? reposters.get(row.reposterId) : undefined;
    if (row.reposterId && !reposter) continue;
    items.push(reposter ? { kind: "repost", post: view, repostedBy: authorOf(reposter, avatars.get(reposter.id) ?? null), repostedAt: row.sortAt.toISOString() } : { kind: "post", post: view });
  }
  return items;
}

/** The cursor for the page after these rows, or null when the page was not full. */
export function pageCursor(rows: { sortAt: Date; postId?: string; profileId?: string; reposterId?: string | null }[], limit: number): string | null {
  if (rows.length < limit) return null;
  const last = rows[rows.length - 1]!;
  return encodeCursor({ t: last.sortAt.getTime(), id: (last.postId ?? last.profileId)!, ...(last.reposterId ? { r: last.reposterId } : {}) });
}
```

```ts
import { setTimeout as sleep } from "node:timers/promises";
import pino from "pino";
import { HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS, storeLayout, uploadsLayout } from "@korbat/media-protocol";
import { loadConfig } from "./config";
import { WATCHDOG_MS, prepareStore, tick, writeHeartbeat, type LoopDeps } from "./loop";
import { configureDecoder, processImage } from "./pipeline";
import { scorerFrom } from "./score";

/**
 * The image worker. It reads uploads from one volume and writes WebP files, results and a
 * heartbeat to another, one image at a time. It has no network, no database and no queue: the two
 * volumes are everything it can reach. See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-18-images-2b-design.md.
 */
const config = loadConfig();
const log = pino({ level: config.logLevel, base: undefined });
configureDecoder(config.formats);

// 3d Task 6: the R1 scorer of R1_CLASSIFIER, none while it is off; the configuration refused a test scorer on an open site.
const scorer = scorerFrom(config.r1Classifier);

const deps: LoopDeps = {
  uploads: uploadsLayout(config.uploadsDir),
  store: storeLayout(config.storeDir),
  formats: config.formats,
  log,
  now: Date.now,
  // 2d Task 3: an avatar's upload carries its job file's crop.
  process: (path, formats, avatar) => processImage(path, formats, scorer, avatar),
  abort: (reason) => {
    log.fatal({ reason }, "watchdog: exiting so the container restarts");
    process.exit(1);
  },
  watchdogMs: WATCHDOG_MS,
};

await prepareStore(deps.store);
await writeHeartbeat(deps);
// The heartbeat has its own timer: decoding runs off the main thread, so it keeps beating during a long image.
const heartbeat = setInterval(() => void writeHeartbeat(deps).catch((err: unknown) => log.error({ err }, "heartbeat failed")), HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS);

let running = true;
const stop = (signal: string) => {
  log.info({ signal }, "stopping after the current image");
  running = false;
};
process.on("SIGTERM", () => stop("SIGTERM"));
process.on("SIGINT", () => stop("SIGINT"));

log.info({ formats: config.formats, r1Classifier: config.r1Classifier }, "worker started");
while (running) {
  const worked = await tick(deps).catch((err: unknown) => {
    log.error({ err }, "tick failed");
    return false;
  });
  if (!worked) await sleep(500);
}
clearInterval(heartbeat);
```

```ts
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import { existsSync } from "node:fs";
import { lstat, mkdir, open, readFile, readdir, rename, rm } from "node:fs/promises";
import path from "node:path";
import type { Logger } from "pino";
import type { AvatarCrop } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { AvatarJob, MAX_ATTEMPTS, MAX_JOB_BYTES, RESULT_VERSION, isMediaId, resultFileId, type Heartbeat, type MediaFormat, type ResultFile, type StoreLayout, type UploadsLayout } from "@korbat/media-protocol";
import type { Processed } from "./pipeline";

export interface LoopDeps {
  uploads: UploadsLayout;
  store: StoreLayout;
  formats: readonly MediaFormat[];
  log: Logger;
  now: () => number;
  /**
   * The image pipeline. Tests pass a stand-in; the process passes processImage. 2d Task 3: `avatar`, the crop of the
   * upload's job file, for an avatar's upload; undefined for a post's.
   */
  process: (path: string, formats: readonly MediaFormat[], avatar?: { crop: AvatarCrop }) => Promise<Processed>;
  /** Ends the process when one upload takes too long. Docker restarts the container, and the attempt counter does the rest. */
  abort: (reason: string) => void;
  watchdogMs: number;
}

export const WATCHDOG_MS = 120_000;

/** Creates the store's directories and forgets files a crash left half written. */
export async function prepareStore(store: StoreLayout): Promise<void> {
  await rm(store.tmp, { recursive: true, force: true });
  for (const dir of [store.files, store.results, store.attempts, store.tmp]) await mkdir(dir, { recursive: true });
}

/** Write under tmp/, flush, rename: the API never sees half a file, and a finished file survives a power cut. */
async function writeAtomic(store: StoreLayout, target: string, data: string | Buffer): Promise<void> {
  const temp = path.join(store.tmp, randomUUID());
  const handle = await open(temp, "w");
  try {
    await handle.writeFile(data);
    await handle.sync();
  } finally {
    await handle.close();
  }
  await rename(temp, target);
}

export async function writeHeartbeat(deps: Pick<LoopDeps, "store" | "now">): Promise<void> {
  const beat: Heartbeat = { v: 1, at: deps.now() };
  await writeAtomic(deps.store, deps.store.heartbeat, JSON.stringify(beat));
}

/** Names in a directory that are media ids and regular files. Anything else, a symlink included, is ignored. */
async function mediaFiles(dir: string): Promise<{ id: string; mtimeMs: number }[]> {
  const names = await readdir(dir).catch(() => [] as string[]);
  const found: { id: string; mtimeMs: number }[] = [];
  for (const name of names) {
    if (!isMediaId(name)) continue;
    const stats = await lstat(path.join(dir, name)).catch(() => null);
    if (stats?.isFile()) found.push({ id: name, mtimeMs: stats.mtimeMs });
  }
  return found.sort((a, b) => a.mtimeMs - b.mtimeMs || a.id.localeCompare(b.id));
}

async function readAttempts(store: StoreLayout, id: string): Promise<number> {
  const text = await readFile(store.attempt(id), "utf8").catch(() => "0");
  const count = Number.parseInt(text, 10);
  return Number.isInteger(count) && count >= 0 ? count : MAX_ATTEMPTS;
}

const writeResult = (store: StoreLayout, result: ResultFile) => writeAtomic(store, store.result(result.id), JSON.stringify(result));

/**
 * 2d Task 3 (design, sections 7.2 and 7.4): the upload's job file, which the API writes before the upload itself. None for
 * a post's upload (no file of that name); its crop for an avatar's; "malformed" for anything else that has the name: an
 * entry that is not a plain file, one over MAX_JOB_BYTES, or text that is not exactly AvatarJob. Read from a volume this
 * process does not trust, so it is looked at before it is opened, read whole only within its bound, and parsed strictly.
 */
async function avatarJob(uploads: UploadsLayout, id: string): Promise<{ crop: AvatarCrop } | null | "malformed"> {
  const file = uploads.avatarJob(id);
  const entry = await lstat(file).catch((err: NodeJS.ErrnoException) => (err.code === "ENOENT" ? null : err));
  if (entry === null) return null;
  if (entry instanceof Error || !entry.isFile() || entry.size > MAX_JOB_BYTES) return "malformed";
  try {
    const parsed = AvatarJob.safeParse(JSON.parse(await readFile(file, "utf8")));
    return parsed.success ? { crop: parsed.data.crop } : "malformed";
  } catch {
    return "malformed";
  }
}

/**
 * A deletion request stays until the API sees the image gone and removes it, so this runs for the
 * same id on several ticks. It only acts while something is left, which makes repeats free, and it
 * also catches files that were written after the request arrived.
 */
async function handleDeletions(deps: LoopDeps): Promise<boolean> {
  let worked = false;
  for (const { id } of await mediaFiles(deps.uploads.deletions)) {
    const leftovers = [deps.store.imageDir(id), deps.store.result(id), deps.store.attempt(id)].filter((target) => existsSync(target));
    if (leftovers.length === 0) continue;
    for (const target of leftovers) await rm(target, { recursive: true, force: true });
    deps.log.info({ id }, "image deleted");
    worked = true;
  }
  return worked;
}

/** One upload, start to finish. The attempt is counted before any decoding, so a file that kills the process cannot loop. */
async function processOne(deps: LoopDeps, id: string): Promise<void> {
  const { store, uploads, log } = deps;
  const attempts = await readAttempts(store, id);
  if (attempts >= MAX_ATTEMPTS) {
    await writeResult(store, { v: RESULT_VERSION, id, status: "failed", reason: "processing_failed" });
    log.warn({ id, attempts }, "upload failed: too many attempts");
    return;
  }
  await writeAtomic(store, store.attempt(id), String(attempts + 1));
  // 2d Task 3: an avatar's upload whose job file cannot be read as a crop fails for good, before any decoder runs.
  const job = await avatarJob(uploads, id);
  if (job === "malformed") {
    await writeResult(store, { v: RESULT_VERSION, id, status: "failed", reason: "processing_failed" });
    log.warn({ id }, "upload failed: its avatar job file is malformed");
    return;
  }

  const started = deps.now();
  const watchdog = setTimeout(() => deps.abort(`upload ${id} took longer than ${deps.watchdogMs} ms`), deps.watchdogMs);
  let processed: Processed;
  try {
    processed = await deps.process(uploads.upload(id), deps.formats, job ?? undefined);
  } catch (err) {
    if (!existsSync(uploads.upload(id))) return; // The API withdrew the upload while it was being read.
    log.error({ id, err }, "processing threw; the upload will be tried again");
    return;
  } finally {
    clearTimeout(watchdog);
  }

  if (!processed.ok) {
    await writeResult(store, { v: RESULT_VERSION, id, status: "failed", reason: processed.reason });
    log.info({ id, reason: processed.reason, ms: deps.now() - started }, "upload refused");
    return;
  }
  await mkdir(store.imageDir(id), { recursive: true });
  await writeAtomic(store, store.image(id, "large"), processed.large);
  await writeAtomic(store, store.image(id, "small"), processed.small);
  // The result is the commit point: it is written last, when both files are in place. 3d Task 6: with the scorer's model
  // and score while one runs. The score is not logged: it is a fact about an image the API alone keeps. 2d Task 3: version
  // 3, and the mark of an avatar's two squares on an avatar's ready result alone, which the API holds against the row's kind.
  await writeResult(store, {
    v: RESULT_VERSION,
    id,
    status: "ready",
    width: processed.width,
    height: processed.height,
    blurhash: processed.blurhash,
    ...(processed.r1 !== undefined ? { r1: processed.r1 } : {}),
    ...(job !== null ? { avatar: true as const } : {}),
  });
  log.info({ id, width: processed.width, height: processed.height, ms: deps.now() - started }, "upload processed");
}

/** A result or an attempt counter whose upload is gone has been consumed by the API, or belongs to an upload it withdrew. */
async function cleanResults(deps: LoopDeps): Promise<void> {
  for (const name of await readdir(deps.store.results).catch(() => [] as string[])) {
    const id = resultFileId(name);
    if (id && !existsSync(deps.uploads.upload(id))) await rm(deps.store.result(id), { force: true });
  }
  for (const id of await readdir(deps.store.attempts).catch(() => [] as string[])) {
    if (isMediaId(id) && !existsSync(deps.uploads.upload(id))) await rm(deps.store.attempt(id), { force: true });
  }
}

/**
 * One pass: deletions, then at most one upload, then result cleanup. Returns whether it did any
 * work, so the caller only sleeps when there was none.
 */
export async function tick(deps: LoopDeps): Promise<boolean> {
  let worked = await handleDeletions(deps);
  // An upload that already has a result is waiting for the API; one with a deletion request is not wanted any more.
  const pending = (await mediaFiles(deps.uploads.incoming)).filter(({ id }) => !existsSync(deps.store.result(id)) && !existsSync(deps.uploads.deletion(id)));
  const next = pending[0];
  if (next) {
    await processOne(deps, next.id);
    worked = true;
  }
  await cleanResults(deps);
  return worked;
}
```

```ts
import { closeSync, openSync, readSync } from "node:fs";
import { encode } from "blurhash";
import sharp from "sharp";
import type { AvatarCrop, MediaFailure } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { AVATAR_VARIANTS, MAX_SIDE, PIXEL_CAP, SNIFF_BYTES, VARIANTS, isAnimatedPng, sniffImage, type ByteReader, type MediaFormat } from "@korbat/media-protocol";
import type { Scorer } from "./score";

/**
 * Everything that touches the image decoder lives in this file. The decoder is the most
 * exploitable code korbat runs, so it only ever sees formats on an allowlist, only after the
 * file's first bytes said it is one of them, and only with a pixel cap it enforces from the header.
 */

/** libvips loader classes. Unblocking a parent class unblocks its file, buffer and source loaders. */
const LOADER: Record<MediaFormat, string> = {
  jpeg: "VipsForeignLoadJpeg",
  png: "VipsForeignLoadPng",
  webp: "VipsForeignLoadWebp",
  gif: "VipsForeignLoadNsgif",
  avif: "VipsForeignLoadHeif",
};

/** What sharp's metadata calls each format. AVIF arrives as "heif" with AV1 compression. */
const METADATA_FORMAT: Record<MediaFormat, string> = { jpeg: "jpeg", png: "png", webp: "webp", gif: "gif", avif: "heif" };

/**
 * Blocks every loader libvips has (the prebuilt binary also carries SVG and TIFF), then unblocks the
 * enabled formats. libvips ignores a class name it does not know, so a typo here would not raise an
 * error; the tests prove that every enabled format decodes and that SVG and TIFF do not. One image
 * at a time, and no operation cache, keep memory predictable.
 */
export function configureDecoder(formats: readonly MediaFormat[]): void {
  sharp.block({ operation: ["VipsForeignLoad"] });
  sharp.unblock({ operation: formats.map((format) => LOADER[format]) });
  sharp.cache(false);
  sharp.concurrency(1);
}

/**
 * What processing made of an upload. 3d Task 6: `r1`, the scorer's model and score, while a scorer runs and it answered
 * one; absent otherwise, and then the result file carries no score.
 */
export type Processed =
  | { ok: true; width: number; height: number; blurhash: string; small: Buffer; large: Buffer; r1?: { model: string; score: number } }
  | { ok: false; reason: MediaFailure };

const refuse = (reason: MediaFailure): Processed => ({ ok: false, reason });

/** Reads from an open file descriptor without ever loading the whole file. */
function fileReader(fd: number): ByteReader {
  return (offset, length) => {
    const buffer = Buffer.alloc(length);
    return buffer.subarray(0, readSync(fd, buffer, 0, length, offset));
  };
}

/** The first bytes decide what the file is. No decoder has run when this returns. */
function sniffFile(path: string, formats: readonly MediaFormat[]): { format: MediaFormat } | { reason: MediaFailure } {
  const fd = openSync(path, "r");
  try {
    const read = fileReader(fd);
    const sniffed = sniffImage(read(0, SNIFF_BYTES));
    if (sniffed.kind === "animated") return { reason: "animated_not_supported" };
    if (sniffed.kind !== "image" || !formats.includes(sniffed.format)) return { reason: "unsupported_format" };
    if (sniffed.format === "png" && isAnimatedPng(read)) return { reason: "animated_not_supported" };
    return { format: sniffed.format };
  } finally {
    closeSync(fd);
  }
}

/** What a decoder error means for the person who uploaded the file. A missing input is not their fault and is rethrown. */
function failureOf(err: unknown): MediaFailure {
  const message = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);
  if (/input file is missing/i.test(message)) throw err;
  if (/exceeds pixel limit/i.test(message)) return "image_too_large";
  if (/timeout/i.test(message)) return "processing_failed";
  return "corrupt_image";
}

/**
 * Turns one uploaded file into the two WebP sizes and a blurhash, or says why not. The output is a
 * fresh encode: rotated by EXIF, in sRGB, without EXIF, GPS, ICC, XMP, IPTC, thumbnails or gain
 * maps, and without anything that was appended to the file. `failOn: "error"` refuses truncated
 * and broken files but not the harmless libjpeg warnings many phone cameras trigger.
 *
 * 3d Task 6 (design, sections 5 "The adapters" and 10.2): with a scorer, the small size's raw pixels, which are rendered
 * here once for the WebP and the blurhash, are also handed to it, with their width, height and channels; nothing else is.
 *
 * 2d Task 3 (design, section 7.4): with `avatar`, the crop of the upload's job file, the same checks run first, and then
 * the two squares of avatarSquares are made instead of the two sizes. The uncropped image is never written.
 */
export async function processImage(path: string, formats: readonly MediaFormat[], scorer: Scorer | null = null, avatar?: { crop: AvatarCrop }): Promise<Processed> {
  const sniffed = sniffFile(path, formats);
  if ("reason" in sniffed) return refuse(sniffed.reason);
  const { format } = sniffed;
  const input = { limitInputPixels: PIXEL_CAP[format], failOn: "error", sequentialRead: true } as const;

  try {
    const meta = await sharp(path, input).metadata();
    if (meta.format !== METADATA_FORMAT[format]) return refuse("unsupported_format");
    if (format === "avif" && meta.compression !== "av1") return refuse("unsupported_format");
    if ((meta.pages ?? 1) > 1) return refuse("animated_not_supported");
    if ((meta.width ?? 0) > MAX_SIDE || (meta.height ?? 0) > MAX_SIDE) return refuse("image_too_large");
    if (avatar !== undefined) return await avatarSquares(path, input, meta.autoOrient, avatar.crop, scorer);

    const resized = (edge: number) =>
      sharp(path, input).autoOrient().resize({ width: edge, height: edge, fit: "inside", withoutEnlargement: true }).timeout({ seconds: 30 });
    const large = await resized(VARIANTS.large.edge).webp({ quality: VARIANTS.large.quality, effort: 4 }).toBuffer({ resolveWithObject: true });

    // The small size is rendered to pixels once. Its WebP and the blurhash both come from those
    // pixels, so neither depends on a decoder: the WebP loader may be switched off.
    const pixels = await resized(VARIANTS.small.edge).toColourspace("srgb").raw().toBuffer({ resolveWithObject: true });
    const raw = { width: pixels.info.width, height: pixels.info.height, channels: pixels.info.channels };
    const small = await sharp(pixels.data, { raw }).webp({ quality: VARIANTS.small.quality, effort: 4 }).timeout({ seconds: 30 }).toBuffer();
    const thumb = await sharp(pixels.data, { raw }).resize(32, 32, { fit: "inside" }).ensureAlpha().raw().toBuffer({ resolveWithObject: true });
    const blurhash = encode(new Uint8ClampedArray(thumb.data), thumb.info.width, thumb.info.height, 4, 3);
    const score = scorer === null ? null : await scorer.score(pixels.data, raw.width, raw.height, raw.channels);

    return { ok: true, width: large.info.width, height: large.info.height, blurhash, small, large: large.data, ...(scorer !== null && score !== null ? { r1: { model: scorer.model, score } } : {}) };
  } catch (err) {
    return refuse(failureOf(err));
  }
}

/**
 * 2d Task 3 (design, sections 7.1 and 7.4): an avatar's two squares. With `w` and `h` the image's size once its EXIF
 * orientation is applied and `s` the shorter of the two, the square of side `s` is cut along the longer side at 0 (start),
 * at half the difference rounded down (centre) or at the difference (end); sharp orients an input that autoOrient marks
 * before it extracts, so the crop is taken from the image as it is shown. The square is rendered once to raw sRGB pixels
 * of at most AVATAR_VARIANTS.large.edge on a side, never enlarged: those pixels make large.webp and, with a scorer, are what
 * it scores, as a post's image is scored from its small size. The small square is resized from them, and its pixels make
 * small.webp and the blurhash. Every file is a fresh encode of pixels, so no metadata of the source survives, and no
 * decoder of WebP is needed. Runs inside processImage's try: a decoder's error is its failure.
 */
async function avatarSquares(path: string, input: Parameters<typeof sharp>[1], oriented: { width: number; height: number }, crop: AvatarCrop, scorer: Scorer | null): Promise<Processed> {
  const side = Math.min(oriented.width, oriented.height);
  const spare = Math.max(oriented.width, oriented.height) - side;
  const offset = crop === "start" ? 0 : crop === "centre" ? Math.floor(spare / 2) : spare;
  const region = oriented.width >= oriented.height ? { left: offset, top: 0, width: side, height: side } : { left: 0, top: offset, width: side, height: side };
  const square = (edge: number) => ({ width: edge, height: edge, fit: "inside" as const, withoutEnlargement: true });

  const large = await sharp(path, input).autoOrient().extract(region).resize(square(AVATAR_VARIANTS.large.edge)).toColourspace("srgb").raw().timeout({ seconds: 30 }).toBuffer({ resolveWithObject: true });
  const largeRaw = { width: large.info.width, height: large.info.height, channels: large.info.channels };
  const largeWebp = await sharp(large.data, { raw: largeRaw }).webp({ quality: AVATAR_VARIANTS.large.quality, effort: 4 }).timeout({ seconds: 30 }).toBuffer();
  const small = await sharp(large.data, { raw: largeRaw }).resize(square(AVATAR_VARIANTS.small.edge)).raw().toBuffer({ resolveWithObject: true });
  const smallRaw = { width: small.info.width, height: small.info.height, channels: small.info.channels };
  const smallWebp = await sharp(small.data, { raw: smallRaw }).webp({ quality: AVATAR_VARIANTS.small.quality, effort: 4 }).timeout({ seconds: 30 }).toBuffer();
  const thumb = await sharp(small.data, { raw: smallRaw }).resize(32, 32, { fit: "inside" }).ensureAlpha().raw().toBuffer({ resolveWithObject: true });
  const blurhash = encode(new Uint8ClampedArray(thumb.data), thumb.info.width, thumb.info.height, 4, 3);
  const score = scorer === null ? null : await scorer.score(large.data, largeRaw.width, largeRaw.height, largeRaw.channels);

  return { ok: true, width: largeRaw.width, height: largeRaw.height, blurhash, small: smallWebp, large: largeWebp, ...(scorer !== null && score !== null ? { r1: { model: scorer.model, score } } : {}) };
}
```

```ts
 */
export const ACTIVITY_NOT_SHOWN = ["muted", "post_not_visible", "unfollowed", "actor_deleted"] as const;
export type ActivityNotShown = (typeof ACTIVITY_NOT_SHOWN)[number];

/**
 * One Activity entry the account received, as the export lists it, ungrouped: its kind, when it was written (to the
 * microsecond), the post's id (null for a follow, and for a post the account may not see, so the export never discloses
 * another person's moderation), the actor's handle at the time of export, and `shown`: true, or why the list hides it.
 */
const ExportedActivityEntry = z
  .object({
    kind: z.enum(ACTIVITY_KINDS),
    at,
    postId: z.uuid().nullable(),
    actorHandle: z.string(),
    shown: z.union([z.literal(true), z.enum(ACTIVITY_NOT_SHOWN)]),
  })
  .refine((entry) => entry.kind !== "follow" || entry.postId === null, { message: "a follow names no post", path: ["postId"] })
  .refine((entry) => entry.shown !== "post_not_visible" || entry.postId === null, { message: "a post the account may not see is named by no id", path: ["postId"] });

/**
 * 3b (design, section 11.2): one of the account's imports, newest first: its source, state and times, when the person made
 * the statement, the choice confirmed (null before a confirmation) and its counts. Never a file name, a handle or a text:
 * the archive and the work folder are not exported.
 */
const ExportedImport = z.object({
  id: z.uuid(),
  source: ImportSource,
  status: ImportStatus,
  createdAt: at,
  endedAt: at.nullable(),
  statedAt: at.nullable(),
  choice: ImportChoice.nullable(),
  counts: z.object({ postsPublished: z.int().min(0), postsRemoved: z.int().min(0), imagesKept: z.int().min(0), imagesLeftOut: z.int().min(0) }),
});

/** A passkey of the account as the export lists it (1c design, section 7.7): what the Security screen shows, and nothing that identifies the key, its id or its authenticator. */
const ExportedPasskey = z.object({
  name: z.string(),
  createdAt: at,
  lastUsedAt: at.nullable(),
  /** Backed up, so the password manager syncs it to the owner's other devices. */
  synced: z.boolean(),
  /** The label of the device that added it; null once that device is gone. */
  createdOn: z.string().nullable(),
});

/**
 * A decision about the account or one of its posts, as the export lists it (3c design, section 7.11): one of the decisions
 * the Cases screen lists, which are those its author was told of, with what its statement of reasons tells.
 *   - `decidedOn` is the decision's UTC day, as the list shows it; `postId` the entry of `posts` a decision about a post
 *     concerns, null for a decision about the account's display name or bio.
 *   - `ground` and `ruleId` name the law or the rule it rests on, and `rulesVersion` the version of the rulebook it was
 *     made under.
 *   - `measures` are what it imposed, each with `noEffect` set when it changed nothing anyone saw (the content was already
 *     not shown, or already deleted); `reversals` what it lifted. An image measure names the account's own image.
 *   - `facts`, `reason` and `legalReference` are the statement's texts while korbat holds them; null for a text the
 *     decision never had, one that was erased, and the facts and the reason of a decision that restricted nothing.
 *   - `appeal` is where the account's appeal of the decision stands; null when it filed none.
 * It names its source nowhere: no report, no reporter, no notifier and no staff member is part of it.
 */
const ExportedDecision = z.object({
  id: z.uuid(),
  decidedOn: day,
  postId: z.uuid().nullable(),
  kind: z.enum(["interim", "final", "order", "review", "correction"]),
  outcome: z.enum(["restricted", "no_violation", "not_evident", "kept", "partly_reversed", "reversed"]),
  ground: z.enum(["incompatible", "illegal"]).nullable(),
  ruleId: z.enum(RULE_IDS).nullable(),
  rulesVersion: z.number().int().positive(),
  measures: z.array(z.object({ kind: z.enum(MEASURE_KINDS), mediaId: z.uuid().nullable(), noEffect: z.enum(["already", "deleted"]).nullable() })),
  reversals: z.array(z.object({ kind: z.enum(REVERSAL_KINDS), mediaId: z.uuid().nullable() })),
  facts: z.string().nullable(),
  reason: z.string().nullable(),
  legalReference: z.string().nullable(),
  appeal: z
    .discriminatedUnion("state", [
      z.object({ state: z.literal("pending"), result: z.null() }),
      z.object({ state: z.literal("answered"), result: z.enum(["kept", "partly_reversed", "reversed"]) }),
    ])
    .nullable(),
  /**
   * 3f (design, W.7): an order's decision once its author was told, never before: its notice's facts (the order's kind,
   * state, authority, reference and day, whether korbat confirmed it, whether and until when the notice was held, the
   * preservation's end) and, read at the export's time, the authority's words and the day of an erasure; a reinstatement's
   * entry with its ground. Absent on every other decision.
   */
  order: OrderNoticeFacts.optional(),
  orderTexts: OrderTexts.optional(),
  erasedOn: day.nullable().optional(),
  /**
   * 3d (design, W.10): what the statement says of automated means, as its own columns and its signal give it
   * (DecisionStatement's three members: false, not_automated and null for a decision made before 3d), and the text the
   * account sent with "Ask for a person" about a program's measure, with its time, while korbat keeps it; null otherwise.
   * Never a score, a hash, a list version or a classification.
   */
  automatedDetection: z.boolean(),
  automatedDecision: z.enum(AUTOMATED_DECISIONS),
  signal: StatementSignal.nullable(),
  objection: z.object({ text: z.string(), createdAt: at }).nullable(),
});

/**
 * 3d (design, W.6 and W.10): a release that concerned the account's posts or one of its uploads, as its notice reads it:
 * its ground (a leave or instruction, or a period) and its time, and whether it was of an upload. Listed only from the
 * time the account may be told of it: never while its notice is held. Never an authority, a reference or an assessment.
 */
const ExportedRelease = z.object({ id: z.uuid(), basis: z.enum(["leave", "period"]), releasedAt: at, upload: z.boolean() });

/**
 * One item of a report in its sender's export: its place in the report, its korbat address (an account's under the handle
 * the report named, never a later one) and whether it is the re-examination of the item before it. `outcome`, its words
 * as the list of reports reads them (`outcomeText`) and whether a re-examination can still be asked for
 * (`reexaminationOpen`) are told together, once the daily release has shown the outcome; until then all three are null,
 * whether or not a moderator has decided, as on the list and on the report's page.
 */
const ExportedReportItem = z
  .object({
    position: z.number().int().min(1).max(20),
    link: z.string(),
    reexamines: z.boolean(),
    outcome: z.enum(ITEM_OUTCOMES).nullable(),
    outcomeText: z.string().nullable(),
    reexaminationOpen: z.boolean().nullable(),
  })
  .refine((item) => (item.outcome === null) === (item.outcomeText === null) && (item.outcome === null) === (item.reexaminationOpen === null), {
    message: "an outcome, its words and whether a re-examination is open are told together or not at all",
  });

/**
 * A report or a notice the account sent, while korbat keeps its record (3c design, sections 6.6 and 7.11): its reference,
 * when korbat received it, whether it said that something breaks a rule or is illegal, the rule it cited (always for a
 * report on a rule, optionally for a notice of illegality), its Transparency Database category, and the sender's own
 * explanation. A report on the path for child sexual abuse material records no sender, the account included, so it is in
 * nobody's export.
 */
const ExportedReport = z.object({
  ref: NoticeRef,
  receivedAt: at,
  ground: z.enum(["rule", "illegal"]),
  ruleId: z.enum(RULE_IDS).nullable(),
  category: z.enum(TDB_CATEGORIES),
  explanation: z.string().nullable(),
  items: z.array(ExportedReportItem),
});

/**
 * A strike the account was given (3e design, section 18, W.8): the decision that gave it, the post it was given for, the
 * rule, when it was given, until when it counts, and when it was overruled (null while it stands). Strikes from posts are
 * the account's own data; nothing here names another person.
 */
const ExportedStrike = z.object({ decisionId: z.uuid(), postId: z.uuid(), ruleId: z.enum(RULE_IDS), givenAt: at, countsUntil: at, overruledAt: at.nullable() });

/**
 * A suspension, a termination, a warning about reporting or a restriction of reporting of the account (3e design, W.8):
 *   - `decisionId` is the decision that took it, `kind` the measure, `basis` what the database found it rests on, `days`
 *     the days the decision gave (null for a termination and a warning), `announced` whether it was announced (null for
 *     a warning), and `decidedAt` the decision's time.
 *   - `earliestStart` is the earliest start a suspension or a termination was announced with (null for the two reporting
 *     measures). `startsAt` and `endsAt` are its period as the ledger gives it now: null for a suspension that has no
 *     start (an announcement still waiting, or one lifted before its start); `endsAt` null for a termination; a
 *     warning runs from its decision to the end of its counting, a restriction from its decision for its days; each end
 *     is cut to a lift or to a broken basis.
 *   - `liftedAt` and `liftedBy` are the reversal that lifted it and its decision, `replaced` whether that was a withdrawal
 *     for another measure; `basisEndedAt` and `basisEndedBy` the reversal that broke what it rested on and its decision.
 * It names no staff member and no reporter.
 */
const ExportedStanding = z.object({
  decisionId: z.uuid(),
  kind: z.enum(["suspend", "terminate", "warn_reporting", "restrict_reporting"]),
  basis: z.enum(STANDING_BASES),
  days: z.number().int().min(STANDING_DAYS.min).max(STANDING_DAYS.max).nullable(),
  announced: z.boolean().nullable(),
  decidedAt: at,
  earliestStart: at.nullable(),
  startsAt: at.nullable(),
  endsAt: at.nullable(),
  liftedAt: at.nullable(),
  liftedBy: z.uuid().nullable(),
  replaced: z.boolean(),
  basisEndedAt: at.nullable(),
  basisEndedBy: z.uuid().nullable(),
});

/**
 * A reply the account sent to a suspension or a termination (3e design, W.8): the decision it answered, when it was filed
 * and whether before the start, its text while korbat holds it (null when none was written, or once erased, with
 * `erasedAt`), and the decision that answered it. A reply is never erased before it is answered.
 */
const ExportedReply = z.object({
  decisionId: z.uuid(),
  filedAt: at,
  onTime: z.boolean(),
  text: z.string().max(REPLY_TEXT_MAX).nullable(),
  erasedAt: at.nullable(),
  answeredAt: at.nullable(),
  answeredBy: z.uuid().nullable(),
});

/**
 * The account's own reporting counts (3e design, W.8 and section 6.3): the frame they are counted in, the rule reports it
 * sent on each UTC day korbat still counts, every mark "manifestly unfounded" on its own reports by the report's
 * reference and the item's position (when its report was sent, when it was marked, when a correction withdrew it, and
 * whether it counts now), and the marked reports in the frame, which is what a warning's and a restriction's threshold
 * reads. Nothing in it names another person: never the item reported, its author, or the decision's staff member.
 */
const ExportedReporting = z.object({
  frameDays: z.number().int().positive(),
  days: z.array(z.object({ day, reports: z.number().int().positive() })),
  marks: z.array(z.object({ ref: NoticeRef, position: z.number().int().min(1).max(20), sentOn: day, markedAt: at, withdrawnAt: at.nullable(), counts: z.boolean() })),
  markedReports: z.number().int().nonnegative(),
});

/**
 * export.json inside the data export archive (1b design, section 7.5): everything the account owns, and
 * nothing about other people beyond the handle they had at export time.
 */
/**
 * What deleting an account removes, and what korbat keeps of it (3c design, section 2, row Deletion and cases): the one
 * sentence the deletion screen and both deletion mails say. Since moderation cases, korbat keeps a case's copy of a
 * reported or restricted post or profile for the periods its terms give, and sealed images for the authorities, also
 * after the account is gone, so no sentence about a deletion says that everything is gone for good. 3f (design, W.5):
 * a post preserved under an authority's order and an address held for a report to the authorities outlive the account
 * too, so the sentence names what the law obliges korbat to keep, for every account alike: a sentence for one account
 * alone would tell what a non-disclosure decision forbids.
 */
export const ACCOUNT_DELETION_WORDS =
  "Your posts, images and profile are removed from korbat for everyone, except what korbat keeps for a time: where a post or your profile was reported or restricted, its copy for that case, and what the law obliges korbat to keep, each for the periods in its terms (Terms, Your data).";

export const ExportFormat = z.object({
  format: z.literal("korbat-export-1"),
  exportedAt: at,
  account: z.object({
    id: z.uuid(),
    email: z.email(),
    createdAt: at,
    role: Role,
    mfaEnabled: z.boolean(),
    hasPassword: z.boolean(),
    verified: z.boolean(),
    termsVersion: z.string().nullable(),
    termsAcceptedAt: at.nullable(),
    /** The account's passkeys, newest first. Added to korbat-export-1 without a new format name: a reader that does not know the member loses nothing by skipping it. */
    passkeys: z.array(ExportedPasskey),
  }),
  profile: z.object({
    handle: z.string(),
    displayName: z.string(),
    bio: z.string(),
    createdAt: at,
    /** Every handle the account ever had, the current one included. */
    handleHistory: z.array(z.string()),
    /**
     * "Show my posts in Explore" as it stands (2c design, section 8). Added to korbat-export-1 without a new format name: a
     * reader that does not know the member loses nothing by skipping it.
     */
    showInExplore: z.boolean(),
    /**
     * The account's own handles that korbat retired and that are still retired, each with when (3e design, W.8): such a
     * handle stays in `handleHistory`, which lists plain strings, so its time is told here. Added to korbat-export-1
     * without a new format name, last in the profile; empty when none is retired.
     */
    retiredHandles: z.array(z.object({ handle: z.string(), retiredAt: at })),
    /**
     * 2d Task 3 (design, sections 7.8 and 11.2): the account's picture while one is set and the account is shown it, with its
     * file in the archive (the 400 px square, `media/<id>.webp`, listed in missingMedia when it could not be read) and its
     * size; null otherwise. Added to korbat-export-1 without a new format name, before sharePreviews.
     */
    avatar: z.object({ id: z.string(), file: z.string(), width: z.number().int().positive(), height: z.number().int().positive() }).nullable(),
    /**
     * 2d (design, section 11.2; decision 21): the link-preview switch as it stands. Added to korbat-export-1 without a new
     * format name, last in the profile.
     */
    sharePreviews: z.boolean(),
  }),
  posts: z.array(ExportedPost),
  likes: z.array(PostRef),
  reposts: z.array(PostRef),
  bookmarks: z.array(PostRef),
  following: z.array(HandleRef),
  blocks: z.array(HandleRef),
  mutes: z.array(HandleRef),
  /** The live sessions. `id` is the session's handle, as the session list names it; the hash of its token never leaves the server. */
  sessions: z.array(z.object({ id: z.string(), createdAt: at, lastUsedAt: at, current: z.boolean() })),
  devices: z.array(z.object({ label: z.string().nullable(), platform: Platform, firstSeenAt: at, lastSeenAt: at })),
  /** The account's own security events: their kind and time, without the metadata. */
  events: z.array(z.object({ type: z.string(), at })),
  /** Ids of ready images whose file was not on disk when the archive was written. */
  missingMedia: z.array(z.string()),
  /**
   * What korbat's moderation holds for the account (3c design, section 7.11): the decisions about it that its Cases screen
   * lists, newest first, and its own reports and notices, newest first. Never another person's report, a reporter, a
   * notifier or a staff member. Added to korbat-export-1 without a new format name, last in the document: a reader that
   * does not know the member loses nothing by skipping it. `strikes` (3e) lists the account's strikes, newest first;
   * then `standing` its suspensions, terminations and reporting measures, newest first, `replies` its replies to them,
   * newest first, and `reporting` its own reporting counts (3e design, W.8).
   */
  moderation: z.object({
    decisions: z.array(ExportedDecision),
    reports: z.array(ExportedReport),
    strikes: z.array(ExportedStrike),
    standing: z.array(ExportedStanding),
    replies: z.array(ExportedReply),
    reporting: ExportedReporting,
    /**
     * 3d (design, W.10): the account's refused uploads, newest first, each as its notice reads it (UploadRefusalView: the
     * day, the source, the kind of match, the objection, the end and the release as far as the account may be told of
     * them), with no file and no hash; and the releases about its posts or uploads that it may be told of, newest first.
     */
    uploads: z.array(UploadRefusalView),
    releases: z.array(ExportedRelease),
  }),
  /**
   * 3b (design, section 11.2): the account's imports, newest first, each as ExportedImport. Added to korbat-export-1
   * without a new format name, last in the document: a reader that does not know the member loses nothing by skipping it.
   */
  imports: z.array(ExportedImport),
  /**
   * 2d (design, section 11.2; decision 28): the account's Activity as korbat holds it: the seen marker (null before the
   * first visit), the settings (the defaults for an account that never changed them), and every entry it received that
   * korbat still holds, newest first and ungrouped, shown or not. Moderation entries are not repeated here: the
   * `moderation` member holds them. Added to korbat-export-1 without a new format name, last in the document.
   */
  activity: z.object({ seenAt: at.nullable(), settings: ActivitySettings, received: z.array(ExportedActivityEntry) }),
});
export type ExportFormat = z.infer<typeof ExportFormat>;
```

```ts
import { z } from "zod";
import { AvatarView } from "./media";
import { FORBIDDEN_FORMAT } from "./text";

/** Every code the auth endpoints can put in ErrorEnvelope.error.code. */
export const AuthErrorCode = z.enum([
  "invalid_code",
  "code_expired",
  "too_many_attempts",
  "invalid_credentials",
  "mfa_required",
  "invalid_mfa_code",
  "reauth_required",
  "csrf_failed",
  "turnstile_failed",
  "disposable_email",
  "age_requirement",
  "terms_required",
  "handle_taken",
  "handle_invalid",
  "handle_reserved",
  "password_too_short",
  "password_too_long",
  "password_breached",
  "password_check_unavailable",
  "staff_mfa_required",
  "onboarding_required",
  "mail_unavailable",
  "rate_limited",
  "handle_cooldown",
  "email_in_use",
  "phone_in_use",
  "badge_unavailable",
  "verify_unavailable",
  // Passkeys (1c design, sections 8 and 9).
  "passkey_invalid",
  "passkey_unsupported",
  "passkey_limit",
  "passkey_suspended",
  "passkey_not_found",
  "challenge_expired",
  // 3e (design, section 10.5): a handle korbat retired, refused to everyone, its former holder included; the social
  // module's handle change answers it too.
  "handle_retired",
]);
export type AuthErrorCode = z.infer<typeof AuthErrorCode>;

export const Platform = z.enum(["web", "ios", "android"]);
export type Platform = z.infer<typeof Platform>;

export const Role = z.enum(["user", "moderator", "admin"]);
export type Role = z.infer<typeof Role>;

/** Random id created once per app install. The server stores only a keyed hash of it. */
export const DeviceId = z.string().regex(/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{22,64}$/);
/** 32 random bytes as base64url without padding: flow ids, MFA tickets, single-use link tokens. */
export const OpaqueId = z.string().regex(/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$/);
export const Email = z.string().trim().toLowerCase().max(254).pipe(z.email());
export const EmailCode = z.string().regex(/^\d{6}$/);
export const TotpCode = z.string().regex(/^\d{6}$/);
/**
 * A phone number in E.164 once the spaces, hyphens and parentheses people type are dropped: a plus and
 * 7 to 15 digits, the first not zero. Whether the number exists is the verification provider's call.
 */
export const Phone = z
  .string()
  .trim()
  .max(64)
  .transform((raw) => raw.replace(/[\s()-]/g, ""))
  .pipe(z.string().regex(/^\+[1-9][0-9]{6,14}$/, "phone numbers are written like +447911123456"));
/** The six-digit code the verification provider texts to a phone; the development provider's is 000000. */
export const PhoneCode = z.string().regex(/^\d{6}$/);
export const RecoveryCode = z
  .string()
  .trim()
  .toLowerCase()
  .regex(/^[a-z2-7]{4}-[a-z2-7]{4}-[a-z2-7]{4}$/);
/**
 * The prefix of a retired handle's placeholder (3e design, sections 6.2 and 10.1): the placeholder is the prefix and 12
 * lower-case hex digits made from the retirement's id, 20 characters, so it is a valid handle that every reader of a handle
 * reads unchanged. The handle rule reserves the whole prefix, so nobody can choose one, and a trigger refuses it to every
 * role but the migrator.
 */
export const RETIRED_HANDLE_PREFIX = "retired_";

/** Whether a handle has a placeholder's form: the prefix and exactly 12 lower-case hex digits. */
export function isRetiredPlaceholder(handle: string): boolean {
  if (!handle.startsWith(RETIRED_HANDLE_PREFIX)) return false;
  const digits = handle.slice(RETIRED_HANDLE_PREFIX.length);
  return digits.length === 12 && [...digits].every((digit) => "0123456789abcdef".includes(digit));
}

/** Handle rules (3-20 of a-z, 0-9, _; reserved names) are enforced by the flow so it can return a specific error code. */
export const HandleInput = z.string().trim().toLowerCase().min(1).max(64);
export const DisplayName = z
  .string()
  .trim()
  .min(1)
  .max(50)
  .regex(/^[^\p{Cc}]+$/u)
  .refine((name) => !FORBIDDEN_FORMAT.test(name), { message: "invisible direction and spacing characters are not allowed" });
export const TurnstileToken = z.string().min(1).max(2048);
/** Length rules (12-128) are enforced by the flow so it can return password_too_short or password_too_long. */
export const PasswordInput = z.string().min(1).max(1024);

/**
 * A new bearer token after the server rotated the session. Present only for native clients; web
 * clients receive fresh cookies instead.
 */
export const RotatedToken = z.string().optional();

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- email entry and sign-up

export const EmailStartRequest = z.object({
  email: Email,
  turnstileToken: TurnstileToken,
  deviceId: DeviceId,
  platform: Platform,
});
export type EmailStartRequest = z.infer<typeof EmailStartRequest>;

export const FlowResponse = z.object({ flowId: OpaqueId });
export type FlowResponse = z.infer<typeof FlowResponse>;

export const EmailVerifyRequest = z.object({ flowId: OpaqueId, code: EmailCode });
export type EmailVerifyRequest = z.infer<typeof EmailVerifyRequest>;

/** A session was issued. Native clients get the bearer token in the body; web clients only get cookies. */
export const SessionResult = z.object({
  result: z.literal("session"),
  mustReenrollMfa: z.boolean(),
  token: z.string().optional(),
});
export const MfaRequiredResult = z.object({ result: z.literal("mfa_required"), mfaTicket: OpaqueId });
export const SignupRequiredResult = z.object({ result: z.literal("signup_required") });

export const EmailVerifyResponse = z.discriminatedUnion("result", [SessionResult, MfaRequiredResult, SignupRequiredResult]);
export type EmailVerifyResponse = z.infer<typeof EmailVerifyResponse>;

export const SignInResponse = z.discriminatedUnion("result", [SessionResult, MfaRequiredResult]);
export type SignInResponse = z.infer<typeof SignInResponse>;

export const SignupCompleteRequest = z.object({
  flowId: OpaqueId,
  dateOfBirth: z.iso.date(),
  termsVersion: z.string().min(1).max(64),
});
export type SignupCompleteRequest = z.infer<typeof SignupCompleteRequest>;

export const Profile = z.object({ id: z.uuid(), handle: z.string(), displayName: z.string() });
export type Profile = z.infer<typeof Profile>;

export const OnboardingHandleRequest = z.object({ handle: HandleInput, displayName: DisplayName });
export type OnboardingHandleRequest = z.infer<typeof OnboardingHandleRequest>;

export const OnboardingHandleResponse = z.object({ profile: Profile, token: RotatedToken });
export type OnboardingHandleResponse = z.infer<typeof OnboardingHandleResponse>;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- password

export const PasswordSigninRequest = z.object({
  email: Email,
  password: PasswordInput,
  turnstileToken: TurnstileToken,
  deviceId: DeviceId,
  platform: Platform,
});
export type PasswordSigninRequest = z.infer<typeof PasswordSigninRequest>;

export const PasswordSetRequest = z.object({ password: PasswordInput });
export type PasswordSetRequest = z.infer<typeof PasswordSetRequest>;

export const PasswordSetResponse = z.object({ token: RotatedToken });
export type PasswordSetResponse = z.infer<typeof PasswordSetResponse>;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- MFA

export const TotpSetupResponse = z.object({
  otpauthUri: z.string().startsWith("otpauth://totp/"),
  qrSvg: z.string().startsWith("<svg"),
});
export type TotpSetupResponse = z.infer<typeof TotpSetupResponse>;

export const TotpCodeRequest = z.object({ code: TotpCode });
export type TotpCodeRequest = z.infer<typeof TotpCodeRequest>;

/**
 * Turning TOTP off takes no code (1c design, section 2): the route needs a level-2 re-authentication, which already spent
 * the current step. A code a client sends anyway is dropped.
 */
export const TotpDisableRequest = z.object({});
export type TotpDisableRequest = z.infer<typeof TotpDisableRequest>;

export const RecoveryCodesResponse = z.object({ recoveryCodes: z.array(RecoveryCode).length(10) });
export type RecoveryCodesResponse = z.infer<typeof RecoveryCodesResponse>;

export const TotpConfirmResponse = z.object({ recoveryCodes: z.array(RecoveryCode).length(10), token: RotatedToken });
export type TotpConfirmResponse = z.infer<typeof TotpConfirmResponse>;

/** Exactly one of `code` or `recoveryCode`. */
export const MfaVerifyRequest = z.union([
  z.strictObject({ mfaTicket: OpaqueId, code: TotpCode }),
  z.strictObject({ mfaTicket: OpaqueId, recoveryCode: RecoveryCode }),
]);
export type MfaVerifyRequest = z.infer<typeof MfaVerifyRequest>;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- re-authentication

// ReauthRequest lives in passkeys.ts: its `passkey` variant needs AuthenticationResponseJSON, and having auth.ts import
// that would form a cycle (passkeys.ts already imports this file). ReauthResponse stays here, as it names no passkey type.

/**
 * What a re-authentication answers (1c design, section 7.2): the level the session holds now (2 when a second factor
 * stands beside a first within the window, or a user-verified passkey does), the rotated token for native clients (web
 * clients get fresh cookies instead), and, after a recovery code, that two-factor authentication should be set up again.
 */
export const ReauthResponse = z.object({
  level: z.union([z.literal(1), z.literal(2)]),
  token: RotatedToken,
  mustReenrollMfa: z.boolean().optional(),
});
export type ReauthResponse = z.infer<typeof ReauthResponse>;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- sessions and account

export const SessionInfo = z.object({
  /**
   * The session's handle: a random id it keeps for its whole life, which `DELETE /api/auth/sessions/:id` takes. Never the
   * token's hash, which changes whenever the token rotates (at every re-authentication, for one), so a session listed
   * before a rotation can still be revoked after it.
   */
  id: z.uuid(),
  deviceLabel: z.string(),
  platform: Platform,
  createdAt: z.iso.datetime(),
  lastUsedAt: z.iso.datetime(),
  current: z.boolean(),
});
export type SessionInfo = z.infer<typeof SessionInfo>;

export const SessionsResponse = z.object({ sessions: z.array(SessionInfo) });
export type SessionsResponse = z.infer<typeof SessionsResponse>;

export const NotMeRequest = z.object({ token: OpaqueId });
export type NotMeRequest = z.infer<typeof NotMeRequest>;

/**
 * The signed-in account's own profile as /me returns it (the profile-editing routes answer the public ProfileView): the public facts
 * plus when the handle last changed (the app shows when the next change is allowed), whether the
 * verified badge is held, and whether the account's posts show in Explore (2c design, section 8), a
 * switch that is the author's own and never part of the public profile. 2d (9.3, decision 21): and beside it the
 * person's link-preview switch, off until they turn it on, which no public answer carries either.
 */
export const MeProfile = Profile.extend({ handleChangedAt: z.iso.datetime().nullable(), verified: z.boolean(), showInExplore: z.boolean(), sharePreviews: z.boolean() });
export type MeProfile = z.infer<typeof MeProfile>;

/**
 * 3e (design, section 10.2): where the signed-in account's standing stands now, read from the ledger at the request and
 * never kept in a session or a cache, so the banner and a refusal's sentence are true of the row. `activeStrikes` counts
 * the strikes that count now. `measure` is the account's one standing measure that stands and has not ended (a
 * suspension or a termination), or null: its decision, kind and days (null for a termination); its state now (no start
 * yet because the notice mail's outcome is unknown, a start fixed and ahead, a start held by a reply sent in time, or
 * running); the earliest start its statement names, and its start and end once the database has fixed them (the end
 * null for a termination); the reply and whether one can still be sent; the last moment of its appeal while one can be
 * filed, and whether one waits. `reporting` (null until the reporting measures exist, and whenever neither stands): the
 * warning that counts and the restriction that runs. `handleRetired`: the profile holds a placeholder. Defined here
 * beside MeResponse, which the moderation contracts cannot be imported into without a cycle.
 */
export const AccountStanding = z.object({
  activeStrikes: z.number().int().nonnegative(),
  measure: z
    .object({
      decisionId: z.uuid(),
      kind: z.enum(["suspend", "terminate"]),
      days: z.number().int().min(1).max(30).nullable(),
      state: z.enum(["unfixed", "announced", "held", "running"]),
      earliestStart: z.iso.datetime(),
      startsAt: z.iso.datetime().nullable(),
      endsAt: z.iso.datetime().nullable(),
      reply: z.object({ filedAt: z.iso.datetime(), onTime: z.boolean(), answeredAt: z.iso.datetime().nullable() }).nullable(),
      replyOpen: z.boolean(),
      appealUntil: z.iso.datetime().nullable(),
      appealPending: z.boolean(),
    })
    .nullable(),
  reporting: z
    .object({
      warning: z.object({ decisionId: z.uuid(), countsUntil: z.iso.datetime() }).nullable(),
      restriction: z.object({ decisionId: z.uuid(), until: z.iso.datetime() }).nullable(),
    })
    .nullable(),
  handleRetired: z.boolean(),
});
export type AccountStanding = z.infer<typeof AccountStanding>;

export const MeResponse = z.object({
  user: z.object({
    id: z.uuid(),
    email: z.email(),
    role: Role,
    onboarded: z.boolean(),
    mfaEnabled: z.boolean(),
    hasPassword: z.boolean(),
    /** How many passkeys the account holds (1c design, section 7.5): above zero the app offers a passkey re-authentication, at zero it suggests adding one. */
    passkeys: z.number().int().nonnegative(),
  }),
  profile: MeProfile.nullable(),
  /** 3e: the account's standing, read fresh; null for an account without a profile and from an API built without the moderation module. */
  standing: AccountStanding.nullable(),
  /**
   * 2d Task 3 (9.3): the account's own picture, read fresh through the media module; null while it has none, for an account
   * without a profile and from an API built without the media module.
   */
  avatar: AvatarView.nullable(),
});
export type MeResponse = z.infer<typeof MeResponse>;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- email change

/** The new address, under the sign-up rules. The flow refuses the current address and disposable ones. */
export const EmailChangeStartRequest = z.object({ email: Email });
export type EmailChangeStartRequest = z.infer<typeof EmailChangeStartRequest>;

export const EmailChangeVerifyRequest = z.object({ flowId: OpaqueId, code: EmailCode });
export type EmailChangeVerifyRequest = z.infer<typeof EmailChangeVerifyRequest>;

/** The address the account now has. */
export const EmailChangeResponse = z.object({ email: z.email() });
export type EmailChangeResponse = z.infer<typeof EmailChangeResponse>;

/**
 * The token from the link the email_changed notice sends to the old address. It is the only credential
 * the undo needs, since a passwordless account cannot sign in at the old address any more.
 */
export const EmailRevertRequest = z.object({ token: OpaqueId });
export type EmailRevertRequest = z.infer<typeof EmailRevertRequest>;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- verified badge

export const BadgeStartRequest = z.object({ phone: Phone });
export type BadgeStartRequest = z.infer<typeof BadgeStartRequest>;

export const BadgeVerifyRequest = z.object({ flowId: OpaqueId, code: PhoneCode });
export type BadgeVerifyRequest = z.infer<typeof BadgeVerifyRequest>;

export const BadgeVerifyResponse = z.object({ verified: z.literal(true) });
export type BadgeVerifyResponse = z.infer<typeof BadgeVerifyResponse>;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- account deletion

export const DeleteStartResponse = z.object({ flowId: OpaqueId });
export type DeleteStartResponse = z.infer<typeof DeleteStartResponse>;

/** The emailed code and the account's handle typed by the owner; the flow compares the handle case-insensitively. */
export const DeleteConfirmRequest = z.object({ flowId: OpaqueId, code: EmailCode, handle: HandleInput });
export type DeleteConfirmRequest = z.infer<typeof DeleteConfirmRequest>;
```

```ts
import { z } from "zod";
import { FORBIDDEN_FORMAT } from "./text";

/** Every code the media endpoints add to ErrorEnvelope.error.code (plus the shared ones: invalid_request, not_found, rate_limited). */
// 3d Task 7 (design, sections 7.8 step 5 and 10.7): upload_refused, a post that attaches an upload korbat did not accept.
// 2d Task 3 (design, section 9.4), both 409 of PUT /api/me/avatar: avatar_not_ready, an upload that is processing, failed or
// refused; not_an_avatar, a post's image.
export const MediaErrorCode = z.enum(["unsupported_media_type", "file_too_large", "too_many_pending_uploads", "uploads_unavailable", "media_unavailable", "upload_refused", "avatar_not_ready", "not_an_avatar"]);
export type MediaErrorCode = z.infer<typeof MediaErrorCode>;

/** Why processing an upload failed. Reported on the status response, not as an HTTP error. */
export const MediaFailure = z.enum(["unsupported_format", "animated_not_supported", "image_too_large", "corrupt_image", "processing_failed"]);
export type MediaFailure = z.infer<typeof MediaFailure>;

/** 20 MiB. The API counts bytes while it streams an upload to disk and stops here. */
export const MEDIA_MAX_BYTES = 20 * 1024 * 1024;
export const MEDIA_MAX_PER_POST = 4;
/** The types an upload may declare. The bytes decide; the declaration is checked and then forgotten. */
export const MEDIA_ACCEPTED_TYPES = ["image/jpeg", "image/png", "image/webp", "image/avif", "image/gif"] as const;
export type MediaAcceptedType = (typeof MEDIA_ACCEPTED_TYPES)[number];
export const ALT_MAX_LENGTH = 1000;

/** A media id in its canonical lowercase form, which is also how it names files on the media volumes. */
export const MediaId = z.uuid().transform((id) => id.toLowerCase());

export const MEDIA_SIZES = ["small", "large"] as const;
export type MediaSize = (typeof MEDIA_SIZES)[number];

/** Where an image file is served. Views carry these paths, so the server can move images without a client change. */
export function mediaPath(id: string, size: MediaSize): string {
  return `/api/media/${id}/${size}.webp`;
}

/** Length in code points, which is what Postgres char_length counts. */
export function altLength(alt: string): number {
  return Array.from(alt).length;
}

/** Unicode NFC, every run of whitespace (line breaks included) to one space, trimmed. The server and the composer use the same rule. */
export function normalizeAltText(raw: string): string {
  return raw.normalize("NFC").replace(/\s+/gu, " ").trim();
}

const CONTROL = /\p{Cc}/u;

/** An image description as stored: normalized, 1 to 1000 code points, no control characters. */
export const AltText = z
  .string()
  .max(4000)
  .transform(normalizeAltText)
  .refine((alt) => !CONTROL.test(alt), { message: "control characters are not allowed" })
  .refine((alt) => !FORBIDDEN_FORMAT.test(alt), { message: "invisible direction and spacing characters are not allowed" })
  .refine((alt) => altLength(alt) >= 1, { message: "every image needs a description" })
  .refine((alt) => altLength(alt) <= ALT_MAX_LENGTH, { message: `descriptions have at most ${ALT_MAX_LENGTH} characters` });

/** One image of a new post: an upload that is ready, and its description. */
export const MediaAttachment = z.object({ id: MediaId, alt: AltText });
export type MediaAttachment = z.infer<typeof MediaAttachment>;

export const UploadResponse = z.object({ id: MediaId, status: z.literal("processing") });

/**
 * 2d Task 3 (design, sections 6.4 and 7.1): what an upload is for, set at its row's insert and never changed: an image of a
 * post, or a profile's picture, which is never on a post (the CHECK post_media_kind_place). The enum media_kind holds the
 * same values in the same order, which a database test holds.
 */
export const MEDIA_KINDS = ["post", "avatar"] as const;
export type MediaKind = (typeof MEDIA_KINDS)[number];

/**
 * 2d Task 3 (decision 14, 7.2 and 7.4): where the worker cuts an avatar's square along the longer side of the oriented
 * image: at its start (the left or top edge), in its centre (rounded down) or at its end. The picker shows the three over
 * the local file before it is sent.
 */
export const AVATAR_CROPS = ["start", "centre", "end"] as const;
export type AvatarCrop = (typeof AVATAR_CROPS)[number];

/**
 * 2d Task 3 (7.2, 9.2 and 9.4): the query of POST /api/media. Without `kind` the upload is a post's image, as before;
 * `kind=avatar` needs one `crop`, and a `crop` without `kind=avatar` is refused, both invalid_request: the picker always
 * sends one, so an avatar never waits on a default. A repeated parameter arrives as a list and is refused; any other
 * parameter is dropped, as the route read no query before. Read from the query alone, never from the body, which is the
 * file and is streamed.
 */
export const UploadQuery = z
  .object({ kind: z.enum(MEDIA_KINDS).default("post"), crop: z.enum(AVATAR_CROPS).optional() })
  .refine((query) => (query.kind === "avatar") === (query.crop !== undefined), { message: "kind=avatar takes a crop, and a crop goes only with kind=avatar", path: ["crop"] });
export type UploadQuery = z.infer<typeof UploadQuery>;

/**
 * 2d Task 3 (7.1, 7.5 and 9.3): a profile's picture as its readers get it, the two files mediaPath names: small.webp (128 px
 * square), large.webp (400 px square). Nothing else: an avatar has no description, and its size is fixed by the worker.
 * Here beside MediaView rather than in social.ts, because auth.ts's MeResponse carries it too and social.ts reads auth.ts.
 */
export const AvatarView = z.object({ small: z.string(), large: z.string() });
export type AvatarView = z.infer<typeof AvatarView>;
export type UploadResponse = z.infer<typeof UploadResponse>;

/**
 * The state of one upload, for its owner. Width and height are those of the large size, after rotation. A ready image
 * carries its blurhash, except one that moderation sealed: it is shown to nobody, and the blurhash is made from the image.
 * 3d (design, sections 7.1, 9.6 and 10.2): a ready image on a post whose seal was lifted and whose files are not back in
 * the image store yet says `restoring`, and one whose files korbat recorded as lost says `lost`; at most one of the two.
 */
export const MediaStatusResponse = z
  .discriminatedUnion("status", [
    z.object({ id: MediaId, status: z.literal("processing") }),
    z.object({
      id: MediaId,
      status: z.literal("ready"),
      width: z.number().int().positive(),
      height: z.number().int().positive(),
      blurhash: z.string().min(6).optional(),
      restoring: z.literal(true).optional(),
      lost: z.literal(true).optional(),
    }),
    z.object({ id: MediaId, status: z.literal("failed"), error: MediaFailure }),
    // 3d Task 7 (design, sections 7.8 step 5 and 10.2): an upload korbat refused on an acting match, with the refusal's id
    // for the link to its notice and nothing of the file: no blurhash, no sizes. An upload whose check is capped answers
    // processing, as any upload that is still being processed.
    z.object({ id: MediaId, status: z.literal("refused"), refusalId: z.uuid() }),
  ])
  .refine((answer) => !(answer.status === "ready" && answer.restoring && answer.lost), { message: "an image is either being restored or lost, never both" });
export type MediaStatusResponse = z.infer<typeof MediaStatusResponse>;

/**
 * An image on a post, as a reader who is shown it gets it. `moderation` is set only on the author's own image that
 * moderation withheld or removed, with that state: the author keeps seeing such an image, and nobody else is shown it.
 */
export const MediaView = z.object({
  id: MediaId,
  width: z.number().int().positive(),
  height: z.number().int().positive(),
  blurhash: z.string().min(6),
  alt: z.string(),
  small: z.string(),
  large: z.string(),
  moderation: z.enum(["withheld", "removed"]).optional(),
});
export type MediaView = z.infer<typeof MediaView>;

/**
 * What a reader gets in place of an image they are not shown: its id and the mark, never its size, its blurhash, its
 * description or a path. It is what anyone but the author gets for a withheld or removed image, the same for both states,
 * and what everyone gets for a sealed image, its author included: `sealed` is set only then, and only for the author.
 */
export const HiddenMedia = z.strictObject({ id: MediaId, hidden: z.literal(true), sealed: z.literal(true).optional() });
export type HiddenMedia = z.infer<typeof HiddenMedia>;

/** Whether an entry of a post's media list is a hidden image, which has nothing to draw or to open. */
export function isHiddenMedia(item: MediaView | HiddenMedia): item is HiddenMedia {
  return "hidden" in item;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the edge (3d design, sections 2 rows 11 to 13, 7.4 and 10.1)

/**
 * The two numbers of a public image's Cache-Control header (3d Task 3), which the API builds the header from: a browser
 * keeps a copy at most `browserSeconds`, an edge at most `edgeSeconds`, and neither serves a stale one. They are the
 * bound korbat states for a hidden image's copy without an accepted purge, and every sentence that states it prints them
 * from here.
 */
export const EDGE_CACHE = {
  browserSeconds: 60,
  edgeSeconds: 300,
} as const;

/**
 * The outbox's job (7.4): at most `prefixes` images a request and one request a round, a round `roundSeconds` after the
 * last ended (so at most four a minute), each request bounded at `timeoutMs`; a failed row waits `backoffSeconds`, doubled
 * at each failure up to `backoffMaxSeconds`, and is given up `giveUpHours` after it was written; the retention job (Task 8)
 * deletes a row `keepDays` after it was done.
 */
export const EDGE_RULES = {
  prefixes: 30,
  roundSeconds: 15,
  timeoutMs: 5000,
  backoffSeconds: 30,
  backoffMaxSeconds: 3600,
  giveUpHours: 24,
  keepDays: 30,
} as const;

/** The numbers the words about the edge print, in the units they print them: the edge's bound in minutes and the hours of the give-up. */
export const EDGE_WORDS = {
  edgeMinutes: EDGE_CACHE.edgeSeconds / 60,
  giveUpHours: EDGE_RULES.giveUpHours,
} as const;

/** Why an image stopped being public: a state, the image's or its post's; a deletion or an erasure; a release (the CHECK of edge_purges.cause). */
export const EDGE_PURGE_CAUSES = ["state", "deleted", "released"] as const;
export type EdgePurgeCause = (typeof EDGE_PURGE_CAUSES)[number];

/** How an outbox row ended: the provider took the purge, it gave up, or no adapter was on (the CHECK of edge_purges.outcome). */
export const EDGE_PURGE_OUTCOMES = ["accepted", "failed", "off"] as const;
export type EdgePurgeOutcome = (typeof EDGE_PURGE_OUTCOMES)[number];

/**
 * One image's newest outbox row as staff read it (10.3), on a case and on an order's item: its outcome, or `pending` while
 * it has none, and its time (when it ended, or when it was written while it is pending). An image that never stopped
 * being public has no row and no entry.
 */
export const EdgePurgeView = z.strictObject({
  mediaId: z.uuid(),
  outcome: z.enum([...EDGE_PURGE_OUTCOMES, "pending"]),
  at: z.iso.datetime(),
});
export type EdgePurgeView = z.infer<typeof EdgePurgeView>;
```
