```ts
import { z } from "zod";
import { DisplayName, HandleInput } from "./auth";
import { ImportSource } from "./imports";
import { AvatarView, HiddenMedia, MEDIA_MAX_PER_POST, MediaAttachment, MediaId, MediaView } from "./media";
import { RULE_IDS } from "./moderation";
import { FORBIDDEN_CONTROL, FORBIDDEN_FORMAT, normalizePostBody, postLength, visibleLength } from "./text";

/**
 * Every code the social endpoints add to ErrorEnvelope.error.code (plus the shared ones: invalid_request, not_found, rate_limited).
 * explore_refreshed (409) refuses a page of an Explore ranking that is no longer kept. account_suspended (403, 3e design,
 * section 10.5) refuses a write of an account while a suspension or termination of it runs; the media, auth and
 * moderation modules answer it too, as a code they share with this one.
 */
export const SocialErrorCode = z.enum(["post_unavailable", "not_author", "blocked", "self_target", "account_too_new", "explore_refreshed", "account_suspended"]);
export type SocialErrorCode = z.infer<typeof SocialErrorCode>;

/** Postgres returns lowercase ids; the canonical form, so a lookup by any spelling finds the row. */
export const PostId = z.uuid().transform((id) => id.toLowerCase());

/** A handle from a URL or a lookup box: an optional leading @, then the 3 to 20 characters handles may contain. */
export const HandleParam = z
  .string()
  .trim()
  .regex(/^@?[A-Za-z0-9_]{3,20}$/)
  .transform((value) => value.replace(/^@/, "").toLowerCase());

export const POST_MAX_LENGTH = 1000;

// 3b Task 1: postLength, normalizePostBody and FORBIDDEN_CONTROL live in ./text, so that imports.ts can read the body rules
// without loading this module, which reads moderation.ts at load.

/** A post body as stored: normalized, 1 to 1000 code points, some of them visible, no control or disguising characters. */
export const PostBody = z
  .string()
  .max(4000)
  .transform(normalizePostBody)
  .refine((body) => !FORBIDDEN_CONTROL.test(body), { message: "control characters are not allowed" })
  .refine((body) => !FORBIDDEN_FORMAT.test(body), { message: "invisible direction and spacing characters are not allowed" })
  .refine((body) => visibleLength(body) >= 1, { message: "a post needs some text" })
  .refine((body) => postLength(body) <= POST_MAX_LENGTH, { message: `posts have at most ${POST_MAX_LENGTH} characters` });

/** The text of a post that may also carry images: the same rule as PostBody, except that it may be empty. */
export const PostText = z
  .string()
  .max(4000)
  .transform(normalizePostBody)
  .refine((body) => !FORBIDDEN_CONTROL.test(body), { message: "control characters are not allowed" })
  .refine((body) => !FORBIDDEN_FORMAT.test(body), { message: "invisible direction and spacing characters are not allowed" })
  .refine((body) => postLength(body) <= POST_MAX_LENGTH, { message: `posts have at most ${POST_MAX_LENGTH} characters` });

/** A new post, reply or quote: text, up to four images that are ready, or both. */
export const CreatePostRequest = z
  .object({
    body: PostText.default(""),
    replyToId: PostId.optional(),
    quoteOfId: PostId.optional(),
    media: z.array(MediaAttachment).max(MEDIA_MAX_PER_POST).default([]),
    /** 2d (decision 26, 10.6): the composer's "Hide like and repost counts", off unless sent. */
    hideCounts: z.boolean().default(false),
  })
  .refine((post) => !(post.replyToId && post.quoteOfId), { message: "a post is a reply or a quote, not both", path: ["quoteOfId"] })
  .refine((post) => visibleLength(post.body) >= 1 || post.media.length >= 1, { message: "a post needs text or an image", path: ["body"] })
  .refine((post) => new Set(post.media.map((item) => item.id)).size === post.media.length, { message: "an image can be attached once", path: ["media"] });
export type CreatePostRequest = z.infer<typeof CreatePostRequest>;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- posts

/** 2d Task 3 (7.5, 9.3): `avatar`, the author's picture as every reader of a view gets it, or null for the monogram. */
export const Author = z.object({ id: z.uuid(), handle: z.string(), displayName: z.string(), verified: z.boolean(), avatar: AvatarView.nullable() });
export type Author = z.infer<typeof Author>;

/** Stands in for a post where its absence would break structure: an ancestor in a thread or a quoted embed. */
export const Tombstone = z
  .strictObject({ id: z.uuid(), deleted: z.literal(true).optional(), unavailable: z.literal(true).optional() })
  .refine((t) => t.deleted === true || t.unavailable === true, { message: "a tombstone is deleted or unavailable" });
export type Tombstone = z.infer<typeof Tombstone>;

/** Never deleted_by_author: deleted posts only ever appear as tombstones. */
export const PostState = z.enum(["visible", "withheld", "removed"]);
export type PostState = z.infer<typeof PostState>;

/**
 * A post's counts. 2d (decision 26, 9.3): `likes` and `reposts` are null exactly when the post's author hid its counts and
 * the reader is not its author, in every answer that carries counts (a view, a quoted embed, and the answer to the
 * reader's own like, unlike, repost or unrepost), so no reader learns a hidden count by liking. Replies and quotes are
 * always numbers.
 */
export const PostCounts = z.object({
  likes: z.number().int().min(0).nullable(),
  reposts: z.number().int().min(0).nullable(),
  replies: z.number().int().min(0),
  quotes: z.number().int().min(0),
});
export type PostCounts = z.infer<typeof PostCounts>;

export const ViewerPostState = z.object({ liked: z.boolean(), reposted: z.boolean(), bookmarked: z.boolean() });
export type ViewerPostState = z.infer<typeof ViewerPostState>;

const postFields = {
  id: z.uuid(),
  author: Author,
  body: z.string(),
  createdAt: z.iso.datetime(),
  state: PostState,
  /** The handle is null when the viewer could not open the parent: its author is blocked either way, or it is hidden or deleted. */
  replyTo: z.object({ id: z.uuid(), authorHandle: z.string().nullable() }).nullable(),
  counts: PostCounts,
  /** The post's images in order, each as the image or, where the reader is not shown it, as a hidden image in its place. Always present, often empty. */
  media: z.array(z.union([MediaView, HiddenMedia])),
  /** Present only for a signed-in viewer. */
  viewer: ViewerPostState.optional(),
};

/**
 * 3b (design, sections 8.4, 9.3 and 10.6): the provenance label of an imported post, made from the post's own columns and
 * nothing else: its source, the archive's day (YYYY-MM-DD in UTC, never its second, which with the text would fingerprint
 * the original) and whether it was cut to 1,000 characters on import. Null on every native post.
 */
export const ImportedLabel = z.object({ source: ImportSource, at: z.iso.date(), shortened: z.boolean() });
export type ImportedLabel = z.infer<typeof ImportedLabel>;

/**
 * A quoted post as embedded: one level deep, so its own quote is not expanded. 3b (the orchestrator's ruling for Task 6):
 * it carries the label as PostView does, last, for QuoteEmbed's short line (10.6).
 */
export const QuotedPost = z.object({ ...postFields, quoteOf: z.null(), imported: ImportedLabel.nullable() });
export type QuotedPost = z.infer<typeof QuotedPost>;

/**
 * The decision behind the state of the viewer's own withheld or removed post (3c design, sections 5 and 7.6): the decision
 * of the strongest post measure in force, by its id, the rule it cites (null for a decision on the law), whether it rests
 * on the law, and whether korbat is still deciding. The app shows it as the chip that links to the statement. `strikeUntil`
 * (3e design, section 10.2) is the end of counting of the strike the post's decision gave, while that strike stands and
 * still counts; null otherwise.
 */
// 3f: `order` is true when the chip's decision gives effect to an authority's order (a DSA Article 9 order that does not
// withhold, the only order that leaves a post its author sees), so the chip reads [chip.order]; absent otherwise.
export const PostModeration = z.object({ decisionId: z.uuid(), ruleId: z.enum(RULE_IDS).nullable(), legal: z.boolean(), interim: z.boolean(), strikeUntil: z.iso.datetime().nullable(), order: z.boolean().optional() });
export type PostModeration = z.infer<typeof PostModeration>;

export const PostView = z.object({
  ...postFields,
  /**
   * The author's "In Explore" chip (2c design, section 8): present, and true, only on the viewer's own post while it is in
   * the current Explore ranking with their switch on. Nobody else's view carries it, nor does a quoted embed. It sits here
   * rather than in `viewer`, which the like, repost and bookmark answers replace.
   */
  inExplore: z.literal(true).optional(),
  /** Present only on the viewer's own post while moderation withholds or removed it; nobody else's view carries it, nor does a quoted embed. */
  moderation: PostModeration.optional(),
  quoteOf: z.union([QuotedPost, Tombstone]).nullable(),
  /** 3b (9.3): the provenance label of an imported post, last; null on a native post. */
  imported: ImportedLabel.nullable(),
  /**
   * 2d (4.3): the handles of the post's stored mentions that link for this reader, lowercased, in text order: each one's
   * account is live, still holds the handle as written, and (for a signed-in reader) has no block either way with the
   * reader. Always empty for an imported post. After the label; a quoted embed carries none (QuotedPost), since it draws
   * its text plain.
   */
  mentions: z.array(z.string()),
  /** 2d (decision 26): the author hid the like and repost counts; last. Anyone else then reads them as null (PostCounts). */
  countsHidden: z.boolean(),
});
export type PostView = z.infer<typeof PostView>;

/** An item of a timeline or a profile's Posts tab. */
export const TimelineItem = z.discriminatedUnion("kind", [
  z.object({ kind: z.literal("post"), post: PostView }),
  z.object({ kind: z.literal("repost"), post: PostView, repostedBy: Author, repostedAt: z.iso.datetime() }),
]);
export type TimelineItem = z.infer<typeof TimelineItem>;

export function page<T extends z.ZodType>(item: T) {
  return z.object({ items: z.array(item), nextCursor: z.string().nullable() });
}

export const TimelinePage = page(TimelineItem);
export type TimelinePage = z.infer<typeof TimelinePage>;
export const PostPage = page(PostView);
export type PostPage = z.infer<typeof PostPage>;

export const ThreadResponse = z.object({
  ancestors: z.array(z.union([PostView, Tombstone])),
  post: PostView,
  replies: PostPage,
});
export type ThreadResponse = z.infer<typeof ThreadResponse>;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- engagement and graph

export const EngagementResponse = z.object({ counts: PostCounts, viewer: ViewerPostState });
export type EngagementResponse = z.infer<typeof EngagementResponse>;

/** 2d (9.2): PATCH /api/posts/:id/counts, the author's switch of decision 26; its answer is CountsResponse. */
export const CountsRequest = z.object({ hidden: z.boolean() });
export type CountsRequest = z.infer<typeof CountsRequest>;
export const CountsResponse = z.object({ countsHidden: z.boolean() });
export type CountsResponse = z.infer<typeof CountsResponse>;

/** 2d (9.2, decision 21): what POST and DELETE /api/me/share-previews answer, as /api/me/explore answers its switch. */
export const SharePreviewsResponse = z.object({ sharePreviews: z.boolean() });
export type SharePreviewsResponse = z.infer<typeof SharePreviewsResponse>;

export const FollowResponse = z.object({ following: z.boolean(), followerCount: z.number().int().min(0) });
export type FollowResponse = z.infer<typeof FollowResponse>;

export const BlockResponse = z.object({ blocked: z.boolean() });
export type BlockResponse = z.infer<typeof BlockResponse>;

export const MuteResponse = z.object({ muted: z.boolean() });
export type MuteResponse = z.infer<typeof MuteResponse>;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- profiles

export const ProfileCounts = z.object({
  posts: z.number().int().min(0),
  followers: z.number().int().min(0),
  following: z.number().int().min(0),
});

export const ViewerProfileState = z.object({ following: z.boolean(), followedBy: z.boolean(), blocked: z.boolean(), muted: z.boolean() });
export type ViewerProfileState = z.infer<typeof ViewerProfileState>;

export const ProfileView = z.object({
  id: z.uuid(),
  handle: z.string(),
  displayName: z.string(),
  bio: z.string(),
  verified: z.boolean(),
  createdAt: z.iso.datetime(),
  counts: ProfileCounts,
  /**
   * 3b (9.3, 10.6): the account has a visible imported top-level post, so the profile shows its Imported tab, for every
   * reader alike.
   */
  hasImported: z.boolean(),
  /** 2d Task 3 (7.5, 9.3): the profile's picture, or null while it has none or none is shown. */
  avatar: AvatarView.nullable(),
  /** Present only for a signed-in viewer looking at someone else. */
  viewer: ViewerProfileState.optional(),
});
export type ProfileView = z.infer<typeof ProfileView>;

export const ProfileListItem = Author.extend({ bio: z.string(), viewerFollows: z.boolean().optional() });
export type ProfileListItem = z.infer<typeof ProfileListItem>;

export const ProfilePage = page(ProfileListItem);
export type ProfilePage = z.infer<typeof ProfilePage>;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- profile editing

export const BIO_MAX_LENGTH = 160;

/** A bio as stored: trimmed, at most 160 code points, one line of plain text with no control or disguising characters. Empty clears it. */
export const Bio = z
  .string()
  .trim()
  // The line and paragraph separators (Zl, Zp) break a line as a newline does, without being control characters.
  .regex(/^[^\p{Cc}\p{Zl}\p{Zp}]*$/u, "control characters and line breaks are not allowed")
  .refine((bio) => !FORBIDDEN_FORMAT.test(bio), { message: "invisible direction and spacing characters are not allowed" })
  .refine((bio) => postLength(bio) <= BIO_MAX_LENGTH, { message: `bios have at most ${BIO_MAX_LENGTH} characters` });

/** What the profile screen saves: either field, or both. The handle has its own route and rules. */
export const ProfileEditRequest = z
  .object({ displayName: DisplayName.optional(), bio: Bio.optional() })
  .refine((edit) => edit.displayName !== undefined || edit.bio !== undefined, { message: "nothing to change" });
export type ProfileEditRequest = z.infer<typeof ProfileEditRequest>;

/**
 * 2d Task 3 (7.3, 9.2): PUT /api/me/avatar sets the account's picture to one of its own uploads of kind avatar that is
 * ready; DELETE /api/me/avatar takes no body. Both answer AvatarResponse: the picture now, or null after a removal.
 */
export const AvatarRequest = z.object({ mediaId: MediaId });
export type AvatarRequest = z.infer<typeof AvatarRequest>;
export const AvatarResponse = z.object({ avatar: AvatarView.nullable() });
export type AvatarResponse = z.infer<typeof AvatarResponse>;

/** The handle rules and the 30-day cooldown are enforced by the flow, which answers with a specific error code. */
export const HandleChangeRequest = z.object({ handle: HandleInput });
export type HandleChangeRequest = z.infer<typeof HandleChangeRequest>;
```

### Replace `packages/db/src/schema/content.ts` (whole file)

```ts
import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { bigint, boolean, check, index, integer, pgEnum, pgTable, primaryKey, real, smallint, text, uniqueIndex, uuid, type AnyPgColumn } from "drizzle-orm/pg-core";
import { apiRole, bytea, fullAccess, ts } from "./helpers";
import { profiles } from "./identity";
import { importJobs, importSource } from "./imports";

/** 3f (design, section 6.2): `disabled`, a post an authority's order disables, which every reader answers as missing. */
export const postState = pgEnum("post_state", ["visible", "withheld", "removed", "deleted_by_author", "disabled"]);

/**
 * What moderation derives for a post from the measures in force (3c design, section 6.1): the strongest of them.
 * posts.state mirrors it unless the author deleted the post, so post_state gains no value of 3c's. 3f adds `disabled`
 * to both (design, section 6.2), above `removed`: no row holds it before an order is given effect.
 */
export const moderationLevel = pgEnum("moderation_level", ["visible", "withheld", "removed", "disabled"]);

/** An image's own moderation state, beside its post's. Only an image is ever sealed: shown to nobody, its author included. */
export const mediaModerationState = pgEnum("media_moderation_state", ["visible", "withheld", "removed", "sealed"]);

/** A counter kept exact by the application: updated in the same transaction as the action it counts. */
const counter = (name: string) => integer(name).notNull().default(0);

export const posts = pgTable(
  "posts",
  {
    id: uuid("id").primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
    authorId: uuid("author_id").notNull().references(() => profiles.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
    body: text("body").notNull(),
    replyToId: uuid("reply_to_id").references((): AnyPgColumn => posts.id, { onDelete: "set null" }),
    quoteOfId: uuid("quote_of_id").references((): AnyPgColumn => posts.id, { onDelete: "set null" }),
    state: postState("state").notNull().default("visible"),
    likeCount: counter("like_count"),
    repostCount: counter("repost_count"),
    /** Replies that are not deleted. */
    replyCount: counter("reply_count"),
    /** Quotes that are not deleted. */
    quoteCount: counter("quote_count"),
    createdAt: ts("created_at").notNull().defaultNow(),
    /** Set together with state = 'deleted_by_author'; the body is blanked at the same time. */
    deletedAt: ts("deleted_at"),
    /** Derived from the ledger of measures by a migrator-owned function, the only writer; the API role cannot update it. */
    moderationLevel: moderationLevel("moderation_level").notNull().default("visible"),
    /** Set, one way, when the R4 redaction erased the post's content; written only by a migrator-owned function. */
    erasedAt: ts("erased_at"),
    /**
     * Explore's resume rule (3e design, sections 6.1 and 6.4): when the post last left the level visible, when it last came
     * back, and the time its age and window are counted from after its hidden spans. Outside the API's column grants; a
     * later migration gives them their one writer, moderation_apply.
     */
    hiddenAt: ts("hidden_at"),
    restoredAt: ts("restored_at"),
    exploreFrom: ts("explore_from"),
    /**
     * 3b (design, section 6.2): an imported post's import, source, the date its archive gives it, whether it was cut to
     * 1,000 characters, and the key of section 5.4 (32 bytes) by which a later import of the account skips it. All five
     * are set or none is (a native post, or an imported one's tombstone); posts_import_guard (migration 0044) lets an
     * insert set them only for a publishing import of the author with the same source, and an update only clear them, all
     * at once, with the post's tombstone. No on delete clause on the job: its row cannot go while a post names it.
     */
    importJobId: uuid("import_job_id").references((): AnyPgColumn => importJobs.id),
    importSource: importSource("import_source"),
    originalCreatedAt: ts("original_created_at"),
    importShortened: boolean("import_shortened"),
    importKey: bytea("import_key"),
    /**
     * 2d (design, section 6.4, decision 26; migration 0050_post_options): its author hid the post's like and repost counts
     * from everyone else, in the composer or from the post's More menu. Declared last, as the column is the table's last.
     */
    hideCounts: boolean("hide_counts").notNull().default(false),
  },
  (t) => [
    index("posts_author_created_idx").on(t.authorId, t.createdAt),
    /** Explore's restored posts. */
    index("posts_explore_from_idx").on(t.exploreFrom).where(sql`explore_from is not null`),
    index("posts_created_id_idx").on(t.createdAt, t.id),
    /** A thread's replies in order, and every lookup by parent. */
    index("posts_reply_to_created_idx").on(t.replyToId, t.createdAt, t.id),
    /**
     * The public Latest timeline: visible top-level posts and quotes, newest first. 3b (6.2): imported posts are in no
     * feed, so the predicate leaves them out (migration 0045 drops the index and creates it again).
     */
    index("posts_latest_idx").on(t.createdAt, t.id).where(sql`reply_to_id is null and state = 'visible' and import_job_id is null`),
    index("posts_quote_of_idx").on(t.quoteOfId),
    /** 3b: a post is imported once per account while it exists (decision 24). */
    uniqueIndex("posts_import_key_idx").on(t.authorId, t.importKey).where(sql`import_key is not null`),
    /** 3b: an import's posts, for the undo, the foreign key's checks and the job's count. */
    index("posts_import_job_idx").on(t.importJobId, t.id).where(sql`import_job_id is not null`),
    /** 3b (0045): the profile's Imported tab, its top-level imported posts by the archive's date. */
    index("posts_imported_idx").on(t.authorId, t.originalCreatedAt, t.id).where(sql`import_job_id is not null and reply_to_id is null`),
    /**
     * 3b (0045): an author's native posts, for Following's own branch and the Posts and Replies tabs, so a followed
     * account's 50,000 imported posts are never scanned there.
     */
    index("posts_author_native_idx").on(t.authorId, t.createdAt, t.id).where(sql`import_job_id is null`),
    check("posts_body_len", sql`char_length(${t.body}) <= 1000`),
    check("posts_counts_nonnegative", sql`${t.likeCount} >= 0 and ${t.repostCount} >= 0 and ${t.replyCount} >= 0 and ${t.quoteCount} >= 0`),
    check(
      "posts_import_columns",
      sql`(${t.importJobId} is null) = (${t.importSource} is null) and (${t.importJobId} is null) = (${t.originalCreatedAt} is null) and (${t.importJobId} is null) = (${t.importShortened} is null) and (${t.importJobId} is null) = (${t.importKey} is null)`,
    ),
    fullAccess("posts_api_all", apiRole),
  ],
).enableRLS();

/**
 * One Explore ranking (a "generation"), written by the refresh job (2c design, sections 6 and 7). The current ranking
 * is the highest generation; the job also keeps the one before it, so a reader paging through a ranking is not cut
 * off by the next round.
 */
export const exploreRuns = pgTable(
  "explore_runs",
  {
    /** Numbered by the database. One ranking every 5 minutes lasts 20,000 years in an integer. */
    generation: integer("generation").primaryKey().generatedAlwaysAsIdentity(),
    /** The refresh time the round was given; the ranking is computed as of this time. */
    asOf: ts("as_of").notNull(),
    /** The version of the formula the round ranked with (EXPLORE_V2.version in @korbat/contracts; rankings from before 3e hold 1). */
    formula: smallint("formula").notNull(),
    /** Posts that passed the candidate predicate at as_of. */
    candidates: integer("candidates").notNull(),
    /** Posts the ranking holds; their positions run from 1 to this. */
    items: integer("items").notNull(),
    /** How long the round took. */
    tookMs: integer("took_ms").notNull(),
  },
  () => [fullAccess("explore_runs_api_all", apiRole)],
).enableRLS();

/**
 * The posts of one Explore ranking, in order. No score or count is stored: nothing reads them after the insert, and
 * the position is the order. A row goes with its ranking, its post or its author.
 */
export const exploreItems = pgTable(
  "explore_items",
  {
    generation: integer("generation").notNull().references(() => exploreRuns.generation, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
    /** 1 to the ranking's item count, without gaps. */
    position: integer("position").notNull(),
    postId: uuid("post_id").notNull().references(() => posts.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
    /** The post's author, so an author's places in a ranking are counted without reading the posts. */
    authorId: uuid("author_id").notNull().references(() => profiles.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
  },
  (t) => [
    primaryKey({ columns: [t.generation, t.position] }),
    /** A post has one place in a ranking. */
    uniqueIndex("explore_items_generation_post_idx").on(t.generation, t.postId),
    fullAccess("explore_items_api_all", apiRole),
  ],
).enableRLS();

/** An upload is processing until the worker's result is in, then ready or failed for good. */
export const mediaStatus = pgEnum("media_status", ["processing", "ready", "failed"]);

/**
 * 2d Task 3 (design, section 6.4; migration 0051_avatars): what an upload is for, an image of a post or a profile's picture,
 * the contracts' MEDIA_KINDS. New in its migration, created whole: every function compares it as text, and the owner's
 * index names its label as a label (an index predicate takes no cast of an enum to text).
 */
export const mediaKind = pgEnum("media_kind", ["post", "avatar"]);

/**
 * One uploaded image. The files live on the media-store volume under the row's id; no path is
 * stored. Only the API's media module reads or writes this table.
 */
export const postMedia = pgTable(
  "post_media",
  {
    id: uuid("id").primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
    /** Who uploaded it. Only this account may attach it to a post. */
    ownerId: uuid("owner_id").notNull().references(() => profiles.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
    status: mediaStatus("status").notNull().default("processing"),
    /** Why processing failed: one of the contracts' MediaFailure values. */
    error: text("error"),
    /** Set, together with the position, when the image is attached to a post. */
    postId: uuid("post_id").references(() => posts.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
    position: integer("position"),
    /** Of the large size, after rotation. Set, together with the blurhash, when processing succeeds. */
    width: integer("width"),
    height: integer("height"),
    blurhash: text("blurhash"),
    altText: text("alt_text"),
    /** Filled by sub-project 3. Empty until then. */
    nsfwScore: real("nsfw_score"),
    createdAt: ts("created_at").notNull().defaultNow(),
    // The three columns below are forced to their defaults at insert and written only by migrator-owned functions; the
    // API role holds no UPDATE on them (migration 0015).
    /** Derived from the ledger of measures, as the post's level is. */
    moderationState: mediaModerationState("moderation_state").notNull().default("visible"),
    /** The latest end of the image's unreleased holds (media_holds): while it lies ahead, every delete skips the row. */
    holdUntil: ts("hold_until"),
    /** Set when an R4 removal of the image became final and its content was erased. */
    erasedAt: ts("erased_at"),
    /**
     * 3b (design, section 6.3): the image came from an import, which never changes; and the running import that owns the
     * upload, so the sweeper leaves it alone and the import cleans it up. post_media_import_insert (migration 0044) takes an
     * imported row only for a preparing import of its owner and a native one naming no import; the API role holds no
     * UPDATE of either. The import's row may go first: then its id is set null and the row stays imported, which
     * post_media_import_attach lets onto no post.
     */
    imported: boolean("imported").notNull().default(false),
    importJobId: uuid("import_job_id").references((): AnyPgColumn => importJobs.id, { onDelete: "set null" }),
    /**
     * 2d Task 3 (design, sections 6.4 and 7): the upload's kind, from its query, set at insert and never changed (the API
     * role holds no UPDATE of it). An avatar is never on a post, has no position and no description.
     */
    kind: mediaKind("kind").notNull().default("post"),
    /**
     * The profile this avatar is the picture of, while it is: set and cleared only by the media module's attachAvatar and
     * detachAvatar, under post_media_avatar_guard (to the owner's own profile, from null, on a ready, visible, unerased
     * avatar of a live profile), and refused at insert by post_media_insert. No on delete clause: no profile row is ever
     * deleted, and the account's purge deletes the image rows itself. One avatar a profile (post_media_avatar_idx).
     */
    profileId: uuid("profile_id").references(() => profiles.id),
    /**
     * An avatar's SHA-256 as uploaded, in lowercase hex, taken while the upload streams whatever MEDIA_MATCH says, so that
     * a picture a moderator reset can be recognised when it comes back (Task 4's avatar_resets). Null for a post's image.
     */
    avatarSha256: text("avatar_sha256"),
  },
  (t) => [
    uniqueIndex("post_media_post_position_idx").on(t.postId, t.position),
    index("post_media_owner_created_idx").on(t.ownerId, t.createdAt),
    index("post_media_status_created_idx").on(t.status, t.createdAt),
    check("post_media_ready_has_dims", sql`${t.status} <> 'ready' or (${t.width} is not null and ${t.height} is not null and ${t.blurhash} is not null)`),
    check("post_media_attached_is_complete", sql`${t.postId} is null or (${t.status} = 'ready' and ${t.position} between 0 and 3 and ${t.altText} is not null)`),
    check("post_media_alt_len", sql`char_length(${t.altText}) <= 1000`),
    check("post_media_import_link", sql`${t.importJobId} is null or ${t.imported}`),
    // 2d Task 3 (6.4): an avatar is never attached to a post, and a post's image is never an avatar. Kinds compared as text.
    check(
      "post_media_kind_place",
      sql`(${t.kind}::text = 'post' and ${t.profileId} is null) or (${t.kind}::text = 'avatar' and ${t.postId} is null and ${t.position} is null and ${t.altText} is null)`,
    ),
    // An avatar is only ever its owner's own profile's picture.
    check("post_media_avatar_owner", sql`${t.profileId} is null or ${t.profileId} = ${t.ownerId}`),
    // An avatar always has its file's SHA-256, a post's image never has one. "is not null" first: a CHECK passes on a null,
    // and a pattern match on a null is null.
    check("post_media_avatar_sha256", sql`(${t.kind}::text = 'post' and ${t.avatarSha256} is null) or (${t.kind}::text = 'avatar' and ${t.avatarSha256} is not null and ${t.avatarSha256} ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$')`),
    /** 2d Task 3: one avatar a profile, and the one statement of avatarsOf, which reads a page's authors' avatars by profile. */
    uniqueIndex("post_media_avatar_idx").on(t.profileId).where(sql`profile_id is not null`),
    /** 2d Task 3: an owner's avatars, the current one and any former one a hold keeps, for the purge and (Task 4) the seal. */
    index("post_media_owner_avatar_idx").on(t.ownerId).where(sql`kind = 'avatar'`),
    /**
     * 3b: an import's images by their job. The foreign key's set null when a job row goes, and the import's cleanup of its
     * unattached rows in id order (media.deleteImportLeftovers), would scan post_media without it.
     */
    index("post_media_import_job_idx").on(t.importJobId, t.id).where(sql`import_job_id is not null`),
    /**
     * 3b Task 5: the imports whose images are still on no post. import-drive asks it every round, for every import that
     * has ended, so that a stop's or a time limit's leftovers go (7.4); the index holds only rows on their way, never the
     * many attached ones, so the question costs nothing however many images were ever imported.
     */
    index("post_media_import_unattached_idx").on(t.importJobId).where(sql`import_job_id is not null and post_id is null`),
    fullAccess("post_media_api_all", apiRole),
  ],
).enableRLS();

/**
 * The edge's outbox (3d design, sections 2 row 11, 6.3 and 7.4; Task 3): one row each time an image stops being public,
 * which the job edge-purge drains to the purge adapter. No role inserts a row: the two definer triggers post_media_purge
 * and posts_purge write it in the transaction that hides the image, whoever the writer is, and the API's role holds no
 * INSERT, so no route can forget one and none can invent one. The insert trigger edge_purges_insert forces `created_at`
 * (clock_timestamp()) and `next_at` (now(): due at once). The API's job reads it, moves the four columns of a purge's
 * progress and (Task 8) deletes a row 30 days after it was done. No foreign key: an image's row may go, by a deletion or
 * the disposal, while its purge is still owed. The closed lists are the contracts' EDGE_PURGE_CAUSES and
 * EDGE_PURGE_OUTCOMES, written out here; a database test holds each migrated CHECK to its constant.
 */
export const edgePurges = pgTable(
  "edge_purges",
  {
    id: bigint("id", { mode: "number" }).primaryKey().generatedAlwaysAsIdentity(),
    mediaId: uuid("media_id").notNull(),
    /** state, deleted or released. */
    cause: text("cause").notNull(),
    /** Forced: clock_timestamp(). */
    createdAt: ts("created_at").notNull(),
    /** Forced at insert: now(). The job moves it back off after a failed purge. */
    nextAt: ts("next_at").notNull(),
    attempts: smallint("attempts").notNull().default(0),
    /** accepted, failed or off; set with done_at, once. */
    outcome: text("outcome"),
    doneAt: ts("done_at"),
  },
  (t) => [
    check("edge_purges_cause", sql`${t.cause} in ('state', 'deleted', 'released')`),
    check("edge_purges_outcome", sql`${t.outcome} in ('accepted', 'failed', 'off')`),
    check("edge_purges_done", sql`(${t.outcome} is null) = (${t.doneAt} is null)`),
    check("edge_purges_attempts", sql`${t.attempts} >= 0`),
    /** The job's round: the rows still owed a purge, by when they are due. */
    index("edge_purges_due_idx").on(t.nextAt).where(sql`done_at is null`),
    /** The case's and the order's purge line: the newest row of an image. */
    index("edge_purges_media_idx").on(t.mediaId, t.id),
    fullAccess("edge_purges_api_all", apiRole),
  ],
).enableRLS();

/** user -> user relation table (follows, blocks, mutes). */
function userPairTable(name: string, from: string, to: string) {
  return pgTable(
    name,
    {
      fromId: uuid(from).notNull().references(() => profiles.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
      toId: uuid(to).notNull().references(() => profiles.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
      createdAt: ts("created_at").notNull().defaultNow(),
    },
    (t) => [
      primaryKey({ columns: [t.fromId, t.toId] }),
      /** Pages of either side, newest first, and every lookup by either side. */
      index(`${name}_to_created_idx`).on(t.toId, t.createdAt, t.fromId),
      index(`${name}_from_created_idx`).on(t.fromId, t.createdAt, t.toId),
      check(`${name}_not_self`, sql`${t.fromId} <> ${t.toId}`),
      fullAccess(`${name}_api_all`, apiRole),
    ],
  ).enableRLS();
}

/**
 * user -> post relation table (likes, reposts, bookmarks). `createdBrin` adds `<name>_created_brin`, a BRIN index on
 * created_at, for the tables whose recent rows the Explore refresh reads (2c design, section 6).
 */
function userPostTable(name: string, options: { createdBrin?: boolean } = {}) {
  return pgTable(
    name,
    {
      userId: uuid("user_id").notNull().references(() => profiles.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
      postId: uuid("post_id").notNull().references(() => posts.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
      createdAt: ts("created_at").notNull().defaultNow(),
    },
    (t) => [
      primaryKey({ columns: [t.userId, t.postId] }),
      index(`${name}_post_idx`).on(t.postId),
      /** Per-account lists (your likes, your bookmarks) and the reposts half of the Following timeline. */
      index(`${name}_user_created_idx`).on(t.userId, t.createdAt),
      // Rows arrive roughly in time order, so a BRIN index of a few kilobytes finds the refresh's window as fast as a
      // btree of many megabytes. Unlikes, blocks and purges let later rows fill old pages and erode that order slowly.
      ...(options.createdBrin ? [index(`${name}_created_brin`).using("brin", t.createdAt)] : []),
      fullAccess(`${name}_api_all`, apiRole),
    ],
  ).enableRLS();
}

export const follows = userPairTable("follows", "follower_id", "followee_id");
export const blocks = userPairTable("blocks", "blocker_id", "blocked_id");
export const mutes = userPairTable("mutes", "muter_id", "muted_id");
export const likes = userPostTable("likes", { createdBrin: true });
export const reposts = userPostTable("reposts", { createdBrin: true });
/** Bookmarks are private and never count towards Explore, so they need no index by time. */
export const bookmarks = userPostTable("bookmarks");
```

```ts
import path from "node:path";
import type { MediaSize } from "@korbat/contracts";

const MEDIA_ID = /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/;

/** Ids are lowercase UUIDs made by the API. Nothing else may become part of a path. */
export function isMediaId(value: string): boolean {
  return MEDIA_ID.test(value);
}

function checked(id: string): string {
  if (!isMediaId(id)) throw new Error("not a media id");
  return id;
}

/**
 * The uploads volume: the API writes it, the worker only reads it.
 *   tmp/<id>.part     a body being received
 *   incoming/<id>     a complete upload waiting for the worker
 *   delete/<id>       a request to delete image <id>
 *   delete-owed/<id>  the API's own note that a request for image <id> is owed: written inside the transaction that
 *                     deletes the image's row, and removed once the request stands. The worker never reads it, so a
 *                     transaction that does not commit has asked for nothing.
 *   incoming/<id>.avatar  2d Task 3 (design, section 7.2): an avatar's job, its crop (AvatarJob), written through tmp/ and
 *                     renamed into place before the upload itself, so the worker never sees an avatar's upload without it.
 *                     Its name is no media id: the worker's scan of incoming/ skips it as a file of its own, and every
 *                     removal of the upload removes it too.
 */
export function uploadsLayout(root: string) {
  const tmp = path.join(root, "tmp");
  const incoming = path.join(root, "incoming");
  const deletions = path.join(root, "delete");
  const owed = path.join(root, "delete-owed");
  return {
    root,
    tmp,
    incoming,
    deletions,
    owed,
    part: (id: string) => path.join(tmp, `${checked(id)}.part`),
    upload: (id: string) => path.join(incoming, checked(id)),
    deletion: (id: string) => path.join(deletions, checked(id)),
    owedDeletion: (id: string) => path.join(owed, checked(id)),
    avatarJob: (id: string) => path.join(incoming, `${checked(id)}.avatar`),
  };
}
export type UploadsLayout = ReturnType<typeof uploadsLayout>;

/**
 * The store volume: the worker writes it, the API only reads it.
 *   files/<aa>/<id>/small.webp, large.webp   <aa> = the id's first two characters
 *   results/<id>.json                        the outcome, written last
 *   attempts/<id>                            how often processing started
 *   tmp/                                     files being written
 *   heartbeat                                rewritten every ten seconds
 */
export function storeLayout(root: string) {
  const files = path.join(root, "files");
  const results = path.join(root, "results");
  const attempts = path.join(root, "attempts");
  const tmp = path.join(root, "tmp");
  const imageDir = (id: string) => path.join(files, checked(id).slice(0, 2), id);
  return {
    root,
    files,
    results,
    attempts,
    tmp,
    heartbeat: path.join(root, "heartbeat"),
    shard: (id: string) => path.join(files, checked(id).slice(0, 2)),
    imageDir,
    image: (id: string, size: MediaSize) => path.join(imageDir(id), `${size}.webp`),
    result: (id: string) => path.join(results, `${checked(id)}.json`),
    attempt: (id: string) => path.join(attempts, checked(id)),
  };
}
export type StoreLayout = ReturnType<typeof storeLayout>;

/** `<id>.json` to `<id>`, or null when the name is not a result file. */
export function resultFileId(name: string): string | null {
  if (!name.endsWith(".json")) return null;
  const id = name.slice(0, -".json".length);
  return isMediaId(id) ? id : null;
}
```

```ts
/** The image formats korbat can accept. MEDIA_FORMATS in the environment enables a subset. */
export const MEDIA_FORMATS = ["jpeg", "png", "webp", "gif", "avif"] as const;
export type MediaFormat = (typeof MEDIA_FORMATS)[number];

/**
 * Decoding costs memory by pixel count, not by file size: a 932-byte AVIF of 20 megapixels took
 * 423 MB in the 2026-09-18 measurements, while WebP and 8-bit PNG stream at about 100 MB for 48.
 * AVIF therefore has its own cap. The worker passes these to the decoder, which enforces them
 * from the header before any pixel is decoded.
 */
export const PIXEL_CAP: Record<MediaFormat, number> = {
  jpeg: 50_000_000,
  png: 50_000_000,
  webp: 50_000_000,
  gif: 50_000_000,
  avif: 16_000_000,
};

/** The longest side accepted, which is also the most WebP can hold. */
export const MAX_SIDE = 16_383;

/** The two sizes the worker writes. `edge` bounds the longer side; images are never enlarged. */
export const VARIANTS = {
  large: { edge: 2048, quality: 82 },
  small: { edge: 1024, quality: 80 },
} as const;

/**
 * 2d Task 3 (design, sections 7.1 and 7.4): an avatar's two squares, under the two names of every image: `edge` is the
 * square's side, never enlarged. 40 px in lists and 32 px in the composer use the small one up to three device pixels per
 * CSS pixel; the profile's header and a card use the large one.
 */
export const AVATAR_VARIANTS = {
  large: { edge: 400, quality: 82 },
  small: { edge: 128, quality: 80 },
} as const;

/** How often processing of one upload may start. A file that kills the worker is retried at most this often. */
export const MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3;

export const HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS = 10_000;
export const HEARTBEAT_STALE_MS = 60_000;

/** Bounds for files the API reads from the store, which it treats as untrusted. */
export const MAX_RESULT_BYTES = 16 * 1024;
/** 2d Task 3: the most an avatar's job file may hold, which the worker reads from the volume the API writes. */
export const MAX_JOB_BYTES = 256;
export const MAX_VARIANT_BYTES = 32 * 1024 * 1024;

/**
 * MEDIA_FORMATS: a comma-separated subset of the formats, or unset for all of them. Removing a
 * format refuses it at upload and leaves its decoder blocked, which is how an operator reacts to
 * an advisory against one decoder without a deploy.
 */
export function parseFormats(value: string | undefined): MediaFormat[] {
  if (value === undefined) return [...MEDIA_FORMATS];
  const names = value.split(",").map((name) => name.trim().toLowerCase());
  if (names.some((name) => name === "")) throw new Error("MEDIA_FORMATS must name at least one format and have no empty entries");
  const unknown = names.filter((name) => !(MEDIA_FORMATS as readonly string[]).includes(name));
  if (unknown.length > 0) throw new Error(`MEDIA_FORMATS has unknown formats: ${unknown.join(", ")}. Known: ${MEDIA_FORMATS.join(", ")}`);
  return MEDIA_FORMATS.filter((format) => names.includes(format));
}
```

```ts
import { R1_MODEL_NAME } from "./classifier";
import { MAX_SIDE } from "./limits";

const side = z.number().int().min(1).max(MAX_SIDE);
const blurhash = z.string().min(6).max(64);

/**
 * 3d (design, sections 5 and 10.2; Task 6): what the worker found of an image beside its two sizes, in version 2. `r1`:
 * the scorer's model, by the name this build gives it, and its score from 0 to 1, present only while a scorer runs
 * (R1_CLASSIFIER is not off); the API keeps a score only from the model its own setting names. `pdq`: korbat's own
 * perceptual hash of the decoded pixels, its implementation's version and its quality (Task 7 computes and keeps it).
 */

const PdqResult = z.strictObject({
  impl: z.number().int().positive(),
  hash: z.string().regex(/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/),
  quality: z.number().int().min(0).max(100),
});

/**
 * results/<id>.json, the worker's last write for an upload and therefore the commit point. Width
 * and height are those of large.webp, after rotation. The API parses this strictly: the file
 * comes from the one process korbat does not trust.
 *
 * 3d Task 6 (design, section 10.2): the union of version 1 as it stood and version 2, which is version 1's members with
 * `v: 2` and, on a ready result, the optional members `r1` and `pdq`. The worker writes version 2; the API reads both and

export const ResultFile = z.union([
  z.strictObject({ v: z.literal(1), id: z.uuid(), status: z.literal("ready"), width: side, height: side, blurhash }),
  z.strictObject({ v: z.literal(1), id: z.uuid(), status: z.literal("failed"), reason: MediaFailure }),
  z.strictObject({ v: z.literal(2), id: z.uuid(), status: z.literal("ready"), width: side, height: side, blurhash, r1: R1Result.optional(), pdq: PdqResult.optional() }),
  z.strictObject({ v: z.literal(2), id: z.uuid(), status: z.literal("failed"), reason: MediaFailure }),
  z.strictObject({ v: z.literal(3), id: z.uuid(), status: z.literal("ready"), width: side, height: side, blurhash, r1: R1Result.optional(), pdq: PdqResult.optional(), avatar: z.literal(true).optional() }),
  z.strictObject({ v: z.literal(3), id: z.uuid(), status: z.literal("failed"), reason: MediaFailure }),

export type ResultFile = z.infer<typeof ResultFile>;

/** The version the worker writes. */
export const RESULT_VERSION = 3;

/**
 * 2d Task 3 (design, section 7.2): incoming/<id>.avatar, the job of an avatar's upload, which the API writes before the
 * upload and the worker reads strictly: version 1 and the crop's position (AVATAR_CROPS), nothing else, at most

export const AvatarJob = z.strictObject({ v: z.literal(1), crop: z.enum(AVATAR_CROPS) });
export type AvatarJob = z.infer<typeof AvatarJob>;

/** The heartbeat file: when the worker last completed a tick, in epoch milliseconds. */
export const Heartbeat = z.strictObject({ v: z.literal(1), at: z.number().int().nonnegative() });
export type Heartbeat = z.infer<typeof Heartbeat>;
```

```js
async function api(path, { json, token, method } = {}) {
  const headers = {};
  if (json !== undefined) headers["content-type"] = "application/json";
  if (token) headers.authorization = `Bearer ${token}`;
  const res = await fetch(`${base}${path}`, { method: method ?? (json === undefined ? "GET" : "POST"), headers, body: json === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify(json) });
  const text = await res.text();
  let body = null;
  try {
    body = text ? JSON.parse(text) : null;

 * five seconds. On Docker Desktop, containers' outbound calls stall for up to half a minute right after a
 * heavy image build, which is not a fault of the stack, so a Turnstile refusal is tried again every five
 * seconds for up to a minute. A wrong secret still fails, a minute later.

async function withTurnstile(path, json) {

    console.log(`info ${path}: Turnstile could not be verified; trying again in 5 s`);

  if (ifNoneMatch) headers["if-none-match"] = ifNoneMatch;
  if (token) headers.authorization = `Bearer ${token}`;
  const res = await fetch(`${base}${path}`, { method, headers, body });
  return { status: res.status, headers: res.headers, bytes: Buffer.from(await res.arrayBuffer()) };
```
